sources.label: Higher Education Counseling and Student Affairs (HCSA)

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aerospace Fundamentals
courses.description: Introduction to the engineering profession including the aeronautical and astronautical fields. Engineering approach to problem-solving and analysis of data obtained from experiments. Basic nomenclature and design criteria used in the aerospace industry. Applications to basic problems in the field. 1 lecture, 1 laboratory. Formerly AERO 121.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Special Problems for Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Repeatable up to 3 units. Formerly AERO 200.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Consent of department chair.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aerospace Engineering Dynamics
courses.description: Fundamentals of kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. Kinematics of particle and rigid body motion. Newton's 2nd law. Work-energy and momentum methods. Introduction to three-dimensional kinematics and reference frames. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: CE 204 and ME 211, or ENGR 2211.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CE 204 and ME 211, or ENGR 2211.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 270.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Engineering Numerical Analysis
courses.description: Numerical methods for solving aerospace engineering problems in the areas of fluids, thermodynamics, dynamics, control, and structures using modern computing techniques. Numerical precision, iterative methods, numerical integration, Runge-Kutta solvers, finite difference, singular value decomposition and Eigen-problem solutions. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and MATH 244 or MATH 2341.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and MATH 244 or MATH 2341.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Thermo Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: Thermo-fluid-flow properties, standard atmosphere, dimensional analysis, closed-open-isolated systems, laws of thermodynamics, Navier Stokes relations, thermodynamic equations of state and related variables, thermodynamic processes, control volume analysis, (in)compressible internal-external flows, isentropic flow, normal-oblique shocks, compression-expansion waves, (un)steady flows, laminar-turbulent flows. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 4 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: ME 212 or AERO 2220.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ME 212 or AERO 2220. Corequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Thermo Fluids Laboratory
courses.description: Experiments and analysis in applied fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, and heat transfer. Comparisons of analog and digital data sensors and acquisition for applications of conservation of mass, momentum, and energy. 1 laboratory.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Corequisite: AERO 3301.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Heat and Mass Transfer
courses.description: Convection, conduction, and radiation as methods for heat transfer. Specific topics will cover calorically, thermally perfect, and real gas effects, thermodynamic cycle analysis and efficiencies, Rayleigh-Fanno flows, forced-free convection, radiative gases/surfaces, emission-irradiation spectrum, and radiation shields. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures. Formerly AERO 303.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 3301 or AERO 299 and AERO 302; and AERO 300 or AERO 3300.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AERO 3301 or AERO 299 and AERO 302; and AERO 300 or AERO 3300.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aerospace Propulsion Systems
courses.description: Power plant types, components, characteristics, and requirements. Principles of thrust and energy utilization for low and high-speed applications. Thermodynamic processes and performance of gas turbines and ramjets, as well as chemical, electric, and nuclear rocket propulsion. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 401.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM 124 or CHEM 1120.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CHEM 124 or CHEM 1120. Corequisite: AERO 303 or AERO 3303.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Introduction to Aerodynamics
courses.description: Introduction to aerodynamics and its application to a variety of flight conditions. Analytical and empirical relation. Airfoil/wing characteristics corrections for such things as compressibility and wing sweep accounting for the generation of forces and moments. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 306.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 3301 or AERO 299 and AERO 302.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 3301 or AERO 299 and AERO 302.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Air and Space
courses.description: Technological developments of modern aircraft and spacecraft through physics of flight equations, mission analysis, propulsion, structures, materials, and control systems for civil and military aircraft/spacecraft. Synthesis of current and future aerospace technologies through emerging ethical considerations and global impact. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as AERO 3310/HNRS 3313. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly AERO/HNRS 310.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 5A (GE Area B1 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 5A (GE Area B1 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: System Dynamics
courses.description: Introduction to system dynamics principles including dynamics equilibrium and stability. Linearization using perturbations and Taylor series. Laplace Transforms, transfer functions and system response. Equivalent systems, time and frequency domain analysis, and control of linear dynamic systems. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly AERO 320.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 2220 or ME 212.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 2220 or ME 212.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aerospace Structural Analysis I
courses.description: Thin-walled cylindrical and spherical pressure vessels. Euler column buckling. Engineering and principal strains. Stress tensor. Principal stresses. Balance equations. Linear thermoelastic material behavior. Bending, torsion, and shear of advanced beams. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 4 lectures. Formerly AERO 331.
courses.prerequisite: CE 204 and ME211, or ENGR 2211; and MATE 210 or MATE 1220.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CE 204 and ME211, or ENGR 2211; and MATE 210 or MATE 1220. Corequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Introduction to Orbital Mechanics
courses.description: Motion of a body in a central field. Keplerian Orbits. Orbital maneuvers. Interplanetary trajectories. Rocket Trajectories. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 351.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 2220 or ME 212.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 2220 or ME 212.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Introduction to AERO for Transfer Students
courses.description: Introduction to Aerospace Engineering and its application in professional practice. Engineering approach to problem-solving and analysis of data obtained from experiments. Familiarization with 3-D dynamics and rotation/coordinate systems. Not open for students with credit in AERO 121, AERO 1121 and AERO 2220. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 1 lecture.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aerospace Engineering Professional Preparation
courses.description: Professional development for student success including overview of aerospace industry, current events in the aerospace industry, graduate studies, engineering ethics and culture, intellectual property, non-disclosure agreements, teamwork, and innovation and entrepreneurship. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 1 lecture. Formerly AERO 460.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Special Problems for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Repeatable up to 6 units. Formerly AERO 400.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Ground to Space Propulsion
courses.description: Propulsion design for aircraft and spacecraft. Air-breathing propulsion systems performance and component characteristics. Rocket performance, chemical rockets, electric thrusters, thruster placement, system layout, component design, and systems integration. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 3304.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 3304.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Spaceflight Propulsion
courses.description: Aerospace propulsion design characteristics, performance, and integration for chemical, electric, and nuclear propulsion. Transatmospheric and interplanetary propulsion components and integration. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures. Formerly AERO 402.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 3304.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 3304.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Propulsion Laboratory
courses.description: Experimental data collection and analysis of jet and rocket propulsion systems. Experiments in solid, liquid, and hybrid rockets, electric propulsion, propellers, and gas turbines. Experiments on nozzle characteristics in compressible flow. 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 3304.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 3304. Corequisite: AERO 402, AERO 4401, or AERO 4402.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Advanced Aerodynamics
courses.description: Analysis techniques and their application to a variety of flight conditions. Subsonic aerodynamics, viscous drag prediction, supersonic aerodynamics, and hypersonic aerodynamics. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 405.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 306 or AERO 3305.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 306 or AERO 3305.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Experimental Aerodynamics
courses.description: Experimental aerodynamics, experimental testing, validation, measurement techniques, load measurements, pressure measurements, flow visualization, demonstrations of advanced techniques, low-speed and high-speed measurements, measurement uncertainty, error analysis and propagation, reading instrument datasheets, and selection of suitable ranges for commercially available devices. 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 3301 or AERO 299 and AERO 302.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 3301 or AERO 299 and AERO 302. Recommended: AERO 306 or AERO 3305.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Applied Computational Aerodynamics
courses.description: Application of Computational Fluid Dynamics and other computational methods to study a range of problems relating to applications in aerospace engineering. Grid generation, sources of errors in numerical studies, boundary conditions, 2D and 3D external flows, and turbulence modeling. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly AERO 406.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 3301 or AERO 299 and AERO 302.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 3301 or AERO 299 and AERO 302. Recommended: AERO 306 or AERO 3305.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Re-Entry Aerodynamics
courses.description: Near planet environments. Transition from orbital to aero-dynamic motion. Aerodynamic heating and effects on design. Entry, descent, and landing. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 407.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 3301 or AERO 299 and AERO 302.
courses.recommended: AERO 351 or AERO 3351; and AERO 306 or AERO 3305.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: AERO 3301 or AERO 299 and AERO 302. Recommended: AERO 351 or AERO 3351; and AERO 306 or AERO 3305.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aerospace Flight Test
courses.description: Aerospace flight test introduction. Flight test preparation. Flight test design. Flight test execution. Ground control station procedures and team organization. Radio communication. Flight test data analysis and reduction. Flight test reporting. 1 lecture, 2 laboratories. Formerly AERO 409.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 306 or AERO 3305.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: AERO 306 or AERO 3305.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aircraft Dynamics and Control
courses.description: Aircraft flight mechanics. Equilibrium, static and dynamics stability. Aircraft maneuvers. Longitudinal and lateral stability and stick fixed. Stick free neutral point. Analysis of latero-directional equilibrium flight conditions. Introduction to flight dynamics and automatic flight control. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 420.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 306 or AERO 3305; and AERO 320 or AERO 3320.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 306 or AERO 3305; and AERO 320 or AERO 3320.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Spacecraft Attitude Dynamics and Control
courses.description: On orbit disturbances, spin stabilization, gravity-gradient, and momentum exchange devices. Control law design and analysis using frequency- and time- domain methods. Fundamentals of attitude determination, guidance, and navigation systems, including Kalman Filters. Course may be offered in a classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 421.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 320 or AERO 3320; and AERO 351 or AERO 3351.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 320 or AERO 3320; and AERO 351 or AERO 3351.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Flight Dynamics and Automatic Control
courses.description: Airplane attitude representation. Airplane flight dynamics. General equation of unsteady motion. Stability derivatives. Stability of uncontrolled motion (longitudinal). Stability of uncontrolled motion (lateral). Airplane response to control actuation. Automatic stability and control. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 420 or AERO 4420.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 420 or AERO 4420.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aircraft Performance
courses.description: Fundamentals of propeller and jet aircraft performance. Level flight, gliding, climbing. Takeoff and landing. Federal Aviation Regulations related to performance. Turning and pull-ups. Energy methods. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 425.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 306 or AERO 3305.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 306 or AERO 3305.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aerospace Structural Analysis II
courses.description: Energy methods and variational principles. Betti-Maxwell reciprocity theorem. Rayleigh-Ritz method. Statically indeterminate structures. Bending, extension, and buckling of thin plates. Free vibrations of beams and plates. Finite element method for bar and beam elements. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 431.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 331 or AERO 3331.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AERO 331 or AERO 3331.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Experimental Stress Analysis
courses.description: Stress analysis and aerospace structural analysis. Individual and group design project dealing with aerospace structures. Field trip required. 1 laboratory. Formerly AERO 433.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 331 or AERO 3331.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: AERO 331 or AERO 3331.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Spacecraft Electrical and Electric Systems
courses.description: Basic satellite types and applications with specifics applied to power and communication. Interactions between subsystems and their effects on the overall system design. Detailed analysis of key subsystems on a spacecraft with special emphasis on power and communications subsystems. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 446.
courses.prerequisite: ME 212 or AERO 2220; AERO 351 or AERO 3351; and PHYS 143 or PHYS 1143.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ME 212 or AERO 2220; AERO 351 or AERO 3351; and PHYS 143 or PHYS 1143.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Introduction to Aerospace Systems Engineering
courses.description: Systems engineering processes and concepts in aerospace. Multidisciplinary approaches to the design, realization, technical management and planning for the development of aerospace systems and subsystems. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate or senior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate or senior standing.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Intermediate Orbital Mechanics
courses.description: Relative orbital motion and rendezvous, linearization of the equations of motion. Clohessy-Wiltshire equations. Two-impulse rendezvous. Asphericity of the earth, aerodynamic drag, solar radiation pressure, n-body perturbations on an orbit. Encke, Cowell, Variation of Parameters solution techniques. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 452.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 351 or AERO 3351; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 351 or AERO 3351; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Space Environments
courses.description: Effects of the space environment on a spacecraft and design considerations. Issues include Launch, vacuum, neutral, particulate, radiation, thermal and plasma environments. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 355.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 303 or AERO 3303.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 303 or AERO 3303.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Space Environments Laboratory
courses.description: Effects of the space environment on a spacecraft and design considerations through laboratory experiments. Laboratories included the areas of launch, vacuum, neutral, particulate, radiation, thermal and plasma environments. 1 laboratory.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Corequisite: AERO 355 or AERO 4455.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Introduction to Human Spaceflight
courses.description: Requirements and considerations for human spaceflight design and operations. Effects of the spaceflight environment on the human body and countermeasures to mitigate those effects. Designing a spacecraft for the human payload focusing on space operations. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 455.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing or graduate standing.
courses.recommended: AERO 351 or AERO 3351; and AERO 355 or AERO 4455.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Senior standing or graduate standing. Recommended: AERO 351 or AERO 3351; and AERO 355 or AERO 4455.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aircraft Design Senior Project I
courses.description: Design of an aircraft system using multidisciplinary analysis techniques developed in previous engineering courses. Determination of system requirements, mission characteristics and system lifecycle. Analysis of design characteristics to evaluate performance and functional characteristics. Preparation of technical drawings, briefings, and reports. Field trip required. 3 laboratories. Formerly AERO 443.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 3304; AERO 306 or AERO 3305; AERO 320 or AERO 3320; AERO 331 or AERO 3331; AERO 460 or AERO 3460; and IME 144 or IME 1140.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 3304; AERO 306 or AERO 3305; AERO 320 or AERO 3320; AERO 331 or AERO 3331; AERO 460 or AERO 3460; and IME 144 or IME 1140.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aircraft Design Senior Project II
courses.description: Continuation of the design of an aircraft system from Aircraft Design I, using multidisciplinary analysis techniques. Organization of technical activities, system architecture, technology integration, and planning for development, test and manufacturing. Analysis of design characteristics. Preparation of drawings and briefings. Field trip required. 3 laboratories. Formerly AERO 445.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 4401; AERO 405 or AERO 4405; and AERO 443 or AERO 4461.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 4401; AERO 405 or AERO 4405; and AERO 443 or AERO 4461.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Spacecraft Design Senior Project I
courses.description: Design of a spacecraft system using multidisciplinary analysis techniques developed in previous engineering courses. Determination of system requirements, mission characteristics and system lifecycle. Analysis of design characteristics to evaluate performance and functional characteristics. Preparation of technical drawings, briefings, and reports. 3 laboratories. Formerly AERO 447.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 3304; AERO 320 or AERO 3320; AERO 331 or AERO 3331; AERO 351 or AERO 3351; AERO 460 or AERO 3460; and IME 144 or IME 1140.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AERO 401 or AERO 3304; AERO 320 or AERO 3320; AERO 331 or AERO 3331; AERO 351 or AERO 3351; AERO 460 or AERO 3460; and IME 144 or IME 1140.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Spacecraft Design Senior Project II
courses.description: Continuation of the design of a spacecraft system from Spacecraft Design I, using multidisciplinary analysis techniques. Organization of technical activities, system architecture, technology integration, and planning for development, test and manufacturing. Analysis of design characteristics. Preparation of drawings and briefings. 3 laboratories. Formerly AERO 449.
courses.prerequisite: AERO 402 or AERO 4402; AERO 446 or AERO 4446; and AERO 447 or AERO 4463.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AERO 402 or AERO 4402; AERO 446 or AERO 4446; and AERO 447 or AERO 4463.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 470.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Special Advanced Laboratory
courses.description: Directed group laboratory study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 laboratories. Formerly AERO 471.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Cooperative Education Experience
courses.description: Work experience related to aerospace engineering. Positions are paid and usually require relocation and registration in course for one term. Registration in course is required at start of work experience. Formal evaluation by work supervisor required. Repeatable up to 6 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly AERO 493.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Individual Study
courses.description: Advanced study planned and completed under the direction of a member of the department faculty. Enrollment by petition. Repeatable up to 9 units. Formerly AERO 500.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of department chair, graduate advisor, and supervising faculty member.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Consent of department chair, graduate advisor, and supervising faculty member.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Finite Element Analysis of Continua
courses.description: Finite element theory and application with a focus on numerical implementation. Strong and weak forms, variational theorems, displacement based methods, mixed methods, viscoelasticity and plasticity type formulations, augmented Lagrangian formulations, transient and modal analysis, and finite deformation. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as AERO/BMED/CE/ME 5504. Formerly CE/ME 504.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BMED/CE/ME 404, BMED/CE/ME 4404, CE 501, CE 5502, AERO 431, or AERO 4431.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: BMED/CE/ME 404, BMED/CE/ME 4404, CE 501, CE 5502, AERO 431, or AERO 4431.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Computational Aerodynamics
courses.description: Classification of partial differential equations. Numerical methods applicable to the solution of elliptic, parabolic, and hyperbolic partial differential equations. Consideration of accuracy and stability of numerical methods. Application to the fundamental equations of fluid dynamics, grid generation, turbulence modeling. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 525.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Aerospace Engineering; or AERO 3301, or AERO 299 and AERO 302.
courses.recommended: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 306 or AERO 3305.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Aerospace Engineering; or AERO 3301, or AERO 299 and AERO 302. Recommended: AERO 300 or AERO 3300; and AERO 306 or AERO 3305.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Boundary-Layer Theory
courses.description: Concept of boundary-layer. Boundary-layer equations, similarity transformation, integral and differential methods for steady, two-dimensional laminar and turbulent boundary layers, hypersonic boundary layers. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 522.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Aerospace Engineering; or AERO 3301, or AERO 299 and AERO 302.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Aerospace Engineering; or AERO 3301, or AERO 299 and AERO 302. Recommended: AERO 306 or AERO 3305.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Spacecraft Thermal/Fluid Control
courses.description: Satellite thermal/fluid control hardware. Governing equations for flow and heat transfer. Surface tension and liquid/vapor interface. Heat transfer by free convection, forced convection and radiation in low-gravity environment. Heat pipes. Capillary-pumped loops. Cryogenic systems. Fluid management in space. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 526.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Aerospace Engineering; or AERO 3301, or AERO 299 and AERO 302, and AERO 303 or AERO 3303.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Aerospace Engineering; or AERO 3301, or AERO 299 and AERO 302, and AERO 303 or AERO 3303.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Aerospace Structural Dynamics Analysis
courses.description: Vibrations of single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) and multi -degree-of-freedom (MDOF) systems. Lagrange's equations. Hamilton's principle. Bending and torsional vibrations of beams. Rayleigh-Ritz and Galerkin methods. Divergence. Aileron reversal. Classical flutter analysis. The k and pk methods. Aeroelastic flutter by assumed-modes method. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 534.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Aerospace Engineering.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Aerospace Engineering.

courses.subject: AERO
courses.title: Advanced Ground to Space Transportation
courses.description: Systems perspective on propulsion systems for space transportation. Includes launch vehicles and in-space propulsion. Chemical, electric, and nuclear rocket characteristics and performance. Combined cycle propulsion for atmospheric and space transportation. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AERO 540.

courses.description: Development of agribusiness modeling techniques that are applied to solving a diverse and unique set of resource allocation issues encountered throughout the agricultural and food retail sectors. Techniques include linear programming, decision analysis, and computer simulations. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 328.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 260 or AGB 2260; one of the following: MATH 221, MATH 1261, MATH 1267, or appropriate math placement; and STAT 251 or STAT 1210.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: AGB 260 or AGB 2260; one of the following: MATH 221, MATH 1261, MATH 1267, or appropriate math placement; and STAT 251 or STAT 1210.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Agricultural Lending
courses.description: Structure and performance of the agricultural lending industry. Advanced agricultural loan analysis and risk assessment. Agricultural loan documentation, securitization of farm loans, and farm bankruptcy. Exploration of interest rate impacts on agricultural lending. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 335.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 308 or AGB 3308; and AGB 323 or AGB 3323.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AGB 308 or AGB 3308; and AGB 323 or AGB 3323.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Internship in Agribusiness
courses.description: Selected students will spend up to one full academic term with an approved agricultural firm engaged in production or related agribusiness. Time will be spent applying and developing agribusiness functional and managerial skills and abilities. Repeatable up to 12 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly AGB 339.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of internship instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of internship instructor.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Agricultural Strategic Decision Making
courses.description: Strategic decision making in the context of agribusiness situations. Emphasis on both the sequential and simultaneous nature of the decision process in both single and repeated interactions. Game theory concepts as strategy formulation tools. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 452.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 141, MATH 1261, MATH 221, or MATH 1267.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 141, MATH 1261, MATH 221, or MATH 1267.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Agricultural Personnel Management
courses.description: California agricultural personnel management: recruitment, appraisal, and performance evaluation. Compensation, training and development. Discipline, safety, and health. Labor relations and immigration policy. Systemic approach to aspects of managing human capital, and how to implement human resource policies. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 369.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: AGB 212, AGB 2212, ECON 201, ECON 2001, ECON 221, or ECON 2030.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: AGB 212, AGB 2212, ECON 201, ECON 2001, ECON 221, or ECON 2030.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Special Problems
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of special problems. Repeatable up to 6 units. Formerly AGB 400.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Food Retail Management
courses.description: Management principles of perishable and non-perishable food commodities at the retail level. Introduction to the economics of the food retailing sector, including inventory management, price and promotional activity, differentiation, and competitiveness. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 404.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 301 or AGB 3301.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AGB 301 or AGB 3301.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Agribusiness Marketing Research Methods
courses.description: Agricultural marketing research data collection and analysis. Emphasis on food sector market segmentation, product positioning, new product testing, sales forecasting, and marketing plan development through secondary and primary data sources. Experimental research design and implementation. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 405.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 301 or AGB 3301; and AGB 327 or AGB 3327.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AGB 301 or AGB 3301; and AGB 327 or AGB 3327.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Agribusiness Marketing Planning
courses.description: Development of agribusiness marketing plans in self-managed teams. Emphasis on developing presentation skills. Integration of marketing mix, particularly promotional elements in developing agribusiness marketing strategy emphasized. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 406.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 301 or AGB 3301; and AGB 327 or AGB 3327.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AGB 301 or AGB 3301; and AGB 327 or AGB 3327.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Agribusiness Risk Management
courses.description: Theoretical foundations of risk and uncertainty. Strategies that agricultural producers and supply chain firms use to manage risk, including forward contracting, futures and options, swaps, crop insurance, trading and hedging strategies, and their applications to agribusiness problems. Formerly AGB 411.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 301 or AGB 3301; AGB 308 or AGB 3308; and AGB 328 or AGB 3328.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AGB 301 or AGB 3301; AGB 308 or AGB 3308; and AGB 328 or AGB 3328.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Advanced Agricultural Policy
courses.description: Agricultural resource allocation issues with emphasis on current policies that impact agricultural production, the food system, and natural resources. Agricultural resource allocation stressing issues and policies emphasizing economic externalities. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 412.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 312 or AGB 3312.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AGB 312 or AGB 3312.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Transportation and Logistics in Global Agribusiness
courses.description: Scope and elements of the agribusiness logistics system, including supply and distribution channels, transportation, inventory, warehousing, and information. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 422.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 328 or AGB 3328.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AGB 328 or AGB 3328.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Agribusiness Supply Chain Management
courses.description: Focus on the development and application of decision models in food supply chains with emphasis on demand forecasting, aggregate planning, inventory management, supply network design, coordination and sourcing. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 425.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: AGB 327, AGB 3327, AGB 328, or AGB 3328.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: AGB 327, AGB 3327, AGB 328, or AGB 3328.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Rural Property Appraisal
courses.description: Methods of rural appraisal, including farms, ranches and other rural properties. Use of county records. Appraisal practice on different types of rural properties. Discussions with professional appraisers. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 326.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 212 or AGB 2212; and AGB 308 or AGB 3308.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AGB 212 or AGB 2212; and AGB 308 or AGB 3308.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Advanced Agribusiness Data Analysis
courses.description: Advanced topics in agricultural business data analysis. Agricultural price analysis, modeling techniques for agricultural data, and advanced forecasting techniques for agribusiness decision making. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 427.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 327 or AGB 3327.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AGB 327 or AGB 3327.

courses.subject: AGB

courses.description: Fresh fruit and vegetable sales and marketing emphasizing what makes produce unique in food marketing. Analysis of produce distribution channels, strategies for differentiating produce commodities, and research into produce industry trends and their impact on the industry. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 445.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 301 or AGB 3301.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: AGB 301 or AGB 3301.

courses.subject: AGB
courses.title: Agribusiness Strategy Formulation
courses.description: Analysis and development of business plans of firms in the food supply chain with a focus on financial and marketing strategies that impact the whole enterprise. Research and assessment of internal and external environments that affect the development of business plans. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 450.
courses.prerequisite: AGB 214 or AGB 2214; and AGB 301 or AGB 3301.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: AGB 214 or AGB 2214; and AGB 301 or AGB 3301.

courses.title: Senior Project - Applied Agribusiness Problems
courses.description: Selection and analysis of agribusiness problems and opportunities in directed group-based projects. Formal report and presentation required. 3 lectures. Formerly AGB 462.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; AGB 301 or AGB 3301; AGB 308 or AGB 3308; AGB 312 or AGB 3312; AGB 322 or AGB 3322; AGB 369 or AGB 3369; and one of the following: AGB 327, AGB 3327, AGB 328, or AGB 3328.

courses.description: Orientation to leadership development in agriculture and related settings. courses.description: Orientation to the Master of Agricultural Education program. Current requirements, processes, documentation, and discussion of expectations of pre-professional teacher candidates. Completion of formal documents for credentialing in California. 1 seminar. Formerly AGED 501.

courses.description: Research methodologies in agricultural education and communication. Quantitative and qualitative research processes. Appropriate methods to address research problems. Enabling students to effectively evaluate, synthesis, and communication of research findings. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Master of Agricultural Education program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Admission to the Master of Agricultural Education program.

courses.title: Agriculture Specialist Clinical Practice
courses.description: Practice and techniques in management and supervision of programs in agricultural education. Relationships among students, staff, community and school groups. Student Future Farmers of America (FFA) program and work-based learning project management. Formerly AGED 513.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: AGED
courses.title: Program Development in Agricultural Education
courses.description: Approaches to the development of an integrated agricultural education program in the comprehensive high school, based on occupational opportunities and community needs. Philosophy, organization, and administration of programs. Development in curriculum, supervised occupational experience, student leadership such as FFA and summer programs. Course offered online only. 3 seminars. Formerly AGED 520.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Master of Agricultural Education Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Admission to the Master of Agricultural Education Program.

courses.title: Laboratory Pedagogy in Agricultural Technology
courses.description: Organizing agricultural technology laboratory instruction, curriculum, and facilities. Student presentations, assessment, analysis, and evaluation. Field trip required. Not open to students with credit in AGED 523 or AGED 5523. Half-semester course. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly AGED 522.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Corequisite: AGED 524 or AGED 5524.

courses.subject: AGED
courses.title: Laboratory Organization and Management in Agricultural Education
courses.description: Organizing and managing laboratories, including agricultural mechanics curriculum. Student demonstrations, presentations, assessment, analysis, and evaluation. Course designed for in-service secondary agriculture teachers. Field trip required. Not open to students with credit in AGED 522 or AGED 5522. 3 lectures. Formerly AGED 523.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Master of Agricultural Education program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Admission to the Master of Agricultural Education program.

courses.subject: AGED
courses.title: Instructional Processes in Agricultural Education
courses.description: Principles of agricultural teaching methods and developmentally-appropriate pedagogy. Daily and unit lesson plans incorporating content, teaching methods, and assessing learners. Accommodations for English learners and students with special needs. Class demonstrations in teaching procedures, analysis, assessment and reflection. Half-semester course. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly AGED 524.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Single Subject Agriculture Credential program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Admission to the Single Subject Agriculture Credential program. Corequisite: AGED 440 or AGED 4440.

courses.subject: AGED
courses.title: Developing FFA and Supervised Agricultural Experience Programs in Secondary Education
courses.description: Integrating FFA and supervised agricultural experience programs into curriculum. Career development event implementation; officer and committee training; recruitment; retention; retreat and leadership training. Current initiatives and experiential learning opportunities in the workplace and entrepreneurial settings. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly AGED 530.
courses.prerequisite: Senior or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Senior or graduate standing.

courses.title: Teaching Agriculture in Higher Education
courses.description: Selection and use of teaching strategies, methods/approaches, and techniques when planning, delivering, and evaluating instruction. Intended for graduate students interested in pursuing a faculty position in agriculture, as well as other disciplines in higher education. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 seminars. Formerly AGED 536.

courses.title: Graduate Internship in Agricultural Education and Communication
courses.description: Application of theory to the solution of problems of agricultural production or related business in the field of Agricultural Education and Communication. Repeatable up to 6 units. Formerly AGED 539.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.title: Instructional Planning in Agriculture
courses.description: Prior to the first day of teaching agriculture, develop a plan for delivery of instruction in a program of agriculture in a K-14 educational setting. courses.prerequisite: AGED 524 or AGED 5524.

courses.title: Special Problems in Agricultural Education
courses.description: Individual study of modern issues and problems conducted through research, planning and development. Field problems and in-service study in the agriculture industry encouraged. Final written report required. Repeatable up to 9 units. Formerly AGED 580.

courses.title: Comprehensive Examination
courses.description: Comprehensive assessment for a non-thesis master's student showing integration of knowledge, critical and independent thinking, and mastery of agricultural education. courses.title: Special Problems for Undergraduates

courses.subject: ANT
courses.title: Cultural Anthropology
courses.description: Cultural patterns and divergence in language and communication, family organization, gender, adaptation to environment, economics and productivity, political organization, religion and ritual, ethnicity and race, illness and healing, globalization and culture change. Ethnographic analysis and cultural relativity skills emphasized. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 4B (GE Area D2 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ANT 201.

courses.subject: ANT
courses.title: World History Before Writing
courses.description: Long-term development of global biological and cultural diversity from emergence of the first human ancestors 6-7 million years ago to the advent of writing. Biological evolution, cultural development, emergent socio-political complexity and social inequality, migrations, adaptation to climate change, and sustainability. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 4B (GE Area D2 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ANT 202.

courses.title: Biological Anthropology
courses.description: Biological aspects of human unity and diversity. Primate and human evolution, including anatomical, physiological and behavioral adaptations. Evolutionary ecological perspectives and theories on human behavior and biology. Field trip required. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 5B (GE Area B2 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ANT 250.

courses.title: Museum Studies Foundations
courses.description: Exploration of the history of museums, their roles in society, and ethics of preservation, repatriation, and education/outreach. Contextualizes movements to increase representation and equity in the collection and curation of ethnographic and archaeological material. Field trips required. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory.

courses.subject: ANT
courses.title: Elements of Archaeology
courses.description: Overview of archaeological method and theory covering the history and development of archaeological thought, approaches to data recovery, dating and analysis of artifacts and ecofacts, and the construction of theoretical models of prehistoric human behavior. Field trip required. 3 lectures. Formerly ANT 309.
courses.prerequisite: ANT 202 or ANT 2202.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ANT 202 or ANT 2202.

courses.subject: ANT
courses.title: Archaeological Field Methods
courses.description: Hands-on introduction to archaeological field methods emphasizing excavation. Artifact and ecofact identification, lithic technology. Practical experience with hand tools, and stratigraphic interpretation. Methodological approaches to research and management questions. Strenuous outdoor work in a rugged setting. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly ANT 310.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ANT 202, ANT 2202, ANT 309, or ANT 3309.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: One of the following: ANT 202, ANT 2202, ANT 309, or ANT 3309.

courses.subject: ANT
courses.title: Archaeological Laboratory Methods
courses.description: Hands-on introduction to the methods employed in post-field processing, classification, analysis, and preservation of archaeological materials. Compilation of quantitative and qualitative information in data base format to assist in the classification and interpretation of faunal remains and artifacts. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Field trip required. Formerly ANT 311.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ANT 309, ANT 3309, ANT 310, or ANT 3310.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: ANT 309, ANT 3309, ANT 310, or ANT 3310.

courses.subject: ANT
courses.title: Introduction to Cultural Resources Management
courses.description: Introduction to international, federal, state, and local legislation pertinent to identification, evaluation, and treatment of cultural resources. Practical field experience in site recording, map-reading, and cartography using GPS, LIDAR, and drones. Rigorous field work in a rugged setting. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly ANT 312.
courses.prerequisite: GEOG 218 or GEOG 2218; and one of the following: ANT 310, ANT 3310, ANT 311, or 3311.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: GEOG 218 or GEOG 2218; and one of the following: ANT 310, ANT 3310, ANT 311, or 3311.

courses.subject: ANT
courses.title: Bioarchaeology
courses.description: The study of human remains from archaeological sites. Methods for analyzing skeletons to understand health, diet, trauma, and lifestyles of past populations. Case studies, ethical issues, and hands-on lab experience. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: ANT 202 or ANT 2202.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ANT 202 or ANT 2202.

courses.subject: ANT
courses.title: California's Indigenous Past
courses.description: Overview of the paleoenvironment, prehistory, archaeology, and ethnography of Indigenous California. Last 12,000 years of California's past from the appearance of the first human beings to the establishment of Spanish settlements in 1769, and the decline and persistence of Indigenous societies. 3 lectures. Formerly ANT 320.
courses.prerequisite: ANT 202 or ANT 2202.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ANT 202 or ANT 2202.

courses.subject: ANT
courses.title: Indigenous South Americans
courses.description: Indigenous peoples of South America from the past to the present. Cross-cultural study of small band societies, tribes, chiefdoms and large civilization states covering the continent. Traditional cultural focus, pre-colonization. Indigenous rights and issues in contemporary society. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: ANT 201 or ANT 2201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ANT 201 or ANT 2201.

courses.subject: ANT
courses.title: Human Behavioral Ecology
courses.description: Biological and cultural influences of natural and sexual selection on individual behavior. Ecological effects on human behavior to reproduce and acquire resources. Scientific method for understanding foraging, group living, sociality, kinship, parenting, religion, and mating. Cross-cultural, cross-sex, and cross-species comparisons. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ANT 345.

Star Trek is used as a comparative framework to analyze American cultural ideals within broader ethnographic and historical social systems worldwide. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.description: Social and cultural evolution from Paleolithic times to the present. Interactions of demographic, economic and ecological factors are emphasized. Main topics include human nature/culture, sex and gender, cooperation and conflict, the 'agricultural revolution', state formation, social inequality and globalization. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ANT 360.

courses.description: Preparation for professional advancement in the fields of anthropology and geography. Supervised career planning emphasizing resume development, selection of an internship or international experience, exploration of career options and graduate programs. Lectures from outside, practicing professionals. Credit/No Credit grading only. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 seminars. Crosslisted as ANT/GEOG 3384. courses.title: Action-oriented Ethnography
courses.description: Development of knowledge and skills needed to conduct original action-oriented ethnographic research. Grounded in the reflexive 'turn' in anthropology and critical race, science, technology and society, queer and feminist studies, students will engage questions of authority, representation, critical consciousness and justice. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as ANT/ISLA 3393. Formerly ANT/ISLA 393.

courses.title: Sex, Death, and Human Nature
courses.description: Human behavior and variation as shaped by evolutionary processes. Theory and primary approaches, including evolutionary psychology, comparative animal behavior, and human evolutionary biology for investigating human behavior from evolutionary and cross-cultural perspectives. Cooperation, mate choice, morality, religiosity, sexual orientation, and culture. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ANT 344.

courses.subject: ANT
courses.title: Culture and Health
courses.description: Global perspective on the relationship between culture and health. Ecological factors influencing health and illness. Social origins and impact of diseases. Relationship of gender, race, and reproduction to illness. Global health problems. Health-care needs of U.S. racial/ethnic groups. 4 lectures. Formerly ANT 401.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and ANT 201 or ANT 2201.

courses.title: Indigenous North Americans
courses.description: Survey of Indigenous North Americans from earliest times to present, emphasizing regional diversity in traditional lifeways. Origins of New World peoples, domestication, war, social organization, trade and gender roles. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: ANT 201 or ANT 2201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ANT 201 or ANT 2201.

courses.title: Meaning, Gender, and Identity in Anthropological Theory
courses.description: Exploration of the intersection of anthropological theory with meaning, gender/sexuality, and identity formations within and between cultural contexts. courses.title: Anthropology-Geography Research Design and Methods
courses.description: Development of knowledge and skills needed to conduct original scientific anthropology-geography research and prepares students for senior projects. courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: History of World Architecture I: Prehistory to 17th Century
courses.description: World architecture and urbanism from prehistory until seventeenth century. Political, social, religious, environmental, and technological conditions that shaped the built environment in Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ARCH 217.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: History of World Architecture II: 17th Century to the Present
courses.description: World architecture and urbanism from the seventeenth century to the present. Political, social, religious, environmental, and technological conditions that shaped the built environment in Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ARCH 218.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Architectural Representation III
courses.description: Continuation in a multipart sequence in architectural representation. History, theory, and practice of two- and three-dimensional graphic and physical representations of objects and environments. Critical interpretation and creation of drawings and models. Concepts include advanced digital and parametric modeling. Half-semester course. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 1 activity. Formerly ARCH 207.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 132 or ARCH 1102.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ARCH 132 or ARCH 1102. Concurrent: ARCH 2201.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Architectural Representation IV
courses.description: Continuation in a multipart sequence in architectural representation. History, theory, and practice of two- and three-dimensional graphic and physical representations of objects and environments. Critical interpretation and creation of drawings and models. Concepts include rendering and image-making. Half-semester course. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 1 activity. Formerly ARCH 253.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 251 or ARCH 2201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ARCH 251 or ARCH 2201. Concurrent: ARCH 2202.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Topics in Architectural Representation
courses.description: Introduction to concepts, tools, and media in a specified topic of 2- or 3-dimensional architectural representation. Project-based instruction and critique. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Replaced ARCH 313.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Architectural Technology Fundamentals I
courses.description: Introduction to architectural technologies, including those related to daylighting, building materials, load-bearing wall systems, site analysis, topography, and stormwater management. Studies are rooted in knowledge of ecology, carbon economies, and sustainability. Organized into three topic areas: site systems, energy systems, and construction systems. Field trip required. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 2 activities. Formerly ARCH 241.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 131 or ARCH 1101.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Related
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Sustainability Related Prerequisite: ARCH 131 or ARCH 1101.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Architectural Technology Fundamentals II
courses.description: Second course in a multipart sequence that introduces architectural technologies, including those related to urban development, regulatory requirements, passive design strategies for thermal comfort, moisture control, life-safety, and accessibility. Organized into three topic areas: site systems, energy systems, and construction systems. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 2 activities. Formerly ARCH 242.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 241 or ARCH 2241.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Related
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Sustainability Related Prerequisite: ARCH 241 or ARCH 2241.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly ARCH 270.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Integrated Architectural Design
courses.description: Design and development of a comprehensive architectural project. Synthesis of site conditions, user requirements, and sustainable design practices. Integrated design of whole-building systems. Field trip required. 5 laboratories. Formerly ARCH 352.
courses.prerequisite: ARCE 315 or ARCE 3301; ARCH 252 or ARCH 2202; and ARCH 341 or ARCH 3341.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ARCE 315 or ARCE 3301; ARCH 252 or ARCH 2202; and ARCH 341 or ARCH 3341. Concurrent: ARCH 3342.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Topics in Architectural History, Theory, and Criticism
courses.description: In-depth examination of a significant region, movement, subject, or period in architectural history, theory and/or criticism. The material covered will vary depending upon the topic. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable to 6 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 3 (GE Area Upper-Division C for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ARCH 320.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: ARCH 217, ARCH 218, ARCH 2221, ARCH 2222, ART 112, or ART 1112; or ART 212 or ART 2212 and completion of GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
