courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Building Information Modeling
courses.description: Introduction to methods and theories that inform contemporary digital modeling and representation for design, testing, and documentation of buildings. Application of contemporary tools through the creation of a complete Building Information Model (BIM) of an existing building. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 1 lecture, 1 activity. Formerly ARCH 353.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Concurrent: ARCH 3341.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Architectural Systems Integration I
courses.description: Continuation of a multipart sequence with a focus on whole-building and site, form-determinant design decision making for architects. Includes building systems such as life-safety, structural, mechanical, plumbing, and enclosure as they impact the built environment, human experience, building performance, and environment. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 2 activities. Formerly ARCH 341.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 242 or ARCH 2242.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: ARCH 242 or ARCH 2242. Concurrent: ARCH 3331.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Architectural Systems Integration II
courses.description: Continuation of a multipart sequence with a with focus on integration of structural systems with exterior and interior enclosures and their impact on design decision making, sustainability and health. Includes wall, ceiling and floor material assemblies, composition and environmental performance, architectural lighting, and acoustics. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures, 2 activities. Formerly ARCH 342.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 341 or ARCH 3341.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: ARCH 341 or ARCH 3341. Concurrent: ARCH 3301.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Special Problems for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Repeatable up to 6 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly ARCH 400.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Advanced Architectural Design
courses.description: Advanced architectural design projects representative of architecture's many manifestations and interpretations in human culture. Course may be offered through off-campus programs. Field trip may be required. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. Repeatable up to 15 units. 1 discussion, 4 laboratories. Formerly ARCH 351.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 252 or ARCH 2202; one of the following: ARCH 207, ARCH 253, ARCH 2231, or ARCH 2232; ARCH 242 or ARCH 2242; one of the following: PHYS 121, PHYS 141, PHYS 1121, or PHYS 1141; and MATH 119 or MATH 1007, or appropriate math placement.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: ARCH 252 or ARCH 2202; one of the following: ARCH 207, ARCH 253, ARCH 2231, or ARCH 2232; ARCH 242 or ARCH 2242; one of the following: PHYS 121, PHYS 141, PHYS 1121, or PHYS 1141; and MATH 119 or MATH 1007, or appropriate math placement.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Topics in Design
courses.description: Analysis of traditional and alternative principles, practices and methods of design in architecture and related fields. Cultural, geographical, historical and contemporary design approaches are considered through case studies, readings, and student presentations. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 12 units. 3 lectures. Formerly ARCH 469.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: Architecture major, Architectural Engineering major, City and Regional Planning major, Construction Management major, Landscape Architecture major, or Architecture minor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: Architecture major, Architectural Engineering major, City and Regional Planning major, Construction Management major, Landscape Architecture major, or Architecture minor.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Seminar in Architectural History, Theory and Criticism
courses.description: Topics based on the exploration of specific approaches, periods, or areas of architecture and the built environment. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 9 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 seminars. Formerly ARCH 420.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 217, ARCH 218, and ARCH 219; or ARCH 1121, ARCH 2221, and ARCH 2222; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ARCH 217, ARCH 218, and ARCH 219; or ARCH 1121, ARCH 2221, and ARCH 2222; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Architectural Representation
courses.description: Advanced concepts, tools, and media in a specified topic of architectural representation. Project-based instruction and critique. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ARCH 461.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: Architecture major, Architectural Engineering major, City and Regional Planning major, Construction Management major, Landscape Architecture major, or Architecture minor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: Architecture major, Architectural Engineering major, City and Regional Planning major, Construction Management major, Landscape Architecture major, or Architecture minor.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Topics in Computational Design and Digital Fabrication
courses.description: Two- and three-dimensional computational design and digital fabrication methods. Analysis of historic and contemporary computational design and digital fabrication cases in architecture. Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 2 lectures 1 laboratory. Formerly ARCH 460.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ARCH 201, ARCH 253, ARCH 2000, or ARCH 2232.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: ARCH 201, ARCH 253, ARCH 2000, or ARCH 2232.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Issues in Contemporary Professional Practice
courses.description: Exploration of issues related to the practice of architecture, including financial considerations, client obligations, project and practice management, leadership, legal responsibilities, ethics and professional judgment, community and social responsibility, as well as the process and requirements for internship and licensure. 2 lectures, 2 discussions. Formerly ARCH 443.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 342 or ARCH 3342.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ARCH 342 or ARCH 3342.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Topics in Architectural Technology and Practice
courses.description: Exploration of selected topics in architectural technology and/or practice. Topics may address specific materials, methods of construction, building systems, or site technologies. Deploy specific techniques of building design or analysis, or engage expanding modes of practice. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Field trip may be required. Repeatable up to 6 units. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ARCH 462.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: Architecture major, Architectural Engineering major, City and Regional Planning major, Construction Management major, Landscape Architecture major, or Architecture minor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: Architecture major, Architectural Engineering major, City and Regional Planning major, Construction Management major, Landscape Architecture major, or Architecture minor.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Topics in Design Build and Fabrication
courses.description: Experimental design-build projects derived from real-world architectural problems. Objectives achieved through design, analysis, construction, and individual or team-based production. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ARCH 479.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Senior Architectural Thesis Theory and Research Seminar
courses.description: Research of, and critical engagement with, selected aspects of architectural theory and discourse. Development of a final draft written architectural thesis. 3 seminars. Fulfills GWR.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 320, ARCH 420, or ARCH 4425.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F GWR Prerequisite: ARCH 320, ARCH 420, or ARCH 4425. Concurrent: ARCH 4461.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Senior Project: Architectural Thesis I
courses.description: Design research, and preliminary design, of an architectural thesis project. Correlated to a written architectural thesis. Integration of architectural theory with the formal, spatial, material, contextual, technical, and representational aspects of architectural design. Engagement in critical discourse. 1 discussion, 4 laboratories. Formerly ARCH 481.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 352 or ARCH 3301; and ARCH 451, ARCH 452, and ARCH 453 or completion of 15 units of ARCH 4401.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ARCH 352 or ARCH 3301; and ARCH 451, ARCH 452, and ARCH 453 or completion of 15 units of ARCH 4401. Concurrent: ARCH 4460.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Senior Project: Architectural Thesis II
courses.description: Continuation of senior project for Architecture students. Design development and defense of an architectural thesis project, and submission of final thesis book. Integration of architectural theory with the formal, spatial, material, contextual, technical, and representational aspects of architectural design. Engagement in critical discourse. 1 discussion, 4 laboratories.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 481 or ARCH 4461.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ARCH 481 or ARCH 4461.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly ARCH 470.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Cooperative Education Experience
courses.description: Professional work experience in architecture and related fields, usually off-campus. Positions are paid. Formal report and evaluation by work supervisor required. Repeatable up to 24 units. Formerly ARCH 485.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Topics in Architectural Research
courses.description: Development of guided architectural research under the direction of faculty. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 3 seminars. Formerly ARCH 484.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: Architecture major, Architectural Engineering major, City and Regional Planning major, Construction Management major, or Landscape Architecture major.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: Architecture major, Architectural Engineering major, City and Regional Planning major, Construction Management major, or Landscape Architecture major.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Architectural Graduate Research Studio I
courses.description: Research-based architectural design studio under the guidance of faculty. Experimentation and testing of architectural research to inform design proposals. Reviews and critiques of visual and narrative communication of research-informed design proposals. 1 discussion, 4 laboratories. Formerly ARCH 551.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Related
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Sustainability Related Prerequisite: Graduate standing.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Architectural Graduate Research Studio II
courses.description: Research-based architectural design studio under the guidance of faculty. Development of design proposals based on research. Reviews and critiques of visual and narrative communication of designs, data, simulations, and projective speculations. 1 discussion, 4 laboratories.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 551 or ARCH 5501.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Related
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Sustainability Related Prerequisite: ARCH 551 or ARCH 5501.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Testing
courses.description: Fabrication and testing of climate responsive building assemblies in multidisciplinary teams. Exercises introduce materials, workflow, and testing strategies concluding with complex problems exploring the integration of building assemblies in architecture. Field trip required. 3 activities. Formerly ARCH 561.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 551 or ARCH 5501; and ARCH 532 or ARCH 5580.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ARCH 551 or ARCH 5501; and ARCH 532 or ARCH 5580.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for graduate students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly ARCH 570.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Research Methods in Architecture
courses.description: Qualitative, quantitative, and mixed research methods to inform beginning researchers about rigorous approaches to information gathering, research, analysis, and writing. Exercises lead to a final paper on a research plan. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 4 seminars. Formerly ARCH 532.
courses.prerequisite: Enrollment in the MS Architecture program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Enrollment in the MS Architecture program.

courses.subject: ARCH
courses.title: Project
courses.description: Completion of Master's architectural project in response to a climatological problem. Culmination of research, making, and revisions based on faculty supervision and feedback. Communication of design proposal through architectural representations, critical traditions, and written report. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 1 discussion. Formerly ARCH 598.
courses.prerequisite: ARCH 532 or ARCH 5580.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ARCH 532 or ARCH 5580.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Fundamentals of Drawing
courses.description: Introduction to the artistic practice and cultural value of drawing with emphasis on the practical skills of observation, rendering, and understanding meaning in visual art. Projects encourage growth in technical skill, conceptual innovation, critical thinking, and visual communication. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ART 101.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: 2D Design
courses.description: Introduces elements and principles of design, establishing a foundation for all artistic practices. Emphasizing critical thinking and creative problem solving, the interrelationship between form and content are examined. Traditional, digital, and lens-based media are explored through individual and collaborative experiences. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 102.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: 3D Design
courses.description: Essential principles and skills for three-dimensional practices in art and design. Introduction to methods, materials, and conceptual frameworks used to create, analyze, and critique form in space and the built environment. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 104.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: 4D Design
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamental principles of four-dimensional art and design through investigations of technological form and innovation, time and motion, video and audio, animation, and performance art/live actions. Course may be offered classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Introduction to the Visual Arts
courses.description: Introduction to the material techniques and social purposes of painting, graphic arts, sculpture, performance, and architecture across diverse cultures. Builds visual analysis skills and research techniques needed to interpret and talk about the visual arts broadly. Course may be offered in classroom-base, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ART 111.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: European/U.S. Art: A Thematic History
courses.description: Introduction to artistic production, reception, and meaning throughout different eras and contexts of European/United States art. Evaluates the role of European/United States art in relation to religion, politics, and commemoration while considering the expressive nature and affective qualities of images and objects. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ART 112.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Fundamentals of Digital Media Art
courses.description: Introduction to digital media art, illustration, and design, emphasizing visual problem-solving and creative expression. Students acquire a general knowledge of digital art culture and the necessary skills to create visually compelling images. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Design Thinking and Methods
courses.description: Introduction to the principles, methods, and theories of design thinking and visual problem solving. Focus on drawing, brainstorming, ideation, and prototyping skills that designers use to think creatively and communicate visually. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Introduction to Digital Photography
courses.description: Fundamental techniques in photography. Mechanics of digital cameras, optics, composition, perception of light and subject content. Photographic principles and the language of camera vision. Introduction to the impact of photography on culture. Digital camera suggested, limited availability of cameras for check out. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ART 122.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Beginning Sculpture
courses.description: Introduction to the challenges, methods, and modalities within the expanding field of contemporary sculpture. Emphasis on understanding the signs of meaning produced in visual art. Exploration of materials, tools, and techniques, including found objects, casting, carving, wood, and metal. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ART 148.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Ceramics I
courses.description: Introduction to artistic practice and cultural value of ceramics from antiquity to 21st Century. Basic clay working emphasizing design quality and conceptual innovation through hand building and the potter's wheel. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ART 145.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Special Problems for Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies or surveys of selected problems. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly ART 200.
courses.prerequisite: Sophomore standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Sophomore standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Visual Culture and Society: Analysis and Practice
courses.description: How visual forms produce cultural meanings and how those meanings are shaped by mass media platforms and social institutions. Theoretical perspectives from semiotics, aesthetics, feminism, postcolonialism, queer theory, and other fields. Project-based assignments using applied research in visual communication. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Area 4B (GE Area D2 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.recommended: One of the following: ART 101, ART 111, ART 112, ART 212, ART 1101, ART 1111, ART 1112, or ART 2212.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 4B 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area D2
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 4B 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area D2 Recommended: One of the following: ART 101, ART 111, ART 112, ART 212, ART 1101, ART 1111, ART 1112, or ART 2212.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Renaissance to Modern Art
courses.description: The significant visual expressions of European art of the Renaissance to Modern periods. Relevant parallel examples of the art of antiquity. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly ART 212.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Global Contemporary Art
courses.description: Global history of visual art from 1945 to the present. Blending of art and life, the impact of race, gender and sexuality, globalization, post-colonialism, and the development of new mediums like performance, installation, video, and digital art. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Replaced ART 315.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ART 112, ART 211, ART 212, ART 213, ART 1112, or ART 2212.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: ART 112, ART 211, ART 212, ART 213, ART 1112, or ART 2212.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Graphic Design I
courses.description: Exploration of the technical and conceptual underpinnings of graphic design. Focus on the design process and how raw ideas are translated into professional work. Emphasis on inclusive design and addressing the needs of people of different backgrounds and abilities. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 237.
courses.prerequisite: ART 102 or ART 1102; and one of the following: ART 182, ART 183, ART 1130, or ART 1141.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Typography I
courses.description: Introduction to the history, technology, principles, and practices of typography. Focus on the design process, conceptual and technical aspects of visual communication with type and text, and creating accessible design for diverse users/audiences. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 238.
courses.prerequisite: ART 102 or ART 1102; and one of the following: ART 182, ART 183, ART 1130, or ART 1141.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ART 102 or ART 1102; and one of the following: ART 182, ART 183, ART 1130, or ART 1141.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Interaction Design I
courses.description: An introduction to the design and development concepts, principles, and practices for interactive media. Exploration of methods for research, planning, creating, and implementing meaningful interactive experiences and digital spaces. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 288.
courses.prerequisite: ART 237 or ART 2241; and ART 238 or ART 2242.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ART 237 or ART 2241; and ART 238 or ART 2242.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Camera and Light
courses.description: Fundamental techniques, principles, language of photography and video. Use of digital cameras and professional editing software to craft powerful lens-based work and professional prints. Introduction to cultural impact of photography and video. Digital camera required, limited availability of cameras for check out. 2 lecture, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: Art and Design major or Photography and Video minor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Art and Design major or Photography and Video minor.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Creative Lighting
courses.description: Introductory to advanced lighting techniques for photography and video through concept-driven projects. Emphasis on manipulating the quality of available and artificial light to create dynamic cinematic images. Not open to students with credit in ART 3361. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 224.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ART 122, ART 182, ART 1130, ART 1160, or ART 2260.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: ART 122, ART 182, ART 1130, ART 1160, or ART 2260.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Black and White Photography
courses.description: Explore photography as a means of visual communication and creative expression, using analog black and white processes to produce contemporary photographic work. Emphasis on 'photographic seeing', concept development, and professional quality printing. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 222.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. 1 to 4 lectures. Formerly ART 270.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Intermediate Drawing
courses.description: Development of additional drawing techniques with emphasis on form, content, pictorial space, figure drawing, black and white media, color, mixed media, and composition. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 201.
courses.prerequisite: ART 101 or ART 1101.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ART 101 or ART 1101.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Beginning Painting
courses.description: Introduction to technical and formal problems in painting. Exploration of pictorial space, light, and color from observation. Physical characteristics of paint, various tools, studio methods, and styles of painting. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 209.
courses.prerequisite: ART 101 or ART 1101.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ART 101 or ART 1101.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Art of the Americas
courses.description: History of visual art from the United States, Mexico, Central America, and Canada. Emphasis on relationship between artistic developments and socio-political contexts, such as the impact of colonialism on indigenous traditions, industrialization, and the formation of national identities. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 3 (GE Area Upper-Division C for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Nineteenth Century Art of Europe and the United States
courses.description: History of painting and sculpture from the French Revolution to the beginning of the 20th century. Focuses on significant movements such as Neo-Classicism, Romanticism, Realism, Impressionism, and Post-Impressionism. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Design History
courses.description: Study of major design philosophies and historical movements from the early nineteenth century to the present, with a focus on relationships between visual and technical features of design works, their purpose, and their social, cultural, political, and technological contexts. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly ART 313.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ART 112, ART 211, ART 212, ART 213, ART 1112, or ART 2212.

courses.title: History and Contemporary Practices of Photography
courses.description: In-depth survey of the artistic and cultural achievements in photography from its invention to the present day. Focus on social/cultural context and impact as well as the evolution of aesthetic criteria in the context of other visual arts. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 3 (GE Area Upper-Division C for students on the 2022-26 catalog). Formerly ART 314.

courses.title: Asian Art Survey
courses.description: Survey of Asian art - primarily India, China and Japan. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 3 (GE Area Upper-Division C for students on the 2022-26 catalog).

courses.description: The art and life of Michelangelo (1475-1564), the renowned painter, sculptor, architect, and poet, with reference to early biographies and his artistic development. courses.description: Thematic analysis of Renaissance art with special attention paid to politics, religion, mythology, specific regions, and new genres. courses.description: Thematic study of global modern and contemporary art (1900-present) through topics that focus on the relationships between artistic movements and their social, cultural, and political contexts. courses.description: In-depth study of past and contemporary media arts practices in the 20th and 21st centuries; Examines how artists use new technologies to present knowledge and alter social, cultural and political behaviors. courses.title: Politics of Abstraction
courses.description: Thematic exploration of artists from different cultural backgrounds who use abstraction to address social and political issues in a global context. Focus on how abstract visual techniques can communicate meaning and how social contexts shape artistic practice and viewership. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 3 (GE Area Upper-Division C for students on the 2022-26 catalog).

courses.title: Intersectional Feminist Art Histories
courses.description: Intersectional feminist exploration of the role of women, gender, and sexuality in the visual arts and art history. In-depth focus on intersectional feminisms as they impact the study of the visual arts and art history. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 seminars. courses.description: Introduction to the theories, practices, and institutional histories of the curatorial profession, including organizational structures of arts institutions, case studies of major exhibitions, key theories of curatorial practice, and issues of social/cultural representation. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 4 units. Course may be offered in online or hybrid format. 2 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: Art and Design major or Art History minor.

courses.description: Critical thinking and technical skills to design and storyboard for animation, interactive, and immersive projects. Through concept art and storyboarding, students complete short animations, and mixed reality experiences animatics. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 333.

courses.title: Three-dimensional Design and Modeling for Animation and Interactive Art
courses.description: Development of skills and techniques in the use of three-dimensional design and modeling via digital technology. courses.description: Exploration of art activism as a catalyst for change and methodology to mend social issues. courses.title: Typography II
courses.description: Advanced exploration of the history, technology, principles, and practices of typography. courses.title: Interaction Design II
courses.description: Design of original and innovative interaction design products in different media using a user-centered design framework and various methods of design research, testing, and prototyping. courses.description: Exploration of the book as art object. Creation of traditional structures and derivations including accordion, pamphlet, stab, pop-up, and multiple signature books. courses.description: Introduction to commercial illustration used in the visual communications industry. Exploration of illustration history in relation to global and diverse cultural contexts. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 334.
courses.prerequisite: Art and Design major.
courses.recommended: ART 101 or ART 1101; and ART 102 or ART 1102.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Art and Design major. Recommended: ART 101 or ART 1101; and ART 102 or ART 1102.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Portfolio: Graphic Design
courses.description: Focus on professional design practice, presentation skills, and the development of an individualized portfolio. Critically examines the designer's role in contemporary society. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory.

courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ART 237 or ART 2241; ART 238 or ART 2242; and ART 288 or ART 2243.

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Studio Lighting
courses.description: An overview of lighting tools and techniques used in a professional photography studio. Emphasis on seeing and manipulating the quality and shape of light for a variety of commercial and fine art applications. Not open to students with credit in ART 2261. 1 laboratory.

courses.title: Photographic Expression
courses.description: Control of lens-based materials, processes and conceptual development for personal projects. Introduction to semiotics and the study and analysis of historic and contemporary creative photographers. Repeatable up to 8 units. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ART 324.

courses.title: Large Format Photography

courses.title: Advertising Photography

courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ART 122, ART 1160, or ART 2260.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: ART 122, ART 1160, or ART 2260.

courses.title: Portfolio: Photo Video
courses.description: Developing a photography and video practice, portfolio, and professional goals. Rigorous critiques, lectures, discussions, art writing, research, and individual conceptual and formal development. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures 1 laboratory.

courses.description: Continued study of technical and formal problems in painting. Emphasis on the creative process, development of individual ideas, and the connection between form and content. courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ART 209 or ART 2282.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Livestock Evaluation
courses.description: Comparative evaluation of breeding and marketing animals. Selecting and grading for breeding and performance of beef cattle, swine, and sheep. Emphasis on accurate, clear, and concise oral reasoning. 2 laboratories. Formerly ASCI 226.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Recommended: ASCI 112 or ASCI 1102.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
courses.description: Comprehensive overview of the principal organ systems of farm animals using an integrative, systemic approach to learning the mechanisms of homeostasis in mammals with application to their daily care and management. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 229.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 112 or ASCI 1101: and BIO 161 or BIO 1151.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ASCI 112 or ASCI 1101: and BIO 161 or BIO 1151.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Beef and Dairy Cattle Management
courses.description: Selection, breeding, feeding, and management of beef and dairy cattle. Composition and value of beef and dairy products. Overview of marketing factors influencing the production systems. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 112; or ASCI 1101, ASCI 1102, and ASCI 1103.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ASCI 112; or ASCI 1101, ASCI 1102, and ASCI 1103.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Swine and Poultry Management
courses.description: Application of biological principles to the production of swine and poultry. Overview of the swine and poultry industries, biosecurity and health, feeding and nutrition, production and processing systems and management. Not open to students with credit in ASCI 222 and ASCI 225. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 112; or ASCI 1101, ASCI 1102, and ASCI 1103.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ASCI 112; or ASCI 1101, ASCI 1102, and ASCI 1103.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Small Ruminant and Rangeland Management
courses.description: Small ruminant management, industry and application in ecologically sustainable grazing systems. Introduction to rangeland ecology and management, with applications to livestock grazing for natural resource management. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 112; or ASCI 1101, ASCI 1102, and ASCI 1103.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: ASCI 112; or ASCI 1101, ASCI 1102, and ASCI 1103.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Companion Animal Management
courses.description: Equine and other companion animal (canine, feline, reptiles, small mammals kept as pets) anatomy and physiology, management, behavior, reproduction, nutrition, and common diseases. Human-animal bond and zoonotic principles. Current pet industry trends including animal welfare issues. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 112; or ASCI 1101, ASCI 1102, and ASCI 1103.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ASCI 112; or ASCI 1101, ASCI 1102, and ASCI 1103.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Principles of Rangeland Management
courses.description: Characteristics of rangeland ecosystems, processes of directing ecological change, the history of their management, particularly in North America. Laboratory activities introduce basic ecological monitoring practices, including quantification of biomass, soil cover, and species composition. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 239.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly ASCI 270.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of Instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of Instructor.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Animal Genetics
courses.description: Principles of modern classical genetics. Mendelian genetics, meiosis, mitosis, DNA structure and replication, gene mapping, chromosome rearrangement, mutations, genetic variants, gene regulation, transcription, translation, and population, quantitative, and molecular genetics in animals and humans. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly ASCI 302.
courses.prerequisite: BIO 111, BIO 161, or BIO 1151; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: BIO 111, BIO 161, or BIO 1151; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Animal Parasitology
courses.description: Diagnosis, management, and treatment of internal and external parasites in livestock, companion animals, and wildlife. Pathophysiology of parasitic infections in animals. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Replaces ASCI 203.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Animal Genomics
courses.description: Application of genetic principles for domestic animal improvement. Improving animal performance and health through use of genetic markers and diagnostics, gene mapping, and related current technologies. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures. Formerly ASCI 304.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 302 or ASCI 3302.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ASCI 302 or ASCI 3302.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Technical Veterinary Skills
courses.description: Restraint and handling of animals, physical examination, necropsy, wound management, applied pharmacology, and medical record keeping. Assisting with clinical procedures including intravenous catheter placement, fluid administration, venipuncture, imaging, anesthesia, and surgery. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 310.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Advanced Beef Cattle System Management
courses.description: Sustainable beef production. Systems approach for financial analysis, range management, breeding systems, nutrition, health programs, marketing, and production practices to enhance profitability and efficiency of commercial cow-calf operations. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 311.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 221 or ASCI 2230.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ASCI 221 or ASCI 2230.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Production Medicine
courses.description: Basic disease concepts, fundamentals of immunology, antimicrobial stewardship, therapeutics, and disease prevention principles (infectious and non-infectious) on a herd level. Pre-harvest food safety, milk and meat quality assurance. Herd health management programs for production efficiency and product quality. 2 lectures. Formerly ASCI 312.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229; one of the following: ASCI 221, ASCI 2001, ASCI 2003, ASCI 2004, ASCI 2006, ASCI 2230, ASCI 4002, ASCI 4003, ASCI 4005, ASCI 4006, or DSCI 230; and one of the following: ASCI 222, ASCI 223, ASCI 224, ASCI 225, ASCI 227, ASCI 2231, ASCI 2232, or ASCI 2233.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229; one of the following: ASCI 221, ASCI 2001, ASCI 2003, ASCI 2004, ASCI 2006, ASCI 2230, ASCI 4002, ASCI 4003, ASCI 4005, ASCI 4006, or DSCI 230; and one of the following: ASCI 222, ASCI 223, ASCI 224, ASCI 225, ASCI 227, ASCI 2231, ASCI 2232, or ASCI 2233.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Physiological Chemistry of Animals
courses.description: Integration of the principles of chemistry, biochemistry, physiology and nutrition to understand metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins at the cellular, organ and whole animal level. Regulation and coordination of metabolic function within and across tissues in animals. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ASCI 319.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); one of the following: ASCI 229, ASCI 2229, BIO 231, BIO 2231, BIO 361, or BIO 3352; and one of the following: CHEM 212, CHEM 216, CHEM 2242, CHEM 312, or CHEM 2240.
courses.recommended: One of the following: DATA 1000, STAT 130, STAT 218, or STAT 1110.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); one of the following: ASCI 229, ASCI 2229, BIO 231, BIO 2231, BIO 361, or BIO 3352; and one of the following: CHEM 212, CHEM 216, CHEM 2242, CHEM 312, or CHEM 2240. Recommended: One of the following: DATA 1000, STAT 130, STAT 218, or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Zoonoses and Veterinary Public Health Concerns
courses.description: Public health concerns related to animal and bird diseases transmissible to humans, environmental public health hazards, and antimicrobial resistance. Focus on One Health concepts: the relationships between humans, animals, and the environment. 3 lectures. Formerly ASCI 321.
courses.prerequisite: BIO 161 or BIO 1151.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: BIO 161 or BIO 1151.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Internship in Animal Science
courses.description: Work with an approved agriculture firm or related to animal science. Develop production and managerial skills through practices. Repeatable up to 8 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly ASCI 339.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of department head.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of department head.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Animal Welfare and Ethics
courses.description: Introduction to moral principles that have shaped the field of animal welfare science. Definition of Animal Welfare. Identification of science-based measures of welfare. Current welfare concerns with companion, laboratory, production, and exotic animals. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly ASCI 340.
courses.prerequisite: Junior Standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior Standing.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Equine Nutrition
courses.description: Equine gastrointestinal anatomy and physiology, feeding ecology. Nutrient requirements, feed characteristics, analysis and practical applications. Diet formulation and evaluation. Management of common metabolic and nutrition imbalances. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 346.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 220 or ASCI 2220 with a grade of C- or better.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ASCI 220 or ASCI 2220 with a grade of C- or better.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Equine Exercise Physiology
courses.description: Applied physiology of the exercising horse. Examination of musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, respiratory, and endocrine systems. Energetics of metabolism during exercise. Physiological adaptations to conditioning of horses. Gait analysis and common equine sports injuries. 2 lectures. Formerly ASCI 347.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229; and ASCI 224 or ASCI 2233.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229; and ASCI 224 or ASCI 2233.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Nonruminant Nutrition
courses.description: Comparison of the digestive physiology and nutrition of nonruminants. Digestive tract anatomy, energy and nutrient requirements, diet formulation and processing, nutritional management. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 350.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 220 or ASCI 2220 with a grade of C- or better or consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ASCI 220 or ASCI 2220 with a grade of C- or better or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Mechanisms of Hormone Action and Reproductive Physiology
courses.description: Synthesis, secretion, and mechanisms of hormone action. Comparative animal reproductive anatomy and physiology including gametogenesis, behavior, gestation, parturition and mothering. 3 lectures. Formerly ASCI 351.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Ruminant Nutrition
courses.description: Gastrointestinal tract form and function, ingredient characterization and utilization, post-absorptive metabolism, diet formulation, and nutritional management, as applied to ruminant livestock. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 355.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 220 or ASCI 2220; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ASCI 220 or ASCI 2220; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Holistic Management
courses.description: Application of holistic management, a goal-oriented, value-driven framework for making ecologically, economically, and socially sound decisions. Holistic approach to management, especially of land-based resources, aimed toward greater biodiversity and sustainability. Field trip may be required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as AG/ASCI 3360. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly AG/ASCI 360.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5 (GE Areas B1 to B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5 (GE Areas B1 to B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Professional Development in the Animal Sciences
courses.description: Animal or dairy science career development and personal branding. Interpersonal communication and resume development. Interpretation of scientific articles, research-based oral presentations, and interviewing skills. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 1 lecture. Formerly ASCI 363.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Veterinary Pharmacology
courses.description: Investigation of pharmacological principles applied to animal systems. Overview of drugs acting on the nervous, endocrine, circulatory, urinary, and reproductive systems. Specialty areas of pharmacology, and pharmacogenomics of livestock and companion animals. 2 lectures. Formerly ASCI 366.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229; and one of the following: CHEM 216, CHEM 312, CHEM 2240, or CHEM 2242.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229; and one of the following: CHEM 216, CHEM 312, CHEM 2240, or CHEM 2242.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Rangeland Improvements
courses.description: Review of practices used for improving the productivity or ecological functions of rangeland landscapes managed for grazing livestock, wildlife, or for ecological and/or aesthetic values. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures. Formerly ASCI 370.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 239, ASCI 2239, or ASCI 2232.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ASCI 239, ASCI 2239, or ASCI 2232.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: California Rangeland and Ranch Resource Management
courses.description: Rangeland conservation and management practices recommended for environmental protection in California. Includes water quality protection, sensitive species/habitat management, principles of fuels management, and practices appropriate to rangeland ecosystems for reduction of wildfire risk. Field trip may be required. 3 lectures. Formerly ASCI 372.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 239, ASCI 2239, or ASCI 2232.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ASCI 239, ASCI 2239, or ASCI 2232.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Artificial Insemination of Beef Cattle Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Advanced experience in heat detection, estrous synchronization and artificial insemination of beef cattle. Credit/No Credit grading only. Half-semester course. 1 activity.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ASCI 351, ASCI 3351, DSCI 330, or DSCI 3330.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: One of the following: ASCI 351, ASCI 3351, DSCI 330, or DSCI 3330.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Bull Test Management Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Management of a beef bull genetic evaluation program using advanced skills to implement the annual bull sale. Student managers are responsible for training their peers in the following activities: nutritional management, health management, event planning, and marketing. Field trip may be required. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 lecture, 1 activity.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 2003.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: ASCI 2003.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Bull Test Sale Implementation Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Advanced experience in management of the annual Cal Poly Bull Test Sale. Beef cattle marketing, biotechnology, event planning, leadership skills, multimedia applications, and peer mentorship. Credit/No Credit grading only. Half-semester course. 1 activity.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 4002.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: ASCI 4002.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Equine Mustang Management Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Advanced experience in managing the care, training, conditioning, and showcasing of mustangs and other horses used for university events on and off campus. Repeatable up to 4 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 2 activities.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Ranch Management I Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Advanced beef cattle and ranch management experience focused on low-stress cattle handling, calving and breeding management. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 2230.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: ASCI 2230.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Ranch Management II Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Advanced beef cattle and ranch management focused on vaccination, weaning, pregnancy diagnosis, and land management. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 2230.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: ASCI 2230.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Horse and Mule Packing Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Advanced experience in training and packing horses and mules to carry trail worthy loads and participating in packing competitions. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Livestock Event Planning Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Advanced experience in livestock event planning. Organization and planning for the Western Bonanza Junior Livestock Show. Repeatable up to 4 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 2 lectures. Formerly ASCI 412.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 212 or ASCI 2017; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: ASCI 212 or ASCI 2017; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Livestock Event Implementation Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Advanced experience in livestock show implementation. Student management of the Western Bonanza Junior Livestock Show. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Half-semester course. 1 activity. Formerly ASCI 413.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 412 or ASCI 4008.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: ASCI 412 or ASCI 4008.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Livestock Judging Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Advanced analysis and application of factors involved in the selection and evaluation of cattle, sheep, goats, and swine for breeding and slaughter. Presentation of concise oral and/or written reasons to defend selection decisions. Training for college Livestock Judging Team. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Marine Mammal Health Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Participation in NOAA West Coast Stranding Network through a professional partnership with The Marine Mammal Center. Field response of sick and injured marine mammals, animal care, basic medical skills, oiled wildlife response training, investigation of population health concerns. Field trip required. Credit/No Credit grading only. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Performance Horse Production Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Further training of the horses for the annual Cal Poly Performance Horse Sale. Credit/No Credit grading only. 3 activities.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 2011 and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: ASCI 2011 and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Equine Sale Event Planning Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Introduction to equine sales preparation. Design and implement a training program to maximize the saleability of the performance horse. Credit/No Credit grading only. 3 activities.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 4012 and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: ASCI 4012 and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Equine Sale Event Implementation Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Preparation and implementation of a commercial equine sale event, including budgeting, risk management, marketing, promotion. Critical analysis of the individual performance horse as a sales prospect and adaptation to optimized marketability. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 seminar, 2 activities.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 4013 and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: ASCI 4013 and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Veterinary Community Service Advanced Enterprise
courses.description: Advanced experience in Cal Poly Community Veterinary Service Clinics. Field experience providing basic wellness veterinary services (physical exams, flea and tick prevention, vaccination, and nail trims) to pets of the homeless members of the local community. Field trip required. Credit/No Credit grading only. 2 activities.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 2016.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: ASCI 2016.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Special Problems for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of special problems. Repeatable up to 3 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly ASCI 400.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Applied Biotechnology in Animal Science
courses.description: Coverage of current resources, techniques and methodologies used in animal research and biotechnology as well as experimental design, model assessment, and data interpretation with application to an experimental setting in the laboratory. 1 lecture, 2 laboratories. Formerly ASCI 403.
courses.prerequisite: BIO 161 or BIO 1151; and one of the following: ASCI 302, ASCI 3302, BIO 302, BIO 3312, BIO 351, or BIO 3351; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: BIO 161 or BIO 1151; and one of the following: ASCI 302, ASCI 3302, BIO 302, BIO 3312, BIO 351, or BIO 3351; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Domestic Livestock Endocrinology
courses.description: Endocrine physiology with emphasis on the influence of hormones involved in digestion, metabolism and growth. Endocrine regulation of thyroid, parathyroid, and adrenal glands. Aspects of of reproduction, pregnancy, and lactation. Receptor hypothesis and signal transduction. 3 lectures. Formerly ASCI 405.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ASCI 229, ASCI 2229, BIO 361, or BIO 3352.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: One of the following: ASCI 229, ASCI 2229, BIO 361, or BIO 3352.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Animal Embryology and Assisted Reproduction
courses.description: Comparative physiology including molecular understanding of oocyte and spermatozoa development and in vitro fertilization. Culturing, cryopreservation and micromanipulation of gametes and embryos. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly ASCI 406.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229; and ASCI 351 or ASCI 3351.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229; and ASCI 351 or ASCI 3351.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Assisted Reproduction Technologies and Laboratory
courses.description: Coverage of advanced techniques and methodologies of assisted reproduction of gametes and embryos involving in-vivo collection, in-vitro fertilization, cryopreservation and micromanipulation. 1 lecture, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 407.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229; ASCI 351 or ASCI 3351; and ASCI 406 or ASCI 4406.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229; ASCI 351 or ASCI 3351; and ASCI 406 or ASCI 4406.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Applied Animal Behavior Science
courses.description: Principles of behavior applied to animals in managed environments. Observation and measurement of behavior, including sampling and recording methods. Learning, including training and operant conditioning. Discussion of issues related to behavioral welfare. Etiology and management of maladaptive behavior. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 410.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing; or Junior standing and ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing; or Junior standing and ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: HACCP for Meat and Poultry Operations
courses.description: Using Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) principles to develop regulatory inspection plans for meat and poultry operations; development and use of prerequisite programs; microbiological control and process overviews. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly ASCI 415.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: Graduate standing, ASCI 211, ASCI 2210, or FDSC 3330.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: Graduate standing, ASCI 211, ASCI 2210, or FDSC 3330.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Animal Metabolism and Nutritional Modeling
courses.description: Relation of nutrient metabolism to animal production. Methods of determining and predicting nutrient requirements and approaches to developing animal nutritional models. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly ASCI 419.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 220 or ASCI 2220 with grade of C- or better; and one of the following: ASCI 319, ASCI 3319, CHEM 319, CHEM 3350, CHEM 369, or CHEM 3352.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ASCI 220 or ASCI 2220 with grade of C- or better; and one of the following: ASCI 319, ASCI 3319, CHEM 319, CHEM 3350, CHEM 369, or CHEM 3352.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Meat Industry Study Tour
courses.description: Study tour of commercial meat businesses. Livestock harvest and carcass fabrication, further meat processing, retail and food service operations. Personnel, processing procedures, regulatory standards, industry specifications and current issues. Travel for 4 days. 1 activity. Formerly ASCI 425.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing, ASCI 211, or ASCI 2210.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing, ASCI 211, or ASCI 2210.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Systemic Animal Physiology
courses.description: Homeostatic functions in organ systems, integration of systems, and how disruptions in homeostasis result in disease. Neurology, cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, urogenital, and endocrinologic systems. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 438.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing; or ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229.
courses.recommended: One of the following: ASCI 319, ASCI 3319, CHEM 314, CHEM 3350, CHEM 369, or CHEM 3352.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing; or ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229. Recommended: One of the following: ASCI 319, ASCI 3319, CHEM 314, CHEM 3350, CHEM 369, or CHEM 3352.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Immunology and Diseases of Animals
courses.description: Examination of the immune system of domesticated animals. Immunological analyses and examination of current disease issues. Field trip may be required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 440.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ASCI 229 or ASCI 2229.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Equine Reproduction
courses.description: Reproductive anatomy and physiology of the mare and stallion. Assisted reproductive technologies in horses; management of sub-fertile horses, donor and recipient mares; manipulation of endocrine system; embryo technologies; cryobiology of gametes and embryos. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 455.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 224 or ASCI 2233; and ASCI 351 or ASCI 3351.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ASCI 224 or ASCI 2233; and ASCI 351 or ASCI 3351.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Rangeland Assessment and Planning
courses.description: Examination of methods used for evaluating rangeland ecosystems, and the application of planning processes used in the management of rangelands and associated ecosystems. Field trip may be required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 460.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 239, ASCI 2239, or ASCI 2232.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ASCI 239, ASCI 2239, or ASCI 2232.

courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Senior standing; ASCI 363 or ASCI 3363; and consent of department head.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Senior Project - Current Issues in Animal Science
courses.description: Critical evaluation and formal presentation of current issues facing animals in managed systems. Evaluation of current trends and emerging issues, analysis of supporting evidence and logic, and synthesis and formal presentation of the resulting perspectives on different approaches to current challenges. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures. Formerly ASCI 479.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; and ASCI 363 or ASCI 3363.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing; and ASCI 363 or ASCI 3363.

courses.subject: ASCI
courses.title: Poultry Meat and Egg Production and Processing
courses.description: Modern production techniques for the poultry meat industry. Management of hatcheries, poultry production, and poultry meat processing. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ASCI 330.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 211, ASCI 2210, or ASCI 2231.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ASCI 211, ASCI 2210, or ASCI 2231.

courses.subject: ASCI

courses.description: Overview of fundamental concepts in biology and of scientific inquiry. Principles of cellular life and energetics, inheritance and genetic mechanisms, evolution and ecology. Relationship between biology and human affairs. Not open for major credit in Biological Sciences, Microbiology, or Marine Sciences. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 5B (GE Areas B2 and B3 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).
