courses.subject: BUS
courses.title: Business Analytics
courses.description: Introduction to the concepts and applications of business analytics, using business case study and problem-solving approach. Data warehouse design and implementation. Supervised learning techniques for classification and prediction. Unsupervised learning techniques for dimension reduction and pattern recognition. Text analytics. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly BUS 497.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: STAT 252, STAT 301, STAT 1220, or STAT 1510.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP, SU Prerequisite: One of the following: STAT 252, STAT 301, STAT 1220, or STAT 1510.

courses.subject: BUS
courses.title: Business Analytics Project
courses.description: Selection and completion of one or more projects under faculty supervision that complements the coursework on business analytics. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP, SU Corequisite: BUS 4497.

courses.subject: BUS
courses.title: Directed Topics in Information Systems
courses.description: Specialized Information Systems (IS) topic selected from the IS areas of current interest. Intended for advanced IS concentration students who want to learn and acquire in-depth IS knowledge and skills. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 9 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly BUS 498.
courses.prerequisite: BUS 392 or BUS 3392.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: BUS 392 or BUS 3392.

courses.subject: BUS
courses.title: Data Communications and Networking
courses.description: Combines concepts of data communications and networking with practical applications in business. Technical and managerial aspects of business telecommunication. Introduction to data communications, applications and technical fundamentals, network products, technologies, applications, and services. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly BUS 499.
courses.prerequisite: BUS 391 or BUS 3391.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: BUS 391 or BUS 3391.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Orientation to the Child Development Major
courses.description: Orientation to the child development major and child development as a career. Introduction to requirements of the major, available resources, strategies for academic success, and career options in psychology and child development. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures. Formerly CD 102.
courses.prerequisite: Child Development major.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Child Development major.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Observing and Interacting with Children
courses.description: Observation methods and guidance techniques for adults working with children in family, community, and educational settings. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly CD 131.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Special Problems
courses.description: Scholarly investigation of selected topics, engagement in research, applying psychological research and theory to experiential learning opportunities. Includes a written report and topic are chosen with prior approval of instructor. Repeatable up to 8 units. Formerly CD 200.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Developmental Science Technology Activity
courses.description: Technology applications (e.g., websites, film, podcasts, blogs) as they relate to communication of research and theory in developmental science. Digital tools used by developmental researchers and professionals when working with children, youth, and families. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 1 lecture, 2 activities. Replaced CD 302.
courses.prerequisite: CD 102 or CD 1102; and CD/PSY 256 or CD/PSY 2256.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CD 102 or CD 1102; and CD/PSY 256 or CD/PSY 2256.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Children's Learning and Development in Educational Settings
courses.description: Introduction to developmental and learning theories of children/teens. Emphasis on observations/interactions with culturally and linguistically diverse learners. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Crosslisted as CD/EDUC 2207. Formerly CD/EDUC 207.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Research Methods in Psychology
courses.description: Introduction to research methods used in psychology and other behavioral sciences. Includes the logic and ethics of research; experimental, correlational, and survey methodology; library search strategies; basic statistical procedures; and the format of the research report. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as CD/PSY 2229. Replaced PSY 329.
courses.prerequisite: PSY 201 or PSY 2201; and STAT 217 or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: PSY 201 or PSY 2201; and STAT 217 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Preschool Laboratory
courses.description: Preliminary teaching experience with children in a preschool laboratory setting. Participant planning, execution and evaluation of age-appropriate activities. Observation is used as the basis for planning for the development of the whole child. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CD 230.
courses.prerequisite: CD/PSY 256 or CD/PSY 2256.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CD/PSY 256 or CD/PSY 2256.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Child, Family, and Community
courses.description: Research and theory on the dynamics of children's relationships with their families/communities throughout development and within various contexts. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly CD/PSY 254.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Introduction to the scientific study of development with emphasis on the lifespan, from infancy to old age. Basic research and concepts in understanding social, emotional, cognitive, contextual, and diversity influences on development. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as CD/PSY 2256. Formerly CD/PSY 256.
courses.prerequisite: PSY 201 or PSY 2201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: PSY 201 or PSY 2201.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly CD 270.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Infant and Toddler Development
courses.description: Human development from conception through the second year of life. Examination of theory and research in multiple domains of development. Consideration of environments and activities which enhance the emerging capabilities of infants and toddlers. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 lectures. Formerly CD 304.
courses.prerequisite: CD/PSY 256 or CD/PSY 2256.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CD/PSY 256 or CD/PSY 2256.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Early and Middle Childhood Development
courses.description: In-depth study of theory and research on development in early and middle childhood, especially within physical, cognitive, social, and emotional domains. Consideration of case studies and current practices in light of theoretical perspectives and current research. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 lectures. Formerly CD 305.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CD/PSY256, CD/PSY 2256, CD/EDUC207, or CD/EDUC 2207.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: One of the following: CD/PSY256, CD/PSY 2256, CD/EDUC207, or CD/EDUC 2207.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Adolescence
courses.description: Psychological analysis of the years from prepubescence to young adulthood. Current research on behavior and development during adolescence with emphasis on physical, affective, cognitive, sociocultural, historical, family, peer and school aspects of life during the post-child, pre-adult years. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 lectures. Crosslisted as CD/PSY 3306. Formerly CD/PSY 306.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CD/PSY 256, CD/PSY 2256, CD/EDUC 207, or CD/EDUC 2207.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: CD/PSY 256, CD/PSY 2256, CD/EDUC 207, or CD/EDUC 2207.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Advanced Research Methods in Developmental Science
courses.description: Advanced design and analytic techniques in developmental psychology. Critical evaluation of developmental psychological science research. Design and conduct a small-scale research project. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly CD 329.
courses.prerequisite: PSY 329 or CD/PSY 2229; and STAT 217 or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: PSY 329 or CD/PSY 2229; and STAT 217 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Developmental Science in Education
courses.description: Issues and research concerning how children and youth develop and learn in school (preschool - high school). Motivation, views of intelligence, teacher and student relations, constructivist learning environments, socioemotional learning, inclusive school climates, home-school connections. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 lectures. Formerly CD 350.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CD/EDUC 207, CD/EDUC 2207, PSY/CD 256, or PSY/CD 2256.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: One of the following: CD/EDUC 207, CD/EDUC 2207, PSY/CD 256, or PSY/CD 2256.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Learning in Out-of-School Time
courses.description: How children and youth develop and learn in informal settings, such as everyday family activities, nature, informal learning institutions, and organized extracurricular activities. Research findings and theoretical perspectives on how activity in such settings supports development and learning. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 lectures. Formerly CD 351.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CD/PSY 256, CD/PSY 2256, CD/EDUC 207, or CD/EDUC 2207.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: One of the following: CD/PSY 256, CD/PSY 2256, CD/EDUC 207, or CD/EDUC 2207.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Child and Adolescent Mental Health
courses.description: Applications of psychological and developmental principles to child and adolescent mental health outcomes. Differences in cognitive, social, emotional and behavioral outcomes. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 seminars. Crosslisted as CD/PSY 3356. Formerly CD/PSY 356.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: PSY 305, PSY 2205, PSY 252, PSY 2252, PSY 256, or CD/PSY 2256.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing; and one of the following: PSY 305, PSY 2205, PSY 252, PSY 2252, PSY 256, or CD/PSY 2256. Recommended: CD/PSY 256 or CD/PSY 2256.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Special Problems for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Scholarly investigation of special problems, engagement in research, applying psychological research and theory to experiential learning opportunities. Includes a written report and topic are chosen with prior approval of instructor. Repeatable up to 8 units. Formerly CD 400.
courses.prerequisite: One upper-division CD class and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: One upper-division CD class and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Children, Adolescents, and Technology
courses.description: Examination of research and theory on how use of digital technologies such as electronic toys, television, video games, virtual reality, educational technologies, assistive technologies, and social media relates to children's and adolescents' development across domains. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 lectures. Formerly CD 411.
courses.prerequisite: CD 329 or CD 3329; and two of the following: CD 304, CD 3304, CD 305, CD 3305, PSY/CD 306, or PSY/CD 3306.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CD 329 or CD 3329; and two of the following: CD 304, CD 3304, CD 305, CD 3305, PSY/CD 306, or PSY/CD 3306.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Interpersonal Relationships in Childhood and Adolescence
courses.description: Current theories and research on the development of interpersonal relationships in childhood and adolescence. Topics may include parent-child relationships, peer relationships in childhood, intimate relationships in adolescence. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 lectures. Crosslisted as CD/PSY 4417. Formerly CD/PSY 417.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CD 304, CD 3304, CD 305, CD 3305, CD/PSY 306, or CD/PSY 3306; or CD/PSY 256 or CD/PSY 2256, and any upper-division PSY course.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: One of the following: CD 304, CD 3304, CD 305, CD 3305, CD/PSY 306, or CD/PSY 3306; or CD/PSY 256 or CD/PSY 2256, and any upper-division PSY course.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Children's Development in Diverse Cultures
courses.description: Examination of research on child and adolescent development in diverse families and community settings. Close examination of cultural communities in different countries (cross-cultural) and in the United States (multicultural) using sociocultural frameworks. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 seminars. Formerly CD 424.
courses.prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 6 (GE Area F for the 2022-26 catalog); and two of the following: CD 304, CD 3304, CD 305, CD 3305, CD/PSY 306, or CD/PSY 3306.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 6 (GE Area F for the 2022-26 catalog); and two of the following: CD 304, CD 3304, CD 305, CD 3305, CD/PSY 306, or CD/PSY 3306.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Child and Adolescent Assessment
courses.description: Current developmental and psychological assessments used in educational, psychological, and medical settings and research. Practice using, creating, and evaluating assessments. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 lectures. Crosslisted as CD/PSY 4431. Formerly CD/PSY 431.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CD 304, CD 3304, CD 305, CD 3305, CD/PSY 306 or CD/PSY 3306; and PSY 329 or CD/PSY 2229; and CD/PSY 356 or CD/PSY 3356.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: One of the following: CD 304, CD 3304, CD 305, CD 3305, CD/PSY 306 or CD/PSY 3306; and PSY 329 or CD/PSY 2229; and CD/PSY 356 or CD/PSY 3356.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Research Internship I
courses.description: Faculty-supervised research experience on various topics related to child and adolescent development. Student apprenticeship with a department faculty member engaging in a research project. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly CD 448.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; Child Development or Psychology major; CD/PSY 229 or CD/PSY 2229; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Junior standing; Child Development or Psychology major; CD/PSY 229 or CD/PSY 2229; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Research Internship II
courses.description: Faculty-supervised research experience on various topics related to child and adolescent development. Student apprenticeship with a department faculty member to conduct aspects of a research project. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly CD 449.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; Child Development or Psychology major; CD 448 or CD 4448; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Junior standing; Child Development or Psychology major; CD 448 or CD 4448; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Developmental Perspectives on Resilience in Childhood
courses.description: Advanced study of developmental perspectives and research on resilience in childhood and adolescence, and the implications for current programs and social policy. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 seminars. Formerly CD 450.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing, CD 329 or CD 3329, and two of the following: CD 304, CD 3304, CD 305, CD 3305, CD/PSY 306, or CD/PSY 3306.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing, CD 329 or CD 3329, and two of the following: CD 304, CD 3304, CD 305, CD 3305, CD/PSY 306, or CD/PSY 3306.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Supervised Fieldwork Internship I
courses.description: Faculty supervised fieldwork experience. Role of professional apprentice is experienced and analyzed by each student. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly CD 453.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; Psychology or Child Development major; select one of the following: PSY 304, PSY 3304, PSY 323, PSY 3323, PSY 350, PSY 3350, STAT 313, STAT 3520, COMS 316, COMS 3316, COMS 320, or COMS 3320; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Junior standing; Psychology or Child Development major; select one of the following: PSY 304, PSY 3304, PSY 323, PSY 3323, PSY 350, PSY 3350, STAT 313, STAT 3520, COMS 316, COMS 3316, COMS 320, or COMS 3320; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Supervised Fieldwork Internship II
courses.description: Supervised fieldwork experience in various community, governmental, and educational settings which complements the applied experiences gained in Supervised Fieldwork Internship I, and as determined by participating institution, supervising faculty member, and student. Credit/No credit grading only. Formerly CD 454.
courses.prerequisite: CD 453 or CD 4453; Psychology or Child Development major; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: CD 453 or CD 4453; Psychology or Child Development major; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Child Abuse and Neglect
courses.description: Issues in child maltreatment, including definitions and forms, causes, consequences, assessment, reporting, treatment, and prevention. Possible links among research, intervention, and public policy will be emphasized. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 seminars. Crosslisted as CD/PSY 4460. Formerly CD/PSY 460.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and PSY 201 or PSY 2201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing; and PSY 201 or PSY 2201.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Senior Project Seminar
courses.description: Discussion of occupational and graduate school opportunities including current issues in developmental science to define professional objectives and individual projects for senior project. Conduct scholarly literature review for preparation of senior project to inform organization and direction. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 seminars. Formerly CD 461.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; CD 329 or CD 3329; and Psychology or Child Development major.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Senior standing; CD 329 or CD 3329; and Psychology or Child Development major.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Design and completion of a faculty-supervised project in child development. Project results are presented in a formal written report and presented at the Senior Project Showcase. Formerly CD 462.
courses.prerequisite: CD 461 or CD 4461; and Child Development major.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CD 461 or CD 4461; and Child Development major.

courses.subject: CD
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of selected topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 4 lectures. Formerly CD 470.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Introduction to Civil Engineering
courses.description: Review of civil engineering and associated technical disciplines. Case study analysis. Critical self-reflection and educational goals. Leadership, ethical decision-making, design and systems thinking, sustainability, collaboration, research, engineering communication, learning, and motivation. Engineering societies and professional registration. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 lecture. Formerly CE 111.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Related
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Sustainability Related

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Spatial Visualization and Drawing
courses.description: Mentally manipulate two- and three-dimensional structures. Theory and practice of plane surveying. Application of Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Introduction to engineering drawing in the environmental, geotechnical, transportation, and structural sub-disciplines of civil engineering, including sketching and computer aided drawing (CAD). Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 1 lecture, 2 activities. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 1112. Formerly CE 113.
courses.corequisite: One of the following: CE 111, CE 1111, ENVE 111, or ENVE 1111.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Corequisite: One of the following: CE 111, CE 1111, ENVE 111, or ENVE 1111.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Special Problems for Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Repeatable up to 4 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 2200. Formerly CE 200.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor and department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor and department chair.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Computational Applications in Civil and Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Spreadsheet and programming-based approaches to civil and environmental engineering problems. Data analysis and management. Introductory linear regression, statistics and uncertainty. Financial analysis. Macros and user interfaces. Conditional and iterative analysis. Basic differential equations. Linear and basic nonlinear systems. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 2 activities. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 2251. Formerly CE 251.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 143 or MATH 1262.
courses.corequisite: CHEM 124 or CHEM 1120; and PHYS 143 or PHYS 1143.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: MATH 143 or MATH 1262. Corequisite: CHEM 124 or CHEM 1120; and PHYS 143 or PHYS 1143.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Civil Engineering Materials
courses.description: Nature and behavior of materials used for structural, water resources, transportation, geotechnical, and environmental engineering. Experimental determination of mechanical and corrosion properties. Material selection considering mechanical, durability, and sustainability factors. Use of industry standard test equipment. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 259.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM 124 or CHEM 1120; and ENGR 2211 or CE 204 and ME 211.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CHEM 124 or CHEM 1120; and ENGR 2211 or CE 204 and ME 211.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. 1 to 4 lectures. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 2270. Formerly CE 270.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Transportation Engineering
courses.description: Characteristics and functions of different modes of transportation. Fundamentals of transportation design, operations, and planning. Evaluation of costs, benefits, and environmental considerations. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 2 activities. Formerly CE 321.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CE 259, CE 2259, CM 113, CM 1113, or CE/ENVE 3465.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: CE 259, CE 2259, CM 113, CM 1113, or CE/ENVE 3465.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulic Systems
courses.description: Theory and application of fluid statics and dynamics to air and water systems. Fluid properties, pressure within stationary and moving systems, momentum, pipe flow, water regulations and treatment. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 3336.
courses.prerequisite: CE 204 and ME 211 or ENGR 2211; MATH 143 or MATH 1262; and PHYS 143 or PHYS 1143.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CE 204 and ME 211 or ENGR 2211; MATH 143 or MATH 1262; and PHYS 143 or PHYS 1143.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Water Resources & Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Hydrology, hydraulics, and environmental aspects of surface and groundwater systems and their applications to water infrastructure. Systems thinking, climate change, and social and public health issues related to water resources and environmental engineering. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 3337. Formerly CE 337.
courses.prerequisite: CE/ENVE 3336; or CE 336 and ENVE 264 or ENVE 331.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: CE/ENVE 3336; or CE 336 and ENVE 264 or ENVE 331.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Structural Analysis
courses.description: Analysis of 2D and 3D stress and strain conditions in structural materials. Analysis of beam buckling failure. Deflections of determinate and indeterminate structures, including beams, trusses, and frames, using different analytical methods. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 352.
courses.prerequisite: ENGR 2211 or CE 204 and ME 211.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ENGR 2211 or CE 204 and ME 211.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Reinforced Concrete Design
courses.description: Analytical and design principles of reinforced concrete in designing civil engineering systems. Origin of code requirements. Fundamentals of proportioning. Details of elements and structural systems. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 355.
courses.prerequisite: CE 259 or CE 2259; and CE 352 or CE 3352.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CE 259 or CE 2259; and CE 352 or CE 3352.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Construction Engineering and Management
courses.description: Construction engineering fundamentals, project lifecycle, procurement methods, cost engineering, earthworks, and soil erosion. Construction loads, temporary structures, and shoring and bracing. Construction equipment, project scheduling, and construction safety. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE/CM 371.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CE 259, CE 465, CE 2259, or CE/ENVE 3465.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: CE 259, CE 465, CE 2259, or CE/ENVE 3465.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Geotechnical Engineering
courses.description: Engineering geology, weight-volume relationships, clay mineralogy, soil classification, compaction, geostatic stress distributions, steady-state flow, consolidation settlement/rate, shear strength, lateral earth pressure, retaining wall, bearing capacity, and slope stability analyses. Use of standardized laboratory tests to determine engineering properties of soils. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 381.
courses.prerequisite: CE/ENVE 3336 or ME 341 or ENVE 264; and ENGR 2211 or CE 204.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CE/ENVE 3336 or ME 341 or ENVE 264; and ENGR 2211 or CE 204.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Infrastructure Systems
courses.description: Development of civil/environmental infrastructure as a multi-component system. Integration of civil/environmental engineering disciplines, as well as related non-engineering disciplines, as a project goes from concept through construction. Consideration of regulatory, social, management, economic, historical, and other non-technical factors. Field trip required. 2 activities. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 3465. Formerly CE 465.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.recommended: Three of the following: CE 321, CE 3321, CE/ENVE 3336, CE 336, CE/ENVE 3337, CE 352, CE 3352, CE 355, CE 3355, CE 381, CE 3381, ENVE 438, ENVE 3438, ENVE 450, or ENVE 3450.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Junior standing. Recommended: Three of the following: CE 321, CE 3321, CE/ENVE 3336, CE 336, CE/ENVE 3337, CE 352, CE 3352, CE 355, CE 3355, CE 381, CE 3381, ENVE 438, ENVE 3438, ENVE 450, or ENVE 3450.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Structural Steel Design
courses.description: American Institute of Steel Construction Load and Resistance Factor Design (AISC-LRFD). Specifications for design of structural steel components in building systems, including tension members, columns, beams, beam-columns, basic welded connections, and basic bolted connections. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 356.
courses.prerequisite: CE 352 or CE 3352.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CE 352 or CE 3352.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Special Problems
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of special problems. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly CE 400.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Consent of department chair.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Civil Engineering Design Competition
courses.description: Design, build, test, and present a solution to a civil engineering problem posed by a student design competition. The Class schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 403.
courses.prerequisite: CE 113 or CE/ENVE 1112; CE 251 or CE 2251; and CE 259 or CE 2259.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CE 113 or CE/ENVE 1112; CE 251 or CE 2251; and CE 259 or CE 2259.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Applied Finite Element Analysis
courses.description: Finite element solutions to engineering elastostatic problems using commercial finite element code. Practical modeling assignments. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as BMED/CE/ME 4404. Formerly BMED/CE/ME 404.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BMED 410, BMED 3410, CE 352, CE 3352, ME 328, or ME 3328.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: BMED 410, BMED 3410, CE 352, CE 3352, ME 328, or ME 3328.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Structural Dynamics
courses.description: Dynamics of structural systems. Creation of models for stiffness, mass, and damping. Numerical methods and programming techniques for predicting dynamic behavior. Comparison of models with experimental testing. Analysis of multidimensional structural systems via modal analysis and direct time integration. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 407.
courses.prerequisite: CE 352 or CE 3352; and one of the following: ME 212, ME 2212, or ENGR 2212.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 352 or CE 3352; and one of the following: ME 212, ME 2212, or ENGR 2212.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Advanced Civil Computer-Aided Site Design
courses.description: Apply advanced CAD software to develop design techniques and convey the completed design on a set of plans. Site coordination, basic road design, grading, and utility design. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 laboratories. Formerly CE 413.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CM 239, CM 2239, CE 113, or CE/ENVE 1112; and one of the following: CE 321, CE 465, CE 3321, or CE/ENVE 3465.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: CM 239, CM 2239, CE 113, or CE/ENVE 1112; and one of the following: CE 321, CE 465, CE 3321, or CE/ENVE 3465.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Advanced Building Information Modeling for Civil Engineering
courses.description: Building Information Modeling (BIM) process to design, optimize, construct, and manage vertical structures. BIM based quantity take-off, clash detection, 4D modeling, facility management, and 3D laser scanner applications. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 2 laboratories. Formerly CE 415.
courses.prerequisite: CE 3375 or CE/CM 371.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CE 3375 or CE/CM 371.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Traffic Engineering
courses.description: Principles of traffic circulation on highway systems and other modes. Traffic control. Traffic data collection and analysis. Capacity analysis. Traffic modeling. New technologies for traffic flow monitoring and management. Field trip may be required. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 421.
courses.prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Highway Geometrics and Design
courses.description: Principles of geometric design as they relate to highway facilities. Roadway design safety standards. Horizontal, vertical, and cross section components for roadway segments. Interchange and ramp design. Design for safety. Traffic calming methods. Cost/benefit analysis and environmental impacts. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 422.
courses.prerequisite: CE 321 or CE 3321.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 321 or CE 3321.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Intelligent Transportation Systems
courses.description: Specification and operation of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). Traffic surveillance and control systems including applications to freeways, urban streets, rural highways, and public transportation. Standards including the National Architecture for ITS. Field trip may be required. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 423.
courses.prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Public Transportation
courses.description: Development, operation, management, financing, evaluation, and travel demand estimation for urban public transportation systems. Legislative, political, social, and economic aspects of public transportation systems. Methodology and procedures for transit planning. Review of transit studies. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 424.
courses.prerequisite: CE 321 or CE 3321.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 321 or CE 3321.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Introduction to Railway Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to railroad and railway system analysis and design. Railroads, rail transit and high speed rail applications. Track foundation design for various conditions. Approaches to railway analysis and design and an introduction to railway traffic control and signaling. Field trip may be required. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly CE 425.
courses.prerequisite: CE 321 or CE 3321.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 321 or CE 3321.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Highway Pavement Design
courses.description: Theories, principles, and procedures in the structural design of highway pavements. Performance of flexible and rigid pavements in the field. characterization of pavement materials. Design of flexible and rigid pavements. Analysis software. Laboratory testing of pavement materials. Field trip may be required. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 429.
courses.prerequisite: CE 259 or CE 2259, and CE 381 or CE 3381; or CM 113 or CM 1113, and CM 213 or CM 2113.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CE 259 or CE 2259, and CE 381 or CE 3381; or CM 113 or CM 1113, and CM 213 or CM 2113.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Introduction to Coastal Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to Coastal Engineering, including theory and analysis of waves and tides. Wave generation, propagation, and dispersion. Wave velocities, forces, pressures, run-up and overtopping. Beach processes. Coastal protection structures. Estuary processes. Tides and tidal theory. Coastal design considerations. Sea-level rise. Field trip required. 4 lectures. Formerly CE 431.
courses.prerequisite: CE 336 or CE/ENVE 3337; MATH 244 or MATH 2341; and PHYS 143 or PHYS 1143.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 336 or CE/ENVE 3337; MATH 244 or MATH 2341; and PHYS 143 or PHYS 1143.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Coastal Engineering II
courses.description: Coastal processes that influence coastal infrastructure design. Sea-level rise, subsidence, tides, storm surge, tsunamis, wind and wave setup. Introduction to tidal currents, wind circulation, estuarine circulation and salinity intrusion, erosion and sediment transport, turbulent mixing, dispersion, energy dissipation. Harbor resonance. Field trip required. 4 lectures. Formerly CE 432.
courses.prerequisite: CE 431 or CE 4431; and STAT 312 or STAT 3210.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 431 or CE 4431; and STAT 312 or STAT 3210.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Open Channel Hydraulics
courses.description: Analysis and characteristics of flow in open channels. Critical, uniform, gradually and rapidly varied flows. Channel design, transitions and controls. Hydraulic jump and energy dissipaters. Unsteady flows, waves and wave propagation, flood routing. Software applications and numerical methods. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 433.
courses.prerequisite: CE 336 or CE/ENVE 3337.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CE 336 or CE/ENVE 3337.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Groundwater Hydraulics and Hydrology
courses.description: Fundamental equations of groundwater flow, Darcy's Law, differential equations for confined and unconfined flows. Leaky aquifers. Aquifer response to recharge, pumping and injection. Groundwater modeling. Saltwater intrusion and groundwater contamination. Sustainable groundwater management. 3 lectures. Formerly CE 434.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing, CE 336, or CE/ENVE 3337.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing, CE 336, or CE/ENVE 3337.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Engineering Hydrology and Stormwater Management
courses.description: Determining runoff peak, volume, and hydrograph for a storm event. Stormwater drainage systems for land development projects, post-construction stormwater requirements and solutions, floodplain analysis, climate/landuse change impacts on runoff and drainage infrastructure. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly CE 435.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing, CE 336, or CE/ENVE 3337.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing, CE 336, or CE/ENVE 3337.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Heavy Civil Temporary Structures and Shoring
courses.description: Design and construction of retaining walls, concrete formwork, falsework, scaffolding, ramps, platform, bracing, and guying as applied to heavy civil projects. Field trip may be required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as CE/CM 4436. Formerly CE/CM 436.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ARCE 211, ARCE 1121, CE 352 or CE 3352; and one of the following: CM 314, CM 3314, CE/CM 371, or CE 3375.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: ARCE 211, ARCE 1121, CE 352 or CE 3352; and one of the following: CM 314, CM 3314, CE/CM 371, or CE 3375.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Heavy Civil Projects and Equipment
courses.description: Heavy civil projects logistics, construction, operations, planning, management, workflow and sequencing, equipment management, fleet configuration and maintenance, equipment productivity and cost optimization, asphalt specifications. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as CE/CM 4437. Formerly CE/CM 437.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CM 314, CM 3314, CE/CM 371, or CE 3375.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: CM 314, CM 3314, CE/CM 371, or CE 3375.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Hydraulic Systems Engineering
courses.description: Water and storm water flows. Design of water distribution systems. Multiple pumps and pump systems. Water sources for municipal water supply, fire flows and storage reservoirs. Storm water management. Design of storm sewers, inlets, gutters and culverts. Best Management Practices (BMPs) and Low Impact Developments (LIDs). 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 440.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing, CE 336, or CE/ENVE 3336.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing, CE 336, or CE/ENVE 3336.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Seismic Principles for Civil Engineering
courses.description: American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE) Standard 7 seismic load provisions for buildings and other civil structures. Relevant preparation for the California Civil Seismic Principles Examination. 1 activity.
courses.prerequisite: CE 355 or CE 3355.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 355 or CE 3355.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Applied Numerical Methods in Engineering
courses.description: Scalars, vectors, and matrices in finite precision. Solution of linear and nonlinear equations. Eigensystem calculations and applications. Data representation, visualization, and processing. Interpolation and model fitting. Numerical integration and differentiation. Numerical methods for ordinary and partial differential equations. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: CE 251 or CE/ENVE 2251.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CE 251 or CE/ENVE 2251.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Design of Timber Structures
courses.description: Analysis and design of timber structures, emphasizing construction methodology and material behavior. Physical and mechanical properties of structural lumber and glued laminated timber. Lateral load paths, diaphragms, connections, shear wall design, combined load design. Construction sequencing for timber structures. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 455.
courses.prerequisite: CE 355 or CE 3355.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CE 355 or CE 3355.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Bridge Engineering
courses.description: Fundamentals of the structural analysis and design of highway bridges. Construction materials in bridges. Loads on highway bridges. Load path and distribution in bridge superstructure. Design of reinforced concrete, pre-stressed concrete, and composite bridges. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 457.
courses.prerequisite: CE 355 or CE 3355; and CE 356 or CE 4356.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 355 or CE 3355; and CE 356 or CE 4356.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: FRP Strengthening of Reinforced Concrete Structures
courses.description: Flexural and shear strengthening of reinforced concrete members using fiber-reinforced plastic (FRP) composite. Seismic upgrade and rehabilitation of columns. Design philosophy and methodology based on the current understanding of FRP strengthening techniques. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly CE 459.
courses.prerequisite: CE 355 or CE 3355.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 355 or CE 3355.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Senior Design Project I
courses.description: Work in multi-disciplinary teams to complete an integrated civil design project. Includes project-focused instruction on selected topics in construction, geotechnical, structural, transportation, and water resources engineering design. Reinforcement of team building, technical communications, and professional practice skills. 1 activity. Formerly CE 466.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; CE 465 or CE/ENVE 3465; and consent of instructor.
courses.corequisite: CE 321 or CE 3321; CE 336 or CE/ENVE 3337; CE 355 or CE 3355; CE/CM 371 or CE 3375; and CE 381 or CE 3381.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Senior standing; CE 465 or CE/ENVE 3465; and consent of instructor. Corequisite: CE 321 or CE 3321; CE 336 or CE/ENVE 3337; CE 355 or CE 3355; CE/CM 371 or CE 3375; and CE 381 or CE 3381.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Senior Design Project II
courses.description: Continuation of work on multi-disciplinary teams to complete an integrated civil design project. Formal instruction on selected topics in construction, geotechnical, structural, transportation, and water resources engineering design culminating with oral and written presentations. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 467.
courses.prerequisite: CE 466 or CE 4466.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 466 or CE 4466.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. 1 to 4 lectures. Formerly CE 470.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Special Advanced Laboratory
courses.description: Directed group laboratory study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. 1 to 4 laboratories. Formerly CE 471.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Environmental Compliance and Permitting
courses.description: Fundamentals of State and Federal environmental review processes and regulations essential to permitting Civil Engineering projects. Permit compliance through post-construction. Consideration of broader impacts including climate change and environmental justice. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 1 lecture, 1 activity. Formerly CE 474.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; and one of the following: CE 336, CE/ENVE 3337, CE 465, CE/ENVE 3465, CM 314, or CM 3314.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Senior standing; and one of the following: CE 336, CE/ENVE 3337, CE 465, CE/ENVE 3465, CM 314, or CM 3314.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Mechanical, Electrical, and Energy Systems in Buildings
courses.description: Mechanical and electrical systems that operate in the background of modern buildings, with a focus on energy performance. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ARCE/CE 475.
courses.prerequisite: CE 336 or CE/ENVE 3336.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CE 336 or CE/ENVE 3336.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Foundation Design and Construction
courses.description: Analysis and design of shallow and deep foundation systems for vertical, lateral, and combined loading. Bearing capacity, settlement, and earth pressure. Foundation type selection. Construction methods, field monitoring, and load-testing. Structural design considerations. Computer-aided analysis. 4 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382; or CE 3381.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382; or CE 3381.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Earth Fills and Embankments
courses.description: Design and construction of structural fill, embankments, abutments, earth dams, and levees. Design and performance of compacted fill. Slope stability and settlement. Seepage analysis. Filter design and criteria. Computer-aided analysis. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382; or CE 3381.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382; or CE 3381.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Geotechnical Testing and Modeling
courses.description: Advanced soils testing and modeling for saturated flow, volume change, and shear strength. Cyclic loading of soils. Experiment design. Numerical methods and computational tools for geotechnical analysis, design, and visualization. 1 lecture, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382; or CE 3381.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382; or CE 3381.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Earth Retention, Excavations, and Tunnels
courses.description: Earth pressure theory and lateral earth pressure calculations. Analysis, design, and construction of earth retention systems, ground anchors, mechanically-stabilized earth, excavations, and soft ground tunnels. Dewatering methods and soil improvement. Computer-aided analysis. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382; or CE 3381.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382; or CE 3381.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Introduction to Geological Engineering
courses.description: Evaluation of the engineering properties of rocks. Consideration of geomorphic mechanisms as they pertain to civil infrastructure and the built environment. Civil engineering analysis and design related to rock foundations, rock slopes, rock tunneling, rockfall hazard, coastal bluffs. Field trip may be required. 4 lectures. Formerly CE 486.
courses.prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382, or CE 3381; and GEOL 201 or GEOL 2240.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382, or CE 3381; and GEOL 201 or GEOL 2240.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Cooperative Education Experience
courses.description: Work experience in business, industry, government, and other areas of student career interest related to civil engineering. Paid position; typically requires relocation for at least one semester. Registration in course, a formal scope of work, and evaluation by supervisor required. Credit/No Credit grading only. Repeatable up to 24 units. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 4495. Formerly CE 495.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Engineering Risk Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to the basic concepts of probability theory, statistics, and decision theory as they pertain to problems in civil and environmental engineering. Emphasis placed on the use of probabilistic modeling, Bayesian statistics, risk analysis, and decision theory. 4 lectures. Crosslisted as ARCE/CE 5488. Formerly CE 488.
courses.prerequisite: STAT 312, STAT 3210, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: STAT 312, STAT 3210, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Individual Study
courses.description: Advanced study planned and completed under the direction of a member of the department faculty. Open only to graduate students who have demonstrated ability to do independent work. Repeatable up to 4 units. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 5500. Formerly ENVE 500.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of department chair.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Finite Element Analysis of Structures
courses.description: Stiffness and flexibility procedures for the analysis of one, two, and three-dimensional line elements under both static and dynamics loading conditions. Development of algorithms and programs for use in the analysis of structural frameworks. Discussion of modeling issues and limitations. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 501.
courses.prerequisite: CE 407 or CE 4407, and CE 4451; or Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CE 407 or CE 4407, and CE 4451; or Graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Finite Element Analysis of Continua
courses.description: Finite element theory and application with a focus on numerical implementation. Strong and weak forms, variational theorems, displacement based methods, mixed methods, viscoelasticity and plasticity type formulations, augmented Lagrangian formulations, transient and modal analysis, and finite deformation. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as AERO/BMED/CE/ME 5504. Formerly CE/ME 504.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BMED/CE/ME 404, BMED/CE/ME 4404, CE 501, CE 5502, AERO 431, or AERO 4431.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: BMED/CE/ME 404, BMED/CE/ME 4404, CE 501, CE 5502, AERO 431, or AERO 4431.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Continuum Mechanics and Elasticity
courses.description: Introduction to continuum mechanics. Kinematics, stress, and balance laws. Constitutive theory for isotropic and anisotropic solids and viscous fluids. Applications including design of beams and pressure vessels, stress concentrations, fiber-reinforced composites, and non-homogeneous biological materials. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as CE 5511/ME 5501. Formerly CE 511/ME 501.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Inelastic Stress Analysis
courses.description: Perfectly plastic and work hardening materials. Von Mises and Tresca yield, isotropic and kinematic hardening flow rules, and boundary-value problems. Finite elasticity, including kinematics, Cauchy- and Green-elasticity, invariance, constraints, Neo-Hookean and Mooney-Rivlin materials, experimental approaches, anisotropic and fiber reinforced materials, boundary-value problems, stability and strain energy convexity, and viscoelasticity. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as CE 5513/ME 5503. Formerly CE 513/ME 503.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CE 511, CE 5511, ME 501, or ME 5501.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: CE 511, CE 5511, ME 501, or ME 5501.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Transportation Systems Planning
courses.description: Planning of regional multimodal transportation systems. Modeling of transportation networks and travel demand. Travel survey design. Urban data systems. Evaluation of alternatives based on economic, social, technological, and other factors. 2 lectures, 2 activities. Formerly CE 523.
courses.prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Airport Planning and Design
courses.description: Historical background of aviation and airport development. Financing and estimating demand. Aircraft characteristics, airport capacity, airspace and air traffic control. Site selection, airport configuration, geometric design of landing area, planning and development of terminal areas, lighting, pavement design, and drainage. Field trip required. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 525.
courses.prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Transportation Safety
courses.description: Nature and extent of transportation safety problems worldwide and in the US. Road safety, human factors, vehicle safety; crash data collection and management; safety planning and audits; safe systems approach; transportation crash studies; predictive model building; "before-after" studies; countermeasure design. Field trip required. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 526.
courses.prerequisite: CE 321 or CE 3321, and STAT 312 or STAT 3210; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 321 or CE 3321, and STAT 312 or STAT 3210; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Sustainable Mobility
courses.description: Analysis and design for sustainable mobility from an interdisciplinary perspective, including pedestrians, bicyclists, electrification, technologies, and transit. Addresses economy, climate change, environment, and equity issues. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 527.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CE 321 or CE 3321, CRP 435 or CRP 4435, or graduate standing.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: One of the following: CE 321 or CE 3321, CRP 435 or CRP 4435, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Transportation Economics and Analysis
courses.description: Principles of engineering systems analysis and applications to transportation using examples from different modes. Identification of transportation benefits, costs, user and non-user impacts, transportation cost models, pricing, and optimization. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 528.
courses.prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Modeling and Simulation in Transportation
courses.description: Theory and operation of transportation systems, the systems approach, simulation techniques. Use of available software packages. Simulation model development, calibration and use. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 2 activities. Formerly CE 529.
courses.prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 321, CE 3321, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Sustainable Urban Stormwater Management
courses.description: Green stormwater infrastructure including low impact developments, green streets, and regional multi-benefit projects. Hydromodification, erosion and sedimentation. Evaluating benefits of green infrastructure for water quality, flood control, and drought management. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly CE 533.
courses.prerequisite: CE 336, CE/ENVE 3337, or graduate standing.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: CE 336, CE/ENVE 3337, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Water Resources Systems Planning and Management
courses.description: Systems approach to the planning, management, and operation of water resources projects and infrastructure. Application of optimization, simulation, and statistical methods to solving multi-objective and multicriteria water resources projects. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly CE 535.
courses.prerequisite: CE 337, CE/ENVE 3337, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 337, CE/ENVE 3337, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Advanced Modeling in Water Resources
courses.description: Modeling and analysis of water resources systems. Applications of computer models, Geographic Information Systems, remote sensing, and data analytics to the planning and management of water infrastructure. Broader considerations of water resources systems including climate change impacts and social justice. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 536.
courses.prerequisite: CE 433 or CE 4433, and CE 435 or CE 4435; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 433 or CE 4433, and CE 435 or CE 4435; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Groundwater Contamination
courses.description: Sources and types of groundwater contamination. Contaminant fate and transport mechanisms. Prediction of contaminant transport and transformation in groundwater using analytical and numerical models. Design of engineered containment and remediation systems to mitigate groundwater pollution. Environmental justice considerations. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly CE 537.
courses.prerequisite: CE 434, CE 4434, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CE 434, CE 4434, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Urban Water Systems
courses.description: Urban Hydrology; Relationships between surface and groundwater elements of water sources and disposal. Urban Hydraulics; Integration of water delivery, wastewater collection, drainage systems, and associated treatment components in urbanizing areas. Best management practices (BMPs) and low impact developments (LIDs); Sustainable infrastructure. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 538.
courses.prerequisite: CE 440 or CE 4440.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 440 or CE 4440.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Environmental Hydraulics
courses.description: Application of fluid mechanics principles to environmental flows. Emphasis on advection, dispersion, stratification and mixing effects. Stratified flows, turbulent jets and plumes, wastewater and thermal diffusers, cooling ponds and channels, control of environmental problems. 4 lectures. Formerly CE 539.
courses.prerequisite: CE 336, CE/ENVE 3337, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 336, CE/ENVE 3337, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Extreme Events and Climate Change in Water Resources
courses.description: Physics and statistics behind risk and hazard assessment in water resources. Exceedance probabilities; hazard assessments; return periods; intensity-duration-frequency curves. Effects of climate change, including land use and hydrology changes, sea-level rise and subsidence, altered rainfall intensity. Coastal and inland hazards. 4 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: CE 251 or CE/ENVE 2251 and STAT 312 or STAT 3210; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 251 or CE/ENVE 2251 and STAT 312 or STAT 3210; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Ductile Design of Steel Structures
courses.description: American National Standards Institute/ American Institute of Steel Construction (ANSI/AISC) 341 seismic provisions for typical lateral force resisting systems in structural steel buildings, including moment frames, concentrically braced frames, and eccentrically braced frames. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 553.
courses.prerequisite: CE 356, CE 4356, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 356, CE 4356, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Fiber Reinforced Polymer (FRP) Composites in Structural Engineering
courses.description: Strengthening/rehabilitation of reinforced concrete (RC) members using Fiber-Reinforced Plastic (FRP) composite. Seismic upgrade and rehabilitation of columns. Design of new RC structures with FRP rebars. Based on current research and applications. Not open to students with credit in CE 459 or CE 4459. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 556.
courses.prerequisite: CE 355, CE 3355, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 355, CE 3355, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Seismic Analysis and Design
courses.description: General procedures of seismic analysis and design of civil structures. Underlying principles of seismic hazards analysis, structural dynamics, and inelastic structural behavior. Integration of course topics into building codes. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 557.
courses.prerequisite: CE 407, CE 4407, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 407, CE 4407, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Structural Health Monitoring
courses.description: Introduction of structural health monitoring for assessing conditions of various critical structures. Introduction of sensor instrumentation, working mechanism, and performance characteristics. Analysis of sensor signals to extract features of structural performance. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: CE 407, CE 4407, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CE 407, CE 4407, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Prestressed Concrete Design
courses.description: Principals of behavior, analysis, and design of prestressed concrete elements and structures. Determinate precast pre-tensioned concrete components for buildings and highway construction. Indeterminate post-tensioned concrete building structures. Prestressing losses. 4 lectures. Formerly CE 559.
courses.prerequisite: CE 355, CE 3355, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 355, CE 3355, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. 1 to 4 seminars. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 5570. Formerly CE 570.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Special Advanced Laboratory
courses.description: Directed group laboratory study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. 1 to 4 laboratories. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 5571. Formerly CE 571.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Engineering Project Management
courses.description: Principles and techniques of managing projects from conceptual phase through project definition, design, construction, and closeout. Project management with aspects of scope definition, estimates and budgeting, monitoring and control, design coordination, construction phases, risks, quality, procurement, and leadership. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 572.
courses.prerequisite: Senior or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Senior or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Advanced Geotechnical Engineering
courses.description: Advanced field and laboratory tests for shear strength and volume change. Collection and interpretation of test data for analysis and design. Site characterization through geotechnical testing. Geotechnical engineering report preparation. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CE 581.
courses.prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382, or CE 3381; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 381 and CE 382, or CE 3381; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Geotechnical Earthquake Engineering
courses.description: Ground motion topics; tectonics, seismology, seismic hazard analysis, dynamic behavior of soils, seismic site response, and soil structure interaction. Ground failure topics; surface fault rupture, soil liquefaction, lateral spreading, cyclic failure, seismic compression, and seismic slope stability. 4 lectures. Formerly CE 583.
courses.prerequisite: CE 4481 or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 4481 or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Landslides and Slope Stabilization
courses.description: Geotechnical and geological investigations for landslides and slope instability. Computer-aided slope stability analysis methods. Back-analysis of existing landslides. Field instrumentation. Methods for slope stabilization and reconstruction. Influence of groundwater and earthquakes. Field trip required. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: CE 381, CE 3381, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 381, CE 3381, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Geoenvironmental Engineering
courses.description: Principles for containment applications. Engineering properties of soils and geosynthetics and their interaction with contaminants and wastes. Liners. Covers. Leachate and gas collection systems. Contaminant transport. Monitoring systems. Beneficial reuse of wastes and byproducts. 3 lectures. Formerly CE 587.
courses.prerequisite: CE 381, CE 3381, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CE 381, CE 3381, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Ground Improvement
courses.description: Ground improvement applications for modification of geomechanical and hydraulic properties of soils. Engineering properties of soft and problematic ground. Mechanical, chemical, and thermal stabilization for geotechnical applications. Soil reinforcement, geosynthetics, soil inclusions, grouting, drainage, containment, slurry walls, blasting, sustainability. 4 lectures. Formerly CE 588.
courses.prerequisite: CE 381, CE 3381, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 381, CE 3381, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Geosynthetics Engineering
courses.description: Geosynthetics applications within civil engineering. Design content for geotechnical, geoenvironmental, and transportation applications. Manufacturing processes, material properties, interaction with soils, construction, and service conditions. Separation, reinforcement, drainage, filtration, and barrier applications. 4 lectures. Formerly CE 589.
courses.prerequisite: CE 381, CE 3381, or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 381, CE 3381, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Graduate Seminar I
courses.description: Preparation for conducting independent research or graduate-level independent projects in the field of civil and environmental engineering. Development of graduate-level written and oral communication skills. Research skills. Professional ethics. Career pathways. 1 seminar. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 5591. Formerly CE 591.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Graduate Seminar II
courses.description: Preparation for advanced graduate studies and post-graduate engineering careers. Development of oral and written communication skills to a professional level. Presentation of research and/or project work to peers. 1 seminar. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 5592. Formerly CE 592.
courses.prerequisite: CE 591 or CE/ENVE 5591.
courses.corequisite: One of the following: CE 596, CE/ENVE 5597, CE/ENVE 599, or CE/ENVE 5599.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CE 591 or CE/ENVE 5591. Corequisite: One of the following: CE 596, CE/ENVE 5597, CE/ENVE 599, or CE/ENVE 5599.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Cooperative Education Experience
courses.description: Work experience in business, industry, government, and other areas of student career interest. Positions are paid and usually require relocation for at least one term. Registration in course and a formal scope of work and evaluation by work supervisor required. Credit/No Credit grading only. Crosslisted as CE/ENVE 5595. Formerly CE 595.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Comprehensive Examination
courses.description: Comprehensive exam for a non-thesis master's student in civil engineering showing integration of technical knowledge, critical and independent thinking, and mastery of the subject matter. Scheduled with the faculty advisor, typically in the final semester of the graduate program. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly CE 596.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing; and CE 591 or CE/ENVE 5591.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Graduate standing; and CE 591 or CE/ENVE 5591.

courses.subject: CE
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: Under direction of an advisor, student conducts graduate-level research relevant to their field of study. Research efforts culminate in a written report/thesis and oral defense of the study. Repeatable up to 6 units. Formerly CE 599.
courses.corequisite: Graduate standing; and CE 591 or CE/ENVE 5591.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Corequisite: Graduate standing; and CE 591 or CE/ENVE 5591.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Introduction to the Chemical Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the chemistry and biochemistry disciplines. Orientation, advising, career opportunities, and introduction to the faculty. Designed for first-year biochemistry and chemistry majors. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 lecture. Formerly CHEM 101.
courses.prerequisite: Biochemistry or Chemistry major.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: Biochemistry or Chemistry major.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Research Methods I
courses.description: Introduction to experimental and computational methods for laboratory research in the chemical sciences including experimental design, procedure optimization, data evaluation, and presentation of results. Designed for first-year biochemistry and chemistry majors. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CHEM 124, CHEM 125, CHEM 1120, or CHEM 1122.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: One of the following: CHEM 124, CHEM 125, CHEM 1120, or CHEM 1122.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: World of Chemistry
courses.description: The fundamentals of chemical cause/effect and structure/function relationships. The basic principles of chemistry and their applications to solving human problems in areas such as toxicology, environmental science, agriculture, nutrition, forensics, and medicine. Not open for major credit in Biochemistry or Chemistry. Not open to students with credit in CHEM 111, CHEM 124, CHEM 125, CHEM 127, CHEM 1120, or CHEM 1122. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Areas 5A and 5C (GE Areas B1 and B3 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs. Formerly CHEM 110.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 115, MATH 1000, or appropriate Math Placement Level.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 5A 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 5C 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area B1 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area B3

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemistry in Context
courses.description: Exploration of fundamental chemical principles relevant to engineering applications. Atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, acid-base and redox reactions, kinetics, thermodynamics, chemical equilibrium, and electrochemistry. Role of chemistry in energy production, materials science, agriculture, and environmental technology. Not open for major credit in Biochemistry or Chemistry. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 5A (GE Area B1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 5A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area B1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 5A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area B1

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Chemical Structure and Properties
courses.description: Atomic theory, chemical reactions, bonding, stoichiometry, nomenclature, molecular structure, and intermolecular forces. Theoretical concepts and experimental methods for distinguishing kinds of substances, determining the structure of substances, predicting properties of substances based on their underlying structure, and quantifying chemical processes. Not open to students with credit in CHEM 124 or CHEM 127. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Areas 5A and 5C (GE Areas B1 and B3 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 5A 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 5C 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area B1 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area B3
