courses.description: Introduction to fundamentals of Human-Computer Interaction. Discussion of human cognitive and affective factors and computer capabilities and constraints. courses.prerequisite: CSC 307 or CSC 308 or CSC 3100.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CSC 307 or CSC 308 or CSC 3100.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Software Security
courses.description: Principles behind secure software design including threat models, trust management, common vulnerabilities and mitigation techniques, robust software development, isolation of untrusted code, auditability, and testing. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly CSC 424.
courses.prerequisite: CSC 307 or CSC 308 or CSC 3100; and CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CSC 307 or CSC 308 or CSC 3100; and CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Malware Design and Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of malware design and analysis with a focus on static and dynamic analysis of live samples. Ethical consideration, environment preparation, static analysis, dynamic analysis, and payload engineering. 2 lectures, 1 activity.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201; and PHIL 323 or PHIL 3323.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201; and PHIL 323 or PHIL 3323.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Binary Exploitation: Tools and Techniques
courses.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of finding vulnerabilities in production systems with a focus on the evolution of vulnerabilities over time. Emphasis on buffer overflows, return-oriented-programming attacks, return to libc attacks, heap attacks, and common binary exploitation tools. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly CSC 421.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201. Corequisite: PHIL 323 or PHIL 3323.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Web and Cloud Security
courses.description: Survey of web and cloud security, including browser, cloud, and container vulnerabilities and their prevention. Various web-related attacks and their defenses. Case studies on real-world incidents; legal and ethical implications; and emerging web and cloud security threats. 2 lectures, 1 activity.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Privacy and Security Capstone I
courses.description: Interdisciplinary security and privacy engineering with a customer. Design and implementation of a penetration testing plan with consideration of ethics, usability, and cost. Documentation, presentation, and communications to customers. Focus on managing security teams. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as CPE/CSC 4260.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; one of the following: CSC 320, CPE/CSC 321, CPE/CSC 3201, or CSC 3200; and PHIL 323 or PHIL 3323.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Senior standing; one of the following: CSC 320, CPE/CSC 321, CPE/CSC 3201, or CSC 3200; and PHIL 323 or PHIL 3323.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Senior Project - Privacy and Security Capstone II
courses.description: Interdisciplinary testing, analysis, and construction of a secure solution including analysis of the ethical, policy, and usability implications. Focus on effective documentation and communication with various customers and stakeholders. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as CPE/CSC 4261.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 4260.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 4260.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics in Computer Security
courses.description: Special topics in emerging areas of computer security. Potential topics include: network and web security, critical infrastructure protection, embedded systems security, malware analysis, mobile security, and digital forensics, among others. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 1 to 4 lectures. Formerly CSC 429.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201 and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201 and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Seminars in Privacy and Security
courses.description: Faculty supervised readings and discussion on a defined area in privacy and/or security. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 1 seminar.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201; and PHIL 323 or PHIL 3323.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201; and PHIL 323 or PHIL 3323.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Research Experience in Privacy and Security
courses.description: Collaborative research activity under faculty supervision on a defined problem in privacy and/or security. Literature review, prototype development, analysis, documentation. Repeatable up to 4 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 1 to 2 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201; and PHIL 323 or PHIL 3323.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201; and PHIL 323 or PHIL 3323.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Projects in Privacy and Security
courses.description: Instructor guided investigation into advanced design and applications of privacy and computer security. Projects selected from real-world privacy and security problems. Focus on testing, analysis, implementation, and team-based projects. Repeatable up to 4 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 1 to 2 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 321 or CPE/CSC 3201.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Compiler Construction
courses.description: Design and construction of compilers. Concepts include syntactic analysis, semantics, code generation, and code transformations. Examine problems in processing languages. A complete compiler for a small language will be implemented. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Crosslisted as CPE/CSC 4310. Formerly CPE/CSC 431.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 357 or CPE/CSC 2050; and CPE/CSC 225, CPE/EE 233, or CPE 2300.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 357 or CPE/CSC 2050; and CPE/CSC 225, CPE/EE 233, or CPE 2300.

courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.description: Interactive art theory for developing innovative projects, applications, and installations. Definition and specification of a team-based creative collaboration on a digital interactive art project (animation, video game, interactive media display, etc.). Project planning, design, and prototype creation. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 1 lecture, 2 activities. Crosslisted as ART/CSC 4431. Formerly ART/CSC 350.

courses.recommended: CSC 371 or CSC 3710; and ART 376 or ART 4433.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ART 384 or ART 3332. Recommended: CSC 371 or CSC 3710; and ART 376 or ART 4433.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Computing for Interactive Arts Capstone II
courses.description: Team-based design, construction, and deployment of a collaborative interactive computational art project typically found in the fields of animation, game design, and interactive media. Management of interdisciplinary teams, documentation, creative development, testing, and assessment. Ethical considerations in interactive art. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 1 lecture, 2 activities. Crosslisted as ART/CSC 4432. Formerly ART/CSC 450.
courses.prerequisite: ART/CSC 350 or ART/CSC 4431.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ART/CSC 350 or ART/CSC 4431.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Bioinformatics Algorithms
courses.description: Introduction to the use of computers to solve problems in molecular biology. The algorithms, languages, and databases important in determining and analyzing nucleic and protein sequences and their structure. 4 lectures. Formerly CSC 448.
courses.prerequisite: CSC 349 or CSC 3449.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CSC 349 or CSC 3449.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Introduction to Operating Systems
courses.description: Sequential and multiprogramming operating systems; system calls, scheduling, synchronization, files and storage systems, virtual memory, security. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Crosslisted as CPE/CSC 4553. Formerly CPE/CSC 453.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Implementation of Operating Systems
courses.description: Design and implementation of multiprogramming kernels, systems programming methodology, interprocess communications, synchronization, and device drivers. 4 lectures. Formerly CPE/CSC 454.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 453 or CPE/CSC 4553.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 453 or CPE/CSC 4553.

courses.title: Special Advanced Topics in Computer Systems
courses.description: Special aspects of design, implementation, and analysis of networks, advanced operating, and distributed systems. Topics may include process management, virtual memory, process communication, context switching, file system designs, persistent objects, process and data migration, load balancing, security, and networks. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. 1 to 4 lectures. Crosslisted as CPE/CSC 4570. Formerly CPE/CSC 458.

courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 357 or CPE/CSC 2050; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Fundamentals of Machine Learning
courses.description: Theory and practice of Machine Learning, with focus on optimization-based methods and procedures. Likelihood and least-squares estimation. Linear, nonlinear, and penalized regression. Classification by linear separators. Gradient descent and boosting. Unsupervised and semi-supervised learning. Not open to students with credit in CSC 487 or CSC 4667. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as CSC/DATA 4610.
courses.prerequisite: DATA 301 or DATA 3301; and MATH 253 or MATH 2621; or graduate standing in Statistics.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: DATA 301 or DATA 3301; and MATH 253 or MATH 2621; or graduate standing in Statistics.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Foundations and Applications of Deep Learning
courses.description: Overview of modern machine learning techniques that relate to deep learning. Perceptrons, Feed-Forward Neural Networks, Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks, Autoencoders and Decoders, Generative Adversarial Networks, and Transformers. Not open to students with credit in CSC 487 or CSC 4667. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as CSC/DATA 4620.
courses.prerequisite: DATA 4610.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: DATA 4610.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Database Management Systems Organization
courses.description: Architecture of the internals of a modern Database Management System (DBMS). Physical data layout, query execution and optimization, transaction management, logging and recovery, data replication and scalability, and an introduction to distributed DBMSs. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CSC 468.
courses.prerequisite: CSC 365, CSC 3665, or CSC 3660.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CSC 365, CSC 3665, or CSC 3660.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Deep Learning
courses.description: Theory and practice of Deep Learning (DL) paradigms. Gradient Descent, Batch Normalization, Convolutional Neural Networks (NN), Recurrent NN, Dropout, Transformers, and new developments. Emphasis on using DL to solve a real-world application of significant scope. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CSC 487.
courses.prerequisite: DATA 301 or DATA 3301; and one of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: DATA 301 or DATA 3301; and one of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341. Recommended: CSC/DATA 4610, CSC 480, or CSC 4880.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Distributed Systems
courses.description: Foundations in distributed computing. Distributed programming languages. Distributed algorithms. Leader election consensus protocols. Failure detection with gossip protocol. Fault tolerance and replication. Consistency protocols. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as CPE/CSC 4669. Formerly CPE/CSC 469.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 357 or CPE/CSC 2050.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 357 or CPE/CSC 2050.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
courses.description: Graphics software development and use of application programming interfaces for 3D graphics. The graphics pipeline, modeling, geometric and viewing transforms, lighting and shading, rendering, interaction techniques and graphics hardware. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CPE/CSC 471.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 357 or CPE/CSC 2050.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 357 or CPE/CSC 2050.

courses.subject: CSC
courses.title: Advanced Rendering Techniques
courses.description: Computer graphics rendering algorithms. Ray tracing, geometry, tessellation, acceleration structures, sampling, filtering, shading models, and advanced concepts such as global illumination and programmable graphics hardware. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly CSC 473.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 471 or CSC 4710.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 471 or CSC 4710.

courses.title: Computer Animation

Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CSC 474.
courses.prerequisite: CPE/CSC 471 or CSC 4710.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: CPE/CSC 471 or CSC 4710.

courses.title: Real-Time 3D Computer Graphics Software

Real-time rendering and shading, visibility processing, level-of-detail, texture and light maps. Collision detection, bounding volumes, and complexity management. Interactive controls, multi-player game technology, and game engine architecture. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly CPE/CSC 476.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Special Problems for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of special problems. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly DSCI 400.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Physical and Chemical Properties of Dairy Products
courses.description: Composition, structure and properties of milk and milk products. Physical and chemical changes that occur during processing and storage of dairy products. Objective measurement of chemical and physical properties. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly DSCI 401.
courses.prerequisite: CHEM 124, CHEM 127, CHEM 1120, or graduate standing.
courses.recommended: CHEM 312 or CHEM 2240; and CHEM 314 or CHEM 3350.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CHEM 124, CHEM 127, CHEM 1120, or graduate standing. Recommended: CHEM 312 or CHEM 2240; and CHEM 314 or CHEM 3350.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Quality Assurance and Control of Dairy Products
courses.description: Current methods used to evaluate dairy products with respect to production plant economics and consumer safety. Design and interpretation of Hazard Analysis Critical Control Points (HACCP), environmental monitoring, allergen control, and food defense programs for ensuring product quality and safety. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly DSCI 402.
courses.prerequisite: STAT 218, STAT 1110, or graduate standing.
courses.recommended: One of the following: DSCI 444, DSCI 3344, MCRO 421, or MCRO 4421.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: STAT 218, STAT 1110, or graduate standing. Recommended: One of the following: DSCI 444, DSCI 3344, MCRO 421, or MCRO 4421.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Dairy Nutrition
courses.description: Nutrient metabolism and diet formulation technologies for all classes of dairy cattle; whole-farm feed management; physiological and nutritional aspects of predominant metabolic disorders; on-farm auditing and troubleshooting of nutritional management. Field trip may be required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly DSCI 410.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 355 or ASCI 3355; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ASCI 355 or ASCI 3355; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Dairy Farm Consultation
courses.description: Student consultation teams visit dairies and attend management training seminars followed by presenting management recommendations to the dairy owners, consultants, and other industry leaders. Field trip required. 1 seminar and supervised work. Formerly DSCI 412.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Corequisite: DSCI 432 or DSCI 4432.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Breeding and Genetics of Dairy Cattle
courses.description: Evaluation of inherited characteristics in dairy cattle, including principles of inheritance and genomic evaluations. Proving and selecting sires and dams, dairy genetic evaluations. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly DSCI 422.
courses.prerequisite: ASCI 302 or ASCI 3302.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ASCI 302 or ASCI 3302.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Advanced Dairy Herd Management
courses.description: Instruction and lab experience in key areas of dairy farm management including records analysis, cattle health, heifer development, milk production and quality, facilities, safety, and financials. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly DSCI 432.
courses.prerequisite: DSCI 230 or DSCI 2230.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: DSCI 230 or DSCI 2230.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly DSCI 470.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Special Advanced Laboratory
courses.description: Directed group laboratory study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 laboratories. Formerly DSCI 471.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Individual Study
courses.description: Advanced independent study planned and completed under the direction of a member of the Dairy Science faculty. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly DSCI 500.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of department head.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of department head.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 9 units. 1 to 3 seminars. Formerly DSCI 570.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: DSCI
courses.title: Special Advanced Laboratory
courses.description: Directed group laboratory study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 laboratories. Formerly DSCI 571.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Survey of Economics
courses.description: Basic principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics. Emphasis on applications to current local, national and global economic issues. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as ECON/HNRS 2001. Fulfills GE Area 4B (GE Area D2 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ECON/HNRS 201.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 4B 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area D2
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 4B 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area D2

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Using Big Data to Solve Economic and Social Problems
courses.description: Introduction to basic methods in empirical economic analysis, including regression, causal inference, and machine learning. Applications of the methods to equality of opportunity, education, racial disparities, innovation and entrepreneurship, health care, climate change, criminal justice, and tax policy. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 202.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Microeconomics
courses.description: Microeconomic principles. Marginal and equilibrium analysis of commodity and factor markets in determination of price and output. Normative issues of efficiency and equity. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 221.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Macroeconomics
courses.description: Introduction to macroeconomics including aggregate output, employment, inflation, and economic growth. Money and the monetary system. Macroeconomic policy including fiscal and monetary policy. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 4B (GE Area D2 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ECON 222.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 4B 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area D2
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 4B 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area D2

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Programming for Economics and Analytics
courses.description: Basic principles of algorithmic problem solving and computer programming for economics and business analytics applications. Functions, classes, iteration, recursion, and data structures. Testing and debugging. Design of algorithms and algorithmic complexity. Stochastic programs. Graph optimization and economic applications. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 395.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Programming for Economics and Analytics Project
courses.description: Completion of class project under faculty supervision that complements the coursework on programming for economics and analytics. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Corequisite: ECON 3015.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Econometrics
courses.description: Statistical methods applied to economic data to analyze relationships among variables, test economic theories, and predict outcomes. 4 lectures. Formerly ECON 339.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 221 or ECON 2030 and ECON 222 or ECON 2040, or ECON 201 or ECON 2001; and one of the following: MATH 121, MATH 141, MATH 221, MATH 1261, MATH 1264, or MATH 1267; and one of the following: STAT 252, STAT 301, STAT 1510, or STAT 1220.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ECON 221 or ECON 2030 and ECON 222 or ECON 2040, or ECON 201 or ECON 2001; and one of the following: MATH 121, MATH 141, MATH 221, MATH 1261, MATH 1264, or MATH 1267; and one of the following: STAT 252, STAT 301, STAT 1510, or STAT 1220.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
courses.description: Consumer behavior and the theory of demand. Production, cost, supply functions, perfect competition, monopoly and oligopoly, game theory, information economics, and factor markets. 4 lectures. Formerly ECON 311.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 201, ECON 221, ECON 2001, or ECON 2030; and one of the following: MATH 121, MATH 141, MATH 1261, or DATA/MATH 1264.
courses.corequisite: One of the following: MATH 123, MATH 241, DATA/MATH 1265, or MATH 2263.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 201, ECON 221, ECON 2001, or ECON 2030; and one of the following: MATH 121, MATH 141, MATH 1261, or DATA/MATH 1264. Corequisite: One of the following: MATH 123, MATH 241, DATA/MATH 1265, or MATH 2263.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Microeconomics for Business and Public Policy
courses.description: Consumer behavior and the theory of demand. Production, cost, supply functions, perfect competition, monopoly and oligopoly, information technology, externalities, and public goods. Not open to students with credit in ECON 311 or ECON 3030. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 201, ECON 221, ECON 2001, or ECON 2030; and one of the following: MATH 121, MATH 141, MATH 221, MATH 1261, DATA/MATH 1264, or MATH 1267.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 201, ECON 221, ECON 2001, or ECON 2030; and one of the following: MATH 121, MATH 141, MATH 221, MATH 1261, DATA/MATH 1264, or MATH 1267.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
courses.description: Study of the macroeconomy, macroeconomic theories, and macroeconomic policies. Nature of growth. Business cycles. Money and inflation. Fiscal policy. Monetary policy. Financial crises. 4 lectures. Formerly ECON 313.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 201, ECON 222, ECON 2001, or ECON 2040.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 201, ECON 222, ECON 2001, or ECON 2040. Corequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Money, Banking and Credit
courses.description: Financial markets and institutions. Structure of the banking industry and impacts of technological change in banking. Structure and operations of the Federal Reserve. Impacts of monetary policy on the economy. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 337.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 201, ECON 222, ECON 2040, or ECON 2001.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 201, ECON 222, ECON 2040, or ECON 2001.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: The Economics of Equity and Social Welfare
courses.description: Distributive justice and fairness in resource allocation. Welfare properties of exchange and production economies. Welfare properties of economies with externalities and public goods. The measurement of well-being and inequality. Economic inequality, common pool resources, and climate change. 4 lectures. Formerly ECON 312.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: International Trade Theory
courses.description: Theory of comparative advantage, gains from trade, and recent developments in trade theory. Examination of tariffs, quotas, exchange controls, other trade barriers and underlying policy issues. Review of U.S. commercial policy, General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), the common market, regional and world economic organizations. Not open to students with credit in ECON 404 or ECON 4061. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 330.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 221 or ECON 2030 and ECON 222 or ECON 2040; or ECON 201 or ECON 2001.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ECON 221 or ECON 2030 and ECON 222 or ECON 2040; or ECON 201 or ECON 2001.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Environmental and Natural Resource Economics
courses.description: Economics of environmental resource management. Conservation, sustainability, and dynamic efficiency in natural resources. Effects of property rights and economic incentives on environmental and economic systems. Design of local and global environmental policies to align market outcomes with social welfare goals. Not open to students with credit in ECON 4062, ECON 431, or ECON 4071. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and ECON 201 or ECON 2001, or ECON 221 or ECON 2030 and ECON 222 or ECON 2040.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 4 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area D
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 4 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area D Prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and ECON 201 or ECON 2001, or ECON 221 or ECON 2030 and ECON 222 or ECON 2040.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Comparative Economic Systems
courses.description: Exploration of economic systems as frameworks for decision-making in production, distribution, and consumption. Examination of how different systems-market-based, government-controlled, and mixed-affect income distribution, resource allocation, and overall economic well-being. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ECON 304.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: ECON 201, ECON 222, ECON 2001, or ECON 2040.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 4 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area D
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 4 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area D Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: ECON 201, ECON 222, ECON 2001, or ECON 2040.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Mathematical Economics
courses.description: Mathematical techniques employed in microeconomic and macroeconomic theory, with applications to specific economic models in a variety of economic fields. Use of multivariate calculus and linear algebra in formulating economic models. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 408.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Mathematical Economics Project
courses.description: Use of mathematical techniques employed in microeconomic and macroeconomic theory. Application of mathematical techniques to study economic problems. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4010.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Optimization in Julia for Economics and Data Science
courses.description: Optimization as a foundation for Economics and Data Science, using the Julia environment. Constrained and unconstrained least squares via QR factorization. Duality. Applications to game theory, resource allocation, econometrics, and machine learning. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as DATA/ECON 4011.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 395, CSC 101, CSC 231, CSC 232, ECON 3015, CSC 1001, CSC 1031 or CSC 1032.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 395, CSC 101, CSC 231, CSC 232, ECON 3015, CSC 1001, CSC 1031 or CSC 1032.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Julia for Data Analysis Project
courses.description: Completion of coding exercises for data analysis in Julia under faculty supervision that complements the coursework on optimization in Julia for economics and data science. Course offered online only. 1 activity. Crosslisted as DATA/ECON 4011A.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4011.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Probability Models for Economic Decisions
courses.description: Decision making in complex, realistic situations. Simulating discrete and continuous, independent and correlated, random variables. Decision making under risk and uncertainty. Adverse selection, moral hazard, and risk sharing. Dynamic models of growth and arrivals. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 409.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Probability Models for Economic Decisions Project
courses.description: Selection and completion of a project under faculty supervision that complements coursework on probability models for economic decisions. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4012.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Experimental and Behavioral Economics
courses.description: Design and implementation of economic experiments. Computer programming of experiments and statistical analysis of experimental results. Behavioral economic models as an alternative to neoclassical economics include prospect theory, time-inconsistent preferences, and social preferences. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 445.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030; and ECON 395 or ECON 3015.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030; and ECON 395 or ECON 3015.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Experimental and Behavioral Economics Project
courses.description: Completion of an original design, implementation and analysis of a lab experiment testing economic theory under faculty supervision. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Corequisite: ECON 4013.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Advanced Econometrics
courses.description: Advanced econometric techniques used to analyze relationships between variables, test economic theories, or uncover causal effects. Concepts in causal inference such as randomization, covariate-adjustment methods, and instrumental variables. Binary-choice and nonlinear models. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 440.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 339 or ECON 3021.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ECON 339 or ECON 3021.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Advanced Econometrics Project
courses.description: Application of advanced econometric techniques to real-world data to address economic problems by analyzing relationships between variables, testing economic theories, or uncovering causal effects. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4021.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Applied Forecasting
courses.description: Use of economic, financial, and other time series data to build and evaluate forecasting models. Forecasting methods including regression-based models, exponential smoothing, AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and the Generalized AutoRegressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH) family of models. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 406.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 339 or ECON 3021.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ECON 339 or ECON 3021.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Applied Forecasting Project
courses.description: Selection and completion of a time series and forecasting project under faculty supervision. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4024.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Causal Machine Learning for Economics
courses.description: Prediction methods for causal inference. Directed acyclic graphs, double lasso, and double machine learning. Economic applications. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 395, CSC 101, CSC 231, CSC 232, ECON 3015, CSC 1001, CSC 1031, or CSC 1032; and one of the following: ECON 339, STAT 324, STAT 334, ECON 3021, STAT 3430, or STAT 3530.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: ECON 395, CSC 101, CSC 231, CSC 232, ECON 3015, CSC 1001, CSC 1031, or CSC 1032; and one of the following: ECON 339, STAT 324, STAT 334, ECON 3021, STAT 3430, or STAT 3530.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Causal Machine Learning for Economics Project
courses.description: Machine learning and causal inference replication exercises. Complements the coursework on causal machine learning for economics. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Corequisite: ECON 4025.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Industrial Organization
courses.description: Application of basic tools of economics to American industry. Case studies of individual firms and industries. Performance of various business structures, such as monopoly and oligopoly. Effects of government regulation and antitrust policy. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 403.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Industrial Organization Project
courses.description: Application of economic modeling to analyze a selected concept from the field of Industrial Organization. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Corequisite: ECON 4031.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Monetary Economics
courses.description: The role of money in our economy. The links between monetary policy, interest rates, prices, housing markets, mortgage lending and overall economic activity. Public policy issues relating to real estate markets. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 424.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 313 or ECON 3040.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ECON 313 or ECON 3040.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Monetary Economics Project
courses.description: Application of economic theory and econometrics to the analysis of recent events related to the field of monetary economics. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4042.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: International Monetary Economics
courses.description: Nature of international payments, U.S. balance of payments. Theory and practice of foreign exchange rate determination under the gold standard, paper standard, and International Monetary Fund (IMF) system. International money and capital markets. Problems of international liquidity and monetary stability. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 405.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 313 or ECON 3040.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ECON 313 or ECON 3040.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: International Monetary Economics Project
courses.description: Economics research in the field of international monetary economics. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Corequisite: ECON 4043.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Public Finance and Public Policy
courses.description: Principles of rational decision making with respect to government revenues and spending. Externalities and public goods. Measurement of costs and benefits, and criterion selection. Social insurance. Taxation. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 410.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Public Finance and Public Policy Project
courses.description: Use statistical software to analyze topics from public finance. Evaluation of government policy using the criteria of economic efficiency and equity. Cost benefit analysis. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4052.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Labor Economics
courses.description: Wage determination theory. Basic economic factors that affect the labor movement. Economic impact of union activities on employment, output, income, wages, prices, and national economic policy. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 413.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Labor Economics Project
courses.description: Use of software to work with government labor data. Summarize labor outcomes and analyze determinants of wages. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4053.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics of Education
courses.description: Application of microeconomic theory, public economics, labor economics, industrial organization to the economics of education. Relationship between primary, secondary, and higher education and labor markets, education policy, and the impact of educational investments on individual and societal outcomes. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Urban Economics
courses.description: Application of basic tools of economic analysis to problems of urban regions. Economics of urban land use, zoning, housing, transportation, local public goods, and crime. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 434.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 311, ECON 3030, or ECON 3039.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ECON 311, ECON 3030, or ECON 3039. Recommended: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Urban Economics Project
courses.description: Use of statistical software and economic modeling to analyze topics from urban economics. Spreadsheet analysis of residential mortgages. The hedonic method of real estate valuation. Economic policy analysis. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4055.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: International Trade Theory
courses.description: Theory of comparative advantage, neoclassical model of trade, offer curves and terms of trade, edgeworth boxes, valuation of factor inputs, effects of migration and mobility of funds, emerging growth and trade distortions, welfare effects of trade, and recent developments in trade theory. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 404.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: International Trade Project
courses.description: Review and critique of academic literature and/or news media in regard to a selected concept from the field of international trade. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4061.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Development Economics
courses.description: Economic market failures and poverty traps. Public policies for market failures. Causal econometric techniques, and replication exercises on microfinance and microinsurance. Education, health, and agriculture policies, intrahousehold allocations and gender, and corruption and governance. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030; and ECON 440 or ECON 4021.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ECON 311 or ECON 3030; and ECON 440 or ECON 4021.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Environmental Economics
courses.description: Economic dimensions of environmental abuse and protection. Use of simple economic models in developing and evaluating environmental policies. Overview of current environmental problems. Issues related to the sustainability of economic growth at the national and international levels. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 431.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Environmental Economics Project
courses.description: Application of economic modeling to analyze a selected concept from the field of environmental economics. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4071.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics of Energy and Resources
courses.description: Economic theory and public policies for natural resources and energy. Dynamic resource and energy models for public and private sector growth. Principles of capital theory emphasized. Computer software applications of natural resource and energy use under uncertainty. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 432.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics of Energy and Resources Project
courses.description: Application of economic modeling to analyze a concept in natural resource economics. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Corequisite: ECON 4072.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics of Land and Water
courses.description: Economic analysis of natural resource issues, policies and management with an emphasis on land and water use decisions in the western United States. Urban demand for water, water supply, economic growth, economic impacts of surface water law and institutions, and land management. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 435.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ECON 312 or ECON 3050.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics of Land and Water Project
courses.description: Use of computer software to analyze problems in water and land management. Optimal water allocation, optimal forest management, water pricing. Course offered online only. 1 activity.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Corequisite: ECON 4073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Development of Economic Thought
courses.description: Analysis of ideas related to the development of economic theory in the Western civilization from the Greeks through the classical, neoclassical, and Keynesian to the current post-Keynesian concepts. 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 417.
courses.prerequisite: ECON 311, ECON 3030, or ECON 3039.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: ECON 311, ECON 3030, or ECON 3039.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Applied Senior Project
courses.description: Analysis of selected economic topics and problems in directed individual or group-based projects, which require application of economic models, principles and theory to investigate important business, economic or social issues. Formal report required. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 4 seminars. Formerly ECON 464.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; ECON 311 or ECON 3030; ECON 313 or ECON 3040; ECON 339 or ECON 3021; and two 4000-level ECON courses.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing; ECON 311 or ECON 3030; ECON 313 or ECON 3040; ECON 339 or ECON 3021; and two 4000-level ECON courses.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly ECON 470.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Essential Mathematics for Economic Analysis
courses.description: Review and discussion of the math tools needed for graduate work in economics, including set theory, calculus, linear algebra, properties of functions, and optimization. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 510.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SU Prerequisite: Graduate standing. Recommended: ECON 408 or ECON 4010.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Evidence-Based Decision Analysis
courses.description: Representing uncertainty using discrete and continuous conditional probabilities. Monte Carlo simulation of independent and correlated random variables. Optimization under certainty and uncertainty. Case studies. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 544.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and one of the following: ECON 5021, GSE 520, GSB 518, or GSB 5518.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing and one of the following: ECON 5021, GSE 520, GSB 518, or GSB 5518. Recommended: GSE 524 or ECON 5015.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Computing and Machine Learning for Economics
courses.description: Use of computer programming for advanced data analysis in economics and analytics. Computer programming using statistical software, data gathering and cleaning, and machine learning. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 524.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Collaborative Software Development Environment for Economists
courses.description: Best practices for scientific computing in economics research regarding effectiveness, efficiency, maintainability, reproducibility, clarity, scalability and portability. The Unix shell. Version control. Git and GitHub. Automation and Make. Job schedulers. Agile methodologies for project management. Elements of programming style. 1 lecture.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Corequisite: GSE 524 or ECON 5015.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Essential Statistics for Econometrics
courses.description: Statistical concepts for graduate work in econometrics, including probability theory, random variables, distribution functions, independence, expectations, covariance, correlation, random samples, estimation methods, properties of estimators, asymptotic theory, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 518.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SU Prerequisite: Graduate standing. Recommended: GSE 510 or ECON 5010.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Advanced Econometrics I
courses.description: Linear regression model. Confidence and prediction intervals. Hypothesis testing. Generalized regression model and heteroscedasticity. Maximum likelihood estimator and its properties. Simulation and resampling methods. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 520.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing; and GSE 518 or ECON 5020.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing; and GSE 518 or ECON 5020.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Advanced Econometrics II
courses.description: Maximum likelihood estimation. Binary, multinomial, and ordered discrete response models. Simulation methods, bootstrap standard errors. Truncated, censored regression. Structural equation modeling. Random utility and mixed logit models. Demand estimation. Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimation. Single agent dynamic models. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 522.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing; and GSE 520 or ECON 5021.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing; and GSE 520 or ECON 5021.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Microeconometrics
courses.description: Limited dependent variables and selection models. Quantile regression and nonparametric methods. Causal inference: Potential outcomes framework, causal treatment effects, randomization, matching, propensity-score methods, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity, difference-in-difference, two-way fixed effects, synthetic control, and econometrics of randomized experiments. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 526.
courses.prerequisite: GSE 520 or ECON 5021.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: GSE 520 or ECON 5021.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Modeling Financial Time Series
courses.description: Time-series analysis to model the risk and return of financial assets. Linear Time-Series models, Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Stationary and Non-stationary Series, Cointegration, Vector Auto-regression (VAR), Vector Error Correction (VECM), Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity family (GARCH), Value-at-Risk (VaR), and Extreme Value Theorem. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as ECON 5024/GSB 5548.
courses.prerequisite: one of the following: GSB 518, GSB 5518, GSE 518, or ECON 5020; and GSE 520 or ECON 5021.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: one of the following: GSB 518, GSB 5518, GSE 518, or ECON 5020; and GSE 520 or ECON 5021.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Machine Learning for Prediction and Causal Inference
courses.description: Regularization, model selection, and supervised learning. Post model selection inference for causal effects. Double/debiased machine learning, causal trees, causal forests, and synthetic controls. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 552.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Corequisite: GSE 526 or ECON 5023.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Econometrics and Data Analysis
courses.description: Estimation and analysis of econometric models for analyzing business data. Linear regression models, robust standard errors, causal inference, instrumental variables, maximum likelihood estimation, and logistic regression models and extensions. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 519.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: GSB 518, GSE 518, GSB 5518, or ECON 5020.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: GSB 518, GSE 518, GSB 5518, or ECON 5020.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Microeconomic Analysis
courses.description: Preferences and choice, preferences over commodities, consumer demand theory, producer theory, choice under uncertainty, simultaneous and sequential move games, incomplete information games, mechanism and incentive design. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 511.
courses.prerequisite: GSE 510 or ECON 5010.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: GSE 510 or ECON 5010.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Industrial Economics
courses.description: Economic theories of industrial organization with specific reference to cartels, market concentration and performance, vertical integration, franchise contracts, ownership and control of firms, multipart and discriminatory pricing, and tie-in sales. Antitrust law and government regulation of industry. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 538.
courses.prerequisite: GSE 511 or ECON 5030.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: GSE 511 or ECON 5030.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Incentives and Market Design
courses.description: Ascending, first-price, second-price, and double auctions. Revenue equivalence, multi-unit auctions, the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves mechanism, and matching markets. The deferred acceptance algorithm, the immediate acceptance algorithm, and the many-to-one matching model. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 546.
courses.prerequisite: GSE 511 or ECON 5030.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: GSE 511 or ECON 5030.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Dynamic Stochastic Modeling
courses.description: Finite Markov chains, linear state space models, dynamic programming, autoregressive-1 (AR1) processes, optimal growth models, optimal job search models, Arrow securities, consumption-based asset pricing. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 512.
courses.prerequisite: GSE 524 or ECON 5015; and GSE 511 or ECON 5030.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: GSE 524 or ECON 5015; and GSE 511 or ECON 5030.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Public Economics
courses.description: Economic analysis of the rationale for public expenditure and taxation. Externalities, pollution and public policy, income redistribution and public welfare, public goods, collective choice and political institutions, cost-benefit analysis, taxation and tax policy, and state-local finance. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 536.
courses.prerequisite: GSE 511 or ECON 5030.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: GSE 511 or ECON 5030.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Advanced Labor Economics
courses.description: Research methods in labor economics and application of modern empirical techniques to the analysis of labor markets. Labor supply and demand, discrimination, migration, and human capital accumulation. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 542.
courses.prerequisite: GSE 520 or ECON 5021; and GSE 526 or ECON 5023.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: GSE 520 or ECON 5021; and GSE 526 or ECON 5023.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: International Economics
courses.description: Analysis of the international movement of goods, services, capital and payments. The role of exchange rates, tariffs, quotas, and transport costs. Relationship between international trade and economic growth. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 534.
courses.prerequisite: GSE 511 or ECON 5030.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: GSE 511 or ECON 5030.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Environmental and Natural Resource Economics
courses.description: Economic analysis of pollution, congestion, public good provision, and natural resource conservation. Static and dynamic efficiency, economic growth and sustainability, pollution taxes, marketable permits, and the design of market-based regulations. 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 532.
courses.prerequisite: GSE 511 or ECON 5030.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: GSE 511 or ECON 5030.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Advanced study planned and completed under the direction of a departmental faculty member. Repeatable up to 6 units. Formerly GSE 500.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of program director.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of program director.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Applied Economics Project
courses.description: Applied, real-world empirical projects in economics chosen according to the common interests and needs of the students enrolled. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 to 4 seminars. Formerly GSE 580.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in MS Quantitative Economics program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing in MS Quantitative Economics program. Recommended: ECON 5016.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for graduate students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly GSE 570.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Comprehensive Examination
courses.description: Culminating written exam for masters in quantitative economics demonstrating independent thinking using material from economic theory, econometrics, and computer programming. Scheduled in the final semester of the graduate program. Credit/No Credit grading only.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of department chair.

courses.subject: EDES
courses.title: Place, People, and the Built Environment
courses.description: Introduction to design, planning, and construction of the built environment as shaped by social, political, and cultural factors. Examination of the impacts of the built environment on society, including environmental and social justice, well-being, sustainability, and formation of identity and community. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 1 lecture, 2 discussions. Fulfills GE Area 4B (GE Area D2 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 4B 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area D2 Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 4B 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area D2 Sustainability Focused

courses.subject: EDES
courses.title: The Global Environment
courses.description: Interdisciplinary investigation of how human activities impact the Earth's environment on a global scale. Examination of population, resource use, climate change, and biodiversity from scientific/technical and social/economic/ historical/political perspectives. Use of remote sensing maps. Sustainable solutions. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as AG/EDES/ENGR/GEOG/ISLA/SCM/UNIV 3350. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly AG/EDES/ENGR/GEOG/ISLA/SCM/UNIV 350.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5 (GE Areas B1 to B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5 (GE Areas B1 to B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: EDES
courses.title: Sustainable Environments
courses.description: Introduction, illustration and analysis of concepts and principles of sustainability. Integration and application of knowledge of human and natural systems with environmental, social and economic concerns from a global-to-local perspective. Collaboration of interdisciplinary faculty and guest speakers/panelists. Field trip may be required. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly EDES 406.
courses.prerequisite: Senior or graduate standing.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: Senior or graduate standing.

courses.subject: EDES
courses.title: Implementing Sustainability Principles
courses.description: A project-based course for students to collaborate with the purpose of implementing sustainability principles by developing community-based projects and proposals at various scales to address social, environmental and economic issues. 2 lectures, 2 discussions. Formerly EDES 408.
courses.prerequisite: EDES 406 or EDES 4406.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: EDES 406 or EDES 4406.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Children's Learning and Development in Educational Settings
courses.description: Introduction to developmental and learning theories of children/teens. Emphasis on observations/interactions with culturally and linguistically diverse learners. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Crosslisted as CD/EDUC 2207. Formerly CD/EDUC 207.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly EDUC 270.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Historical, Philosophical, and Social Foundations of Public Education
courses.description: Historical, philosophical, and social foundations of public education in relation to school curriculum, instruction and dispositions of effective teachers. Structured observation and participation in PK-12 public schools with attention to instructional practices for diverse learners. 2 seminars, 1 activity. Formerly EDUC 300.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of one lower-division course in GE Area 4 (GE Areas D1 or D2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of one lower-division course in GE Area 4 (GE Areas D1 or D2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Special Problems for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies or surveys of selected problems. Repeatable up to 6 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly EDUC 400.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Learning to Teach PK-8 Health and Physical Education with Diverse Populations
courses.description: Instructional methodologies in health and physical education. Design and implementation of elementary school instruction to address standards for health and physical education. Course offered in hybrid format with classroom-based and online learning. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly EDUC 402.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Developing Teachers of Color
courses.description: Developing and supporting teachers of Color in elementary and secondary (PK-12) education. Focus on structural factors associated with underrepresentation of teachers of Color, culturally sustaining pedagogies, and resources to support teachers of Color. 3 seminars. Formerly EDUC 403.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and completion of GE Area 6 (GE Area F for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Junior standing; and completion of GE Area 6 (GE Area F for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Social, Historical and Cultural Influences on Latinx Students in Education
courses.description: Socio-cultural, historical, political, economic, and educational systems in Latin America and the United States. Factors that influence identity and Latinx schooling experience. Half of the course is delivered in Spanish. Course may be offered in online or hybrid format. 3 seminars, 1 activity. Formerly EDUC 405.
courses.prerequisite: SPAN 203 or SPAN 2202 with a grade of B or better or consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: SPAN 203 or SPAN 2202 with a grade of B or better or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Fundamentals of Teaching
courses.description: Inquiry into sociocultural, historical, philosophical, and psychological foundations of education. Introduction to curriculum design that supports disciplinary literacy development. Emphasis on teaching culturally and linguistically diverse learners in secondary schools. Course offered online only. 4 lectures. Formerly EDUC 416.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SU Prerequisite: Admission to Single Subject Credential Program.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Access to Learning for a More Equitable Society
courses.description: The role of race, ethnicity, language, and inequality in public school experiences of diverse learners. Organization and design of culturally democratic secondary school classrooms contextualized within access to learning. 4 lectures. Formerly EDUC 412.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Admission to the Single Subject Credential Program.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Teaching Emergent Bilingual Students and Students with Alternative Support Needs
courses.description: Culturally responsive instruction to meet the linguistic, social, and academic needs of individual students in diverse classrooms, including emergent bilinguals and students with alternative and extensive support needs. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 4 lectures. Formerly EDUC 418.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Admission to the Single Subject Credential Program.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Seminar in Education
courses.description: Exploration of critical issues and topics in education including translanguaging, equity-centered trauma-informed instruction, media and digital literacies, and interdisciplinary curriculum with an emphasis on project-based learning. Credit/No Credit grading only. 2 seminars.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Single Subject Credential Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Admission to the Single Subject Credential Program.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Culturally Responsive Methods and Inquiry for Teaching Emergent Bilinguals
courses.description: Theories, methods, materials and assessment involved in the culturally responsive instruction of Emergent Bilinguals/English Learners (ELs). Bilingual, transitional, and English-only programs compared across an historical framework. An integrated language arts approach emphasizing theories of language acquisition. Participation in public schools requires mandated fingerprint clearance. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 seminars, 1 activity. Formerly EDUC 427.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing, and Liberal Studies major or Equity in Education Minor; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Senior standing, and Liberal Studies major or Equity in Education Minor; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Learning to Teach PK-3 Literacy with Diverse Populations
courses.description: Integration of theory and practice for planning, instruction and assessment in a comprehensive, research-based PK-3 literacy and language arts program, enabling all children to effectively read, write, speak, and listen. 3 seminars, 1 activity. Formerly EDUC 428.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Learning to Teach 4-8 Literacy in Schools with Diverse Populations
courses.description: Integration of theory and practice for planning, instruction and assessment in a balanced, comprehensive, research-based 4-8 literacy and language arts program to enable children of all abilities and background to read, write, speak, listen and think effectively. 3 seminars. Formerly EDUC 429.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Learning to Teach K-8 Social Studies with Diverse Populations
courses.description: Curriculum instruction and assessment concepts regarding teaching social studies to culturally diverse students in grades K-8, to promote civic competence and the development of elementary students' knowledge and reasoning in the social sciences. 3 seminars. Formerly EDUC 431.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Foundations of Bilingual Education and Biliteracy Instruction
courses.description: Theories, policies and practices associated with bilingual education and biliteracy instruction for Latinx students in California. Observation and teaching in bilingual classrooms. Approximately half of course is delivered in Spanish. Course may be offered in online or hybrid format. 3 seminars, 1 activity. Formerly EDUC 433.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Spanish Authorization for Bilingual Educators (SABE) Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Admission to the Spanish Authorization for Bilingual Educators (SABE) Program.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Learning to Teach PK-8 STEM with Diverse Populations I
courses.description: Curriculum, instruction, and assessment concepts regarding teaching science, technology, engineering and mathematics to culturally diverse students in grades PK-8 with emphasis on inquiry-based teaching. 4 seminars. Formerly EDUC 435.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Learning to Teach PK-8 STEM to Diverse Populations II
courses.description: Differentiation, culturally relevant instruction, and assessment concepts related to teaching STEM to culturally diverse students in grades PK-8. 2 seminars. Formerly EDUC 435.
courses.prerequisite: EDUC 435 or EDUC 4435.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: EDUC 435 or EDUC 4435.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Multiple Subject Clinical Practice Seminar I
courses.description: Discussion of contemporary educational issues and classroom practice; reflection on beginning clinical experiences in elementary education and their connection with educational theory and research. Credit/No Credit grading only. 3 seminars. Formerly EDUC 439.
courses.prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Admission to the Multiple Subject Teacher Preparation Program.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Educating Individuals with Exceptional Needs
courses.description: Terminology, identification, and issues associated with addressing the needs of students with exceptionalities in the general education classroom. Emphasis on inclusion, diversity, federal and state legislative mandates, parental involvement, individualized education programs and foundations in special education. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly EDUC 440.
courses.prerequisite: EDUC 300 or EDUC 3300; or Liberal Studies major and junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: EDUC 300 or EDUC 3300; or Liberal Studies major and junior standing.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: PK-3 Developmental Theory and Applications in Early Childhood School Settings
courses.description: Examination and application in school settings of topics in early childhood development, such as cognitive, language, and physical development; processes underlying social and emotional regulation; adult-child relationships; differences in development and contributions of family, school, and society. 3 seminars.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into the PK-3 credential program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SU Prerequisite: Admission into the PK-3 credential program. Corequisite: EDUC 4460.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: PK-3 Partnerships: Families and Communities
courses.description: Strategies to engage families and communities in education for children aged three through grade three. Building strong relationships for children's development and learning through collaboration, communication, and asset-based ideas. Understanding and addressing children's strengths and needs with cultural competence and equity. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 seminars.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into the PK-3 credential program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SU Prerequisite: Admission into the PK-3 credential program. Corequisite: EDUC 4460.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Learning to Teach PK-3 Mathematics to Diverse Populations
courses.description: Exploration of developmentally appropriate mathematics instruction for aspiring PK-3 teachers. Design of developmentally appropriate mathematics learning activities and experiences that are aligned with preschool learning frameworks and math standards connecting mathematics to children's everyday lived experiences and interests. 3 seminars.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into the PK-3 credential program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Admission into the PK-3 credential program. Corequisite: EDUC 4460.

courses.subject: EDUC
courses.title: Disciplinary Literacy and Integrated Curriculum in PK-3
courses.description: Examine how reading, writing, speaking, listening, and viewing are tools for learning content across the disciplines in PK-3 classrooms; exploration of a disciplinary literacy framework that guides an inquiry-based approach to curriculum planning, curriculum implementation, and assessment principles. 3 seminars.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into the PK-3 credential program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Admission into the PK-3 credential program. Corequisite: EDUC 4469.

courses.subject: EDUC
