courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Flag Football
courses.description: Basic instruction in flag football skill development, knowledge, and desirable attitudes toward physical activity, such that beginning to intermediate levels of play are attained. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly KINE 1141.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Beginning Swimming
courses.description: Development of swimming strokes for adults to improve confidence and endurance as novice swimmers. Enrollment is open to all students. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly KINE 144.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Intermediate Swimming
courses.description: Continuation of stroke refinement for adult swimmers who have basic beginning level swimming skills. Practice of swimming strokes and swimming drills for the enhancement of confidence and improvement of swimming effectiveness and endurance. Enrollment is open to all students. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly KINE 145.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Recommended: Ability to swim 50 yards non-stop.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Advanced Swimming and Conditioning
courses.description: Lap swimming for advanced swimmers. Organized structured swim workouts with emphasis on increasing fitness. Participants should have ability to swim three of the four competitive strokes: freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly. Students must be able to swim 100 yards non-stop using at least two competitive strokes. Enrollment is open to all students. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly KINE 147.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Tennis
courses.description: Basic instruction in tennis skill development and knowledge. Enrollment is open to all students. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly KINE 148.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Volleyball
courses.description: Basic instruction in volleyball skill development, knowledge, and desirable attitudes toward physical activity. Enrollment is open to all students. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly KINE 151.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Beach Volleyball
courses.description: Basic instruction in beach volleyball skill development, knowledge, and desirable attitudes while toward physical activity. Enrollment is open to all students. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly KINE 152.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Strength Training
courses.description: Basic instruction in skill development, knowledge, and desirable attitudes in a weight room/strength training setting. Enrollment is open to all students. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly KINE 154.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Fitness Walking
courses.description: Basic instruction in fitness walking skill development, knowledge, and desirable attitudes toward physical activity. Enrollment is open to all students. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly KINE 176.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Introduction to Kinesiology
courses.description: Introduction to Kinesiology, sub-disciplines, physical activity history, guidelines, scholarly work and careers. Orientation to the department of Kinesiology and Public Health, faculty, and campus resources to facilitate student success. Credit/No Credit grading only. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 1 activity. Formerly KINE 180.
courses.prerequisite: Kinesiology major.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Kinesiology major.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Responding to Emergencies: Comprehensive First Aid, CPR, AED
courses.description: An American Red Cross certification course designed to help participants recognize and respond appropriately to cardiac, breathing, and first aid emergencies. Skills and knowledge necessary in the treatment of life-threatening emergencies, other injuries, and sudden illnesses. Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED certifications issued upon successful completion of certification requirements. Credit/No Credit grading only. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 1 lecture, 1 activity. Formerly KINE 181.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Special Problems for Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of special problems. Repeatable up to 4 units. Crosslisted as HLTH/KINE 2200. Formerly HLTH/KINE 201.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Introduction to Principles of Exercise, Fitness, and Sport
courses.description: Introduction to scientific basis of exercise and sport including concepts associated with health-related components of fitness. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly KINE 240.
courses.prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: HLTH 250, HLTH 255, HLTH 260, HLTH 1150, HLTH 1155, or HLTH 1160.
courses.recommended: MATH 119 or MATH 1007; and one of the following: PHYS 121, PHYS 141, PHYS 1121, or PHYS 1141.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: HLTH 250, HLTH 255, HLTH 260, HLTH 1150, HLTH 1155, or HLTH 1160. Recommended: MATH 119 or MATH 1007; and one of the following: PHYS 121, PHYS 141, PHYS 1121, or PHYS 1141.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Sport and Performance Psychology
courses.description: An introduction to the field of sport and performance psychology. Psychological theories and research related to topics such as motivation to participate in sport and exercise, exercise and psychological well-being, teamwork and leadership, aggression, anxiety, psychological response to athletic injuries, and exercise addiction. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly KINE 266.
courses.prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 1A with a grade of C- or better (GE Area A2 for the 2020-26 catalogs) and completion of GE Area 1C with a grade of C- or better (GE Area A1 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.recommended: Completion of GE Area 1B with a grade of C- or better (GE Area A3 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and PSY 201 or PSY 2201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 1A with a grade of C- or better (GE Area A2 for the 2020-26 catalogs) and completion of GE Area 1C with a grade of C- or better (GE Area A1 for the 2020-26 catalogs). Recommended: Completion of GE Area 1B with a grade of C- or better (GE Area A3 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and PSY 201 or PSY 2201.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 4 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 1 to 3 lectures. Crosslisted as HLTH/KINE 2270. Formerly HLTH/KINE 290.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Introduction to Athletic Training
courses.description: Basic mechanisms of common sports injuries and acute care of these injuries. Prevention, risk management, and basic healthcare administration for athletes. 2 lectures, 1 discussion.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BIO 111, BIO 1111, BIO 161, or BIO 1151.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: BIO 111, BIO 1111, BIO 161, or BIO 1151.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Physiology of Exercise
courses.description: Acute and adaptive responses of the respiratory, cardiovascular, neuromuscular, endocrine, and metabolic systems to exercise. Application to fitness, athletic performance, healthy aging, disease mitigation, and environmental safety. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly KINE 303.
courses.prerequisite: BIO 231 or BIO 2231; and one of the following: BIO 232, BIO 361, BIO 2232, or BIO 3352.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: BIO 231 or BIO 2231; and one of the following: BIO 232, BIO 361, BIO 2232, or BIO 3352.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Adapted Physical Activity
courses.description: Major categories of disabling conditions with implications for the development of physical activity programs for specific disabilities. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as HNRS/KINE 3307. Formerly KINE 307.
courses.prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 5A (GE Area B1 for the 2020-26 catalogs) and completion of GE Area 5B (GE Area B2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 5A (GE Area B1 for the 2020-26 catalogs) and completion of GE Area 5B (GE Area B2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Concepts and Applications in Elementary Physical Education
courses.description: Strategies for teaching physical motor skills in elementary grades K-6. Age-appropriate developmental activities, physical fitness, wellness, social development, cross-cultural understanding, and self-image. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly KINE 310.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Motor Learning
courses.description: Analysis of factors that affect the acquisition of motor skills as related to the learning process and the learning environment. 3 lectures. Formerly KINE 312.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: STAT 217, STAT 218, or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: STAT 217, STAT 218, or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Introduction to Research Methods in Kinesiology
courses.description: Principles of reading and conducting research including contemporary research perspectives in kinesiology. Basic and applied research. Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. Formerly KINE 319.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: STAT 217, STAT 218, or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: STAT 217, STAT 218, or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Sport and Gender
courses.description: Intersections between sport and gender in American society. Identification and discussion of the historical, sociological, and psychological issues that affect the sport experiences of people of different genders, especially as they relate to class, race/ethnicity, sexuality, media, and political movements. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs); USCP; and GWR.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of one lower-division course in GE Area 4 (GE Areas D1 or D2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 4 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area D
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 4 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area D GWR USCP Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of one lower-division course in GE Area 4 (GE Areas D1 or D2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Sports, Media, and United States Popular Culture
courses.description: Relationships between sports, media, and issues of class, race/ethnicity, gender, various forms of deviance, including values, violence, substance abuse, and other aspects of social life. Exploration of sociological manifestations and implications of how the aforementioned social issues are embedded in mediated forms of sports. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs); USCP, and GWR.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of one lower-division course in GE Area 4 (GE Areas D1 or D2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 4 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area D
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 4 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area D GWR USCP Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of one lower-division course in GE Area 4 (GE Areas D1 or D2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Sport and Physical Activity Throughout Civilizations
courses.description: Current and historical trends in human movement from philosophical perspectives including Western and Eastern intellectual traditions. The effects of culture on the view of the human body and the understanding of the role of physical activity and sport in people's lives. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 3 (GE Area Upper-Division C for students on the 2020-26 catalogs); and GWR.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 3 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area C
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 3 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area C GWR Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Group Exercise and Personal Training
courses.description: Instructional competencies in the fundamental components of group exercise classes and individually tailored personal training programs. Instructional techniques, programming, professionalism, and leadership styles conducive to promoting health, fitness, and exercise adherence. Basic theory related to human anatomy, exercise physiology, training principles, and relevant American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM) guidelines are applied to cardio, resistance, and flexibility training. 1 lecture, 1 activities. Formerly KINE 459.
courses.prerequisite: BIO 231 or BIO 2231.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: BIO 231 or BIO 2231.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Early Fieldwork Experience
courses.description: Practical work experience in related activities of kinesiology or public health under qualified supervision. Repeatable up to 4 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Crosslisted as HLTH/KINE 3337. Formerly HLTH/KINE 337.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Exercise Testing and Prescription
courses.description: Selected areas of health/fitness screening and evaluation. Application of components relevant to the development and administration of exercise programs for healthy persons regardless of sex, age, or functional capacity. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly KINE 349.
courses.prerequisite: KINE 303 or KINE 3303.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: KINE 303 or KINE 3303.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Applied Sport and Performance Psychology
courses.description: Psychological considerations of the coach-athlete relationship and mental preparation of teams and individuals for competition, practice, and performance. Application of sport psychology principles to develop a psychological skills training program appropriate to enhance performance and well-being in sport, exercise, or performance contexts. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly KINE 366.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: KINE 266, KINE 2266, PSY 201, or PSY 2201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: KINE 266, KINE 2266, PSY 201, or PSY 2201.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
courses.description: Advanced principles of athletic care, therapeutic modalities, taping and bracing, identifying injuries, care and prevention of injuries. 2 lectures, 1 activity.
courses.prerequisite: KINE 2278; KINE 303 or KINE 3303; and Kinesiology major; or KINE 240 or KINE 2240; and KINE 2278 for all other majors.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: KINE 2278; KINE 303 or KINE 3303; and Kinesiology major; or KINE 240 or KINE 2240; and KINE 2278 for all other majors.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Psychological Aspects of Injury in Sport and Physical Activity
courses.description: Psychosocial antecedents to injury in sport/exercise, factors in psychological experience and treatment of the injured individual. Psychological theories and applied considerations related to injury and rehabilitation. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly KINE 382.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 5A (GE Area B1 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of one lower-division course in GE Area 4 (GE Areas D1 or D2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 4 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area D
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 4 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area D Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 5A (GE Area B1 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of one lower-division course in GE Area 4 (GE Areas D1 or D2 for the 2020-26 catalogs). Recommended: KINE 266 or KINE 2266.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Special Problems for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigations, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Repeatable up to 4 units. Crosslisted as HLTH/KINE 4400. Formerly HLTH/KINE 400.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Leadership in Health and Physical Activity Programs
courses.description: Leadership and management principles relevant to planning and operating programs in public, commercial, private and clinical exercise, health and sport settings with an emphasis on technological and ethical considerations. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly KINE 401.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: HLTH 3344, KINE 266, or KINE 2266.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: HLTH 3344, KINE 266, or KINE 2266.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Biomechanics
courses.description: Fundamental biomechanical concepts and musculoskeletal functioning including examination of activities of daily living and performance settings. Examination of the effects of chronic and acute loading on the body. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly KINE 403.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BIO 231, BIO 411, BIO 2231, BIO 3333, or BIO 4431; PHYS 121 or PHYS 1121.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: BIO 231, BIO 411, BIO 2231, BIO 3333, or BIO 4431; PHYS 121 or PHYS 1121.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Clinical Exercise Physiology
courses.description: Selected human diseases and environmental and societal conditions which may adversely affect health or physical performance: their etiology, pathophysiology, signs and symptoms, diagnosis, and as affected by preventive or therapeutic exercise. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly KINE 304.
courses.prerequisite: KINE 303 or KINE 3303.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: KINE 303 or KINE 3303. Recommended: KINE 445 or KINE 4445.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Motor Control
courses.description: Advanced motor control principles. Sensory motor coupling that govern the non-conscious regulation of posture, locomotion, reaching, and grasping. Central and peripheral nervous system development and functioning. Applications to motor learning and pathologies that lead to dysfunction. 3 lectures. Formerly KINE 406.
courses.prerequisite: BIO 231 and BIO 232, or BIO 2231 and BIO 2232, or BIO 361 or BIO 3352.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: BIO 231 and BIO 232, or BIO 2231 and BIO 2232, or BIO 361 or BIO 3352.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Physical Activity and Aging
courses.description: Special fitness, exercise, and health needs of older adults. Theories of aging and age-related changes. Health and physical activity programs for older adults. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly KINE 408.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: HLTH 250, HLTH 255, HLTH 260, HLTH 1150, HLTH 1155, HLTH 1160, or HLTH 2261; and one of the following: FSN 315, KINE 303, KINE 3303, NUTR 3315, PSY 318, or PSY 3318.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: HLTH 250, HLTH 255, HLTH 260, HLTH 1150, HLTH 1155, HLTH 1160, or HLTH 2261; and one of the following: FSN 315, KINE 303, KINE 3303, NUTR 3315, PSY 318, or PSY 3318.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Projects in Biomechanics
courses.description: Examination of human motion biomechanics. Experimental and analytical methods in motion analysis. Rigid body dynamics. Protocols for protection of human subjects in research. Hypothesis-driven research. Interdisciplinary teams. Proposal development. Written/oral communication to a scientific audience. 1 lecture, 2 activities. Crosslisted as BMED/KINE/ME 4409. Formerly BMED/KINE/ME 409.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BMED 410, BMED 3410, KINE 403, KINE 4403, ME 212, or ME 2212.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: BMED 410, BMED 3410, KINE 403, KINE 4403, ME 212, or ME 2212.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Physical Activity and Public Health
courses.description: Evaluation of scientific evidence supporting current physical activity guidelines for physical and mental well-being. Application of evidence-based strategies to promote physical activity at the individual, community, and policy levels. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly KINE 412.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: HLTH 318, HLTH 3318, KINE 319, or KINE 3319.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: HLTH 318, HLTH 3318, KINE 319, or KINE 3319. Recommended: KINE 303 or KINE 3303.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Physiology and Assessment
courses.description: Cardiopulmonary physiology and methods of assessment of cardiopulmonary function including palpation, auscultation, phonocardiography, electrocardiography, and echocardiography. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly KINE 445.
courses.prerequisite: KINE 303 or KINE 3303.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: KINE 303 or KINE 3303.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Exercise Science Seminar
courses.description: Advanced examination of current and evolving topics in exercise science, including performance and clinical applications with an emphasis on exercise physiology. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. 2 seminars.
courses.prerequisite: KINE 303 or KINE 3303; and KINE 319 or KINE 3319.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: KINE 303 or KINE 3303; and KINE 319 or KINE 3319. Recommended: KINE 304 or KINE 4404.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Nutrition for Fitness and Sport
courses.description: Application of nutritional and metabolic concepts to selected aspects of physical training, diet manipulation, and modification in sport. Nutritional supplementation and special dietary considerations for athletes of all ages. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 4 lectures. Formerly KINE 451.
courses.prerequisite: KINE 303 or KINE 3303; and KINE 319 or KINE 3319.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: KINE 303 or KINE 3303; and KINE 319 or KINE 3319.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Senior Project - Experiential
courses.description: Applied and project-based culminating experience in kinesiology under faculty supervision. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly KINE 460.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); one of the following: HLTH 402, HLTH 4402, KINE 319, or KINE 3319; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Senior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); one of the following: HLTH 402, HLTH 4402, KINE 319, or KINE 3319; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Senior Project - Report
courses.description: Comprehensive synthesis of professional literature from kinesiology that integrates content from major courses resulting in a report. Topic must be approved by the instructor. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 seminars. Formerly KINE 461.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); one of the following: HLTH 402, HLTH 4402, KINE 319, or KINE 3319; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); one of the following: HLTH 402, HLTH 4402, KINE 319, or KINE 3319; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Senior Project - Research
courses.description: Completion of a research project. Results may be submitted for poster presentation or other public/professional forum. Repeatable up to 2 units. Formerly KINE 462.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); one of the following: HLTH 402, HLTH 4402, KINE 319, or KINE 3319; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); one of the following: HLTH 402, HLTH 4402, KINE 319, or KINE 3319; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: KINE
courses.title: Senior Project - Internship
courses.description: Practical experience at an approved agency that provides health promotion or kinesiology programs. Students participate in program administration under the direct supervision of an approved on-site coordinator as a capstone experience. Minimum 90 hours required with some internship sites requiring more hours. Repeatable up to 2 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly KINE 463.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); one of the following: HLTH 434, HLTH 4434, KINE 319, or KINE 3319; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Senior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); one of the following: HLTH 434, HLTH 4434, KINE 319, or KINE 3319; and consent of instructor.

courses.title: Special Advanced Topics

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: History of Landscape Architecture
courses.description: Philosophies, ethics, personalities, and events of landscape architecture explored from recorded time through current centuries. Design theories supporting important landscape architecture projects. Individuals and influential events in industry, the arts and sciences, politics, and society. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly LA 212.

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: Landscape Representation I
courses.description: Introduction to traditional (analog) communication media for landscape architecture, including methods, techniques, skills, and tools used in design expression, exploration, and generation. 1 lecture, 2 laboratories. Formerly LA 170.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: Landscape Representation II
courses.description: Introduction of digital media applications, computer-aided drawing and fabrication techniques for landscape architects. Development of design representation methods and conventions to communicate qualitative and quantitative landscape information. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 4 activities. Replaced LA 431.
courses.prerequisite: LA 170 or LA 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: LA 170 or LA 1110.

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: Studio I - Beginning Design
courses.description: Introduction to principles, methods and elements of two- and three-dimensional design. Exploration of basic design elements including composition, design process and spatial settings. Introduction to site inventory/ site analysis in landscape architecture design process. 3 laboratories. Formerly LA 202.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Corequisite: LA 1112.

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: Landscape Ecology: Concepts, Issues, and Interrelationships
courses.description: Core life science concepts, theories and techniques explored through the lens of landscape ecology, emphasizing connections to sustainability, environmental conservation and natural resource management. Field trip may be required. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 5B (GE Area B2 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly LA 220.

courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 5B 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area B2 Sustainability Focused

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: Materials and Techniques of Landscape Construction
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamental materials, assemblies, and methods of landscape construction with an emphasis on sustainable concepts and practices. Introduction to detail development, construction drawing, and fabrication techniques. Field trip required. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly LA 243.
courses.prerequisite: LA 431 or LA 1112.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Related
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Sustainability Related Prerequisite: LA 431 or LA 1112.

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: Introduction to Planting Design
courses.description: Introduction to theories and applied principles of planting design with connections between art and science in landscape design. Focus on California plant communities and introduction to horticultural characteristics and landscape design, the course includes field identification, installation techniques, and maintenance requirements. 1 lecture, 2 activities. Replaced LA 349.
courses.prerequisite: PLSC 233 or PLSC 2234.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: PLSC 233 or PLSC 2234.

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: Site Engineering Techniques and Applications
courses.description: Introduction and application of the techniques, methods, principles and criteria for site engineering and landform design. Includes an introduction to soil science, survey methods, and experiences in the principles, procedures and application of site grading and drainage for landscape architecture. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 2 activities. Formerly LA 241.
courses.prerequisite: LA 431 or LA 1112.
courses.corequisite: One of the following: MATH 118, MATH 1006, MATH 119, or MATH 1007.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: LA 431 or LA 1112. Concurrent: LA 3320. Corequisite: One of the following: MATH 118, MATH 1006, MATH 119, or MATH 1007.

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
courses.description: Fundamental concepts and functions of Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Create, manage, analyze, and display geographically referenced data. Explore how GIS is applied to analyze environmental, social, and natural resource issues. 2 lecture, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as LA/NR 2218. Formerly LA/NR 218.

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: Studio II - Site Based Design
courses.description: Introduction to landscape design at the site scale. Exploration of inventory and analysis methods to generate program outcome statements, design concepts, spatial development and landscape forms for a landscape project. 3 laboratories. Formerly LA 204.
courses.prerequisite: LA 202 or LA 1120 with grade of a C- or better or consent of instructor.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Related
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Sustainability Related Prerequisite: LA 202 or LA 1120 with grade of a C- or better or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: Studio III - Design for Implementation
courses.description: Introduction to concepts and practices of design development and construction documentation. Includes site analysis, design development, site preparation strategies, topographic manipulation, material selection, detail design and construction document preparation. 3 laboratories. Replaced LA 405.
courses.prerequisite: LA 204 or LA 2220 with a grade of C- or better.

courses.description: Examination of methods, process, and meaning in the theory of landscape architecture design. Discussion of major themes of design theory and related fields. Diverse writers, designers and theoretical viewpoints. Analysis of built work and development of theoretical stances. 3 lectures. Formerly LA 320.
courses.prerequisite: LA 212 or LA 1104.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: LA 212 or LA 1104.

courses.subject: LA
courses.title: Contemporary Issues in Cultural Landscapes
courses.description: Investigation of complexities of interrelated cultural theories, practices, and ethical decisions. Examination of shifting changes in social and environmental justice today. Exploration of historical preservation and cultural narrative meaning. Interpretation of personal and cultural values and ethics expressed in the landscape. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly LA 330.

courses.description: Issues related to the practice of landscape architecture, incorporating processes, procedures, and outcomes of professional practice. Professional ethics, business practice and communication, contractual relationships, legal aspects of the profession, cover letter, resume, and portfolio preparation. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly LA 370.

courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: LA 431 or LA 1112; and LA 405 or LA 2222.

courses.prerequisite: LA 431 or LA 1112.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: LA 431 or LA 1112.

courses.title: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Applications for Design Projects
courses.description: Integration and application of GIS skills in landscape architectural planning and design projects. Exploration of the analytical thinking process, visualization of various types of data, and development of site analyses for projects. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 1 lecture, 2 activities. Formerly LA 438.
courses.prerequisite: LA 431 or LA 1112.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: LA 431 or LA 1112. Concurrent: LA 3322. Recommended: LA 220 or LA 2203.

courses.description: Foundation for understanding the world through geographic information as well as the tools available to utilize spatial data. Experience with Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and related technology. Not open to students with credit in GEOG 218, GEOG 2218, LA/NR 218, or LA/NR 2218. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Field trip required. 4 laboratories. Formerly LA 402.

courses.description: Exploration and integration of environmental systems and landscape ecology into planning and design projects. Emphasis is on the interpretation and application of environmental and ecological issues and strategies across a range of scales. Field trip required. 4 laboratories. Formerly LA 403.
courses.prerequisite: LA 405 or LA 2222 with a grade of C- or better or consent of instructor.

Field trip may be required. 1 lecture, 2 discussions. Formerly LA 433.

Formerly LA 436.
courses.prerequisite: LA 437 or LA 3310.

courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: PLSC 233 or PLSC 2234; and LA 349 or LA 2212.

courses.subject: LA

Field trip may be required. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly LA 482.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.description: Structure, development, processing, applications, and control of properties in ceramic and glass materials. Emphasis on application on processing to achieve desired structure and properties. Mechanical, thermal, optical, magnetic, and electrical properties. 3 lectures. Formerly MATE 422.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: MATE 210, MATE 1210, or MATE 1220.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: MATE 210, MATE 1210, or MATE 1220.

courses.description: Types of corrosion, effects of environmental variables on corrosion, and corrosion prevention design. 3 lectures. Formerly MATE 425.

courses.subject: MATE
courses.title: Micro/Nano Fabrication
courses.description: Fabrication science and technology for creating micro and nano scale devices. Unit operations including oxidation, diffusion, ion implantation, etching, chemical and physical vapor deposition, and photolithography. Analyze process physics to design proper steps for electronic/photonic device fabrication. 2 lectures. Crosslisted as BMED/MATE/ME 4434. Formerly BMED 434/EE 423/MATE 430.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BMED 420, BMED 2420, MATE 210, MATE 1210, MATE 1220, EE 306, or EE 3306.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: BMED 420, BMED 2420, MATE 210, MATE 1210, MATE 1220, EE 306, or EE 3306.

courses.subject: MATE
courses.title: Micro/Nano Fabrication Laboratory
courses.description: Application of basic operations involved in microfabrication: cleanroom protocol, oxidation, diffusion, photolithography, etching, and sputtering. Student teams explore process development through fabrication and testing of microscale silicon devices. 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as BMED/MATE/ME 4435. Formerly BMED 435/EE 473/MATE 435.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Corequisite: BMED 434/EE 423/MATE 430 or BMED/MATE/ME 4434.

courses.subject: MATE
courses.title: Welding Metallurgy and Joining of Advanced Materials
courses.description: Materials manufacturing methods that join materials together. Welding, soldering, crimping, riveting, and adhesives. Material compatibility, process flow, and tradeoffs. Structure property processing relationship. Preparation for the American Welding Society (AWS) Certified Welding Inspectors (CWI) welding certification. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly MATE 440.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: IME 142, IME 1142, MATE 210, MATE 1210, or MATE 1220; and MATE 360 or MATE 3360.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: IME 142, IME 1142, MATE 210, MATE 1210, or MATE 1220; and MATE 360 or MATE 3360.

courses.subject: MATE
courses.title: Fracture and Failure Analysis
courses.description: Modes of mechanical failure in metal alloys, polymers, ceramics, and composites. Relationship between mechanical properties, environmental conditions, and microstructure. courses.prerequisite: MATE 360 or MATE 3360.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: MATE 360 or MATE 3360.

courses.title: Combinatorics I
courses.description: Methods of enumerative combinatorics: sum, product, and division rules, mathematical induction, bijective and recursive techniques, inclusion and exclusion, and generating functions. The theory of partitions, the calculus of finite differences, elementary graph theory, designs, and codes. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly MATH 334.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing or Mathematics major; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: MATH 206, MATH 248, MATH 1151, or MATH 2031.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B Prerequisite: Junior standing or Mathematics major; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: MATH 206, MATH 248, MATH 1151, or MATH 2031.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Graph Theory
courses.description: Introduction to graph theory and its applications: isomorphism, paths and searching, connectedness, trees, planarity, graph colorings, matching theory, network flow, graph matrices. Further areas may include the theory of finite state machines, Ramsey theory, spectral theory and extremal theory. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 335.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing, MATH 248, or MATH 2031.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Junior standing, MATH 248, or MATH 2031.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Number Theory
courses.description: The Euclidean algorithm and greatest common divisors. Diophantine equations. Properties of prime numbers. The theory of congruences. Multiplicative functions and Mobius Inversion. Gauss' Law of Quadratic Reciprocity. Historical and modern applications of number theory. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing or Mathematics major; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and MATH 248 or MATH 2031.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP 2026-28 or later: Upper-Div GE Area 2/5 2020-26 catalogs: Upper-Div GE Area B Prerequisite: Junior standing or Mathematics major; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and MATH 248 or MATH 2031.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Linear Algebra
courses.description: Rigorous development of real and complex vector spaces. May include subspaces, bases, direct sums, linear maps, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, diagonalization, inner product spaces, self-adjoint and normal operators, spectral theorems, nilpotent operators, characteristic and minimal polynomials, Cayley-Hamilton Theorem. 4 lectures. Formerly MATH 306.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; and MATH 248 or MATH 2031 with a grade of C- or better.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; and MATH 248 or MATH 2031 with a grade of C- or better.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Linear Algebra Workshop
courses.description: Facilitated study and discussion of the methods and techniques of proof in linear algebra. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 laboratory. Formerly MATH 316.
courses.corequisite: Enrollment in the associated section of MATH 3152.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Corequisite: Enrollment in the associated section of MATH 3152.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Complex Analysis
courses.description: Elementary analytic functions and mappings. Cauchy-Riemann equations. Cauchy's Integral Theorem. Taylor and Laurent series. Theory of residues and evaluation of integrals. Winding number, the argument principle, and Rouche's theorem. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing or Mathematics major; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and MATH 241 or MATH 2263; and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Equations and Boundary Value Problems
courses.description: Linear theory and methods applied to the solution of differential equations. Series solutions and Frobenius theory. Bases and orthogonality in function spaces, Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization. Regular and singular Sturm-Liouville theory. Fourier series and transforms. Special functions of applied mathematics. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly MATH 344.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing or one of the following: Biomedical Engineering major, Mathematics major, or Mechanical Engineering major; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244C, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343; and one of the following: MATH 241, DATA/MATH 1265, or MATH 2263.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Putnam Exam Seminar
courses.description: Directed group study of mathematical problem-solving techniques. Class members are expected to participate in the annual William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition. Credit/No Credit grading only. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 seminar. Formerly MATH 370.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Math Modeling Seminar
courses.description: Directed group study of mathematical modeling techniques. Class members are expected to participate in the annual Mathematical Competition in Modeling. Credit/No Credit grading only. Repeatable up to 8 units. 2 seminars. Formerly MATH 371.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics for Elementary Teaching I
courses.description: Introduction to reasoning about quantities, numeration, number sense, meaning of rational numbers, and operations on whole numbers, fractions and decimals. Algebraic reasoning related to early elementary mathematics including operations. 4 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: Liberal Studies major; junior standing, LS 230, or LS 2230; and completion of GE Area 2 (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Liberal Studies major; junior standing, LS 230, or LS 2230; and completion of GE Area 2 (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics for Elementary Teaching II
courses.description: Introduction to number theory including prime numbers, composite numbers, and divisibility. The relationship between ratios, rates, and proportions. Problem solving using proportional reasoning. Algebraic reasoning related to patterns and to linear, quadratic, and exponential functions. 4 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 3481 with a grade of C- or better.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: MATH 3481 with a grade of C- or better.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics for Elementary Teaching III
courses.description: Introduction to measurement, congruence and similarity, transformational geometry, polygons and polyhedra. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 3482 with a grade of C- or better.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: MATH 3482 with a grade of C- or better.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Euclidean Geometry
courses.description: Foundations of Euclidean geometry, including constructions, congruence theorems, similarity, polygonal regions, circles, measurement and properties of angles. Includes history of the parallel postulate and principles of neutral geometry. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 442.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 248 or MATH 2031 with a grade of C- or better, or consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MATH 248 or MATH 2031 with a grade of C- or better, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics of Data Science
courses.description: Introduction to mathematical foundations of data science including regression, data dimension reduction, clustering, community detection, and computational topology, with a focus on advanced linear algebra tools needed to establish the mathematical foundations of methods, to show convergence, and for error minimization. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as DATA/MATH 3622.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; MATH 248 or MATH 2031; and CSC 101 or CSC 1001.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; MATH 248 or MATH 2031; and CSC 101 or CSC 1001.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Numerical Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to basic numerical methods including finite precision arithmetic and error propagation, root-finding methods, interpolation, numerical differentiation and quadrature, direct and iterative methods for systems of linear equations, and numerical methods for eigenvalue problems and data fitting. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 451.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343; and one of the following: MATH 241, DATA/MATH 1265, or MATH 2263; and CSC 101 or CSC 1001.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343; and one of the following: MATH 241, DATA/MATH 1265, or MATH 2263; and CSC 101 or CSC 1001.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Typesetting with LaTeX
courses.description: Preparing documents, especially mathematical ones, using the LaTeX typesetting software. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 lecture. Formerly MATH 351.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Programming
courses.description: Symbolic and numerical mathematical algorithms. Recursive problem solving. Formulation of mathematical conjectures from data. Assessment of conjectures using generated data. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 350.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; and one of the following: MATH 241, DATA/MATH 1265 or MATH 2263; and CSC 101 or CSC 1001.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; and one of the following: MATH 241, DATA/MATH 1265 or MATH 2263; and CSC 101 or CSC 1001.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Technology in Mathematics Education
courses.description: Examination of current technologies designed for teaching and exploring mathematics. Exploration of mathematics content and problem solving with technology. Consideration of what mathematics content is appropriate for incorporating technology. Emphasis on activity learning and applications. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 300.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 248 or MATH 2031.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: MATH 248 or MATH 2031.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Combinatorics II
courses.description: Methods of discrete mathematics. Formal power series and generating functions, the exponential formula, integer partitions, permutation statistics, q-analogues, Polya theory, posets, Möbius inversion. Additional concepts may include asymptotics, Lagrange inversion, symmetric functions, rook theory, hypergeometric series, the probabilistic method. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 435.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 334, or MATH 3051.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 334, or MATH 3051.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Abstract Algebra I
courses.description: Introduction to the study of groups and rings. Permutation groups, cyclic and dihedral groups, Lagrange's theorem, conjugation, quotient groups, isomorphism theorems, and automorphisms; basic ring types, ring homomorphisms, ideals, quotients, prime and maximal ideals, factorization in commutative rings. 4 lectures. Formerly offered as part of the MATH 481, 482, 483 series, students may not earn credit for both MATH 481 and MATH 4201.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 306, MATH 341, MATH 3111, or MATH 3152.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 306, MATH 341, MATH 3111, or MATH 3152.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Abstract Algebra II
courses.description: Introduction to field theory. Factorization in polynomial rings, field extensions and Kronecker's theorem, splitting fields, finite fields, Galois groups and Galois field extensions, fundamental theorem of Galois theory. 3 lectures. Formerly offered as part of the MATH 481, 482, 483 series, students may not earn credit for both MATH 483 and MATH 4202.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 482 or MATH 4201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MATH 482 or MATH 4201.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Abstract Algebra I Workshop
courses.description: Facilitated study and discussion of the methods and techniques of proof in abstract algebra. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 laboratory. Formerly MATH 491.
courses.corequisite: Enrollment in the associated section of MATH 4201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Corequisite: Enrollment in the associated section of MATH 4201.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Real Analysis I
courses.description: Introduction to concepts and methods basic to real analysis. Concepts may include the real number system, sequences, continuity, differentiation and Riemann integration of functions of a single real variable. 4 lectures. Formerly offered as part of the MATH 412, 413, 414 series, students may not earn credit for both MATH 412 and MATH 4264.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 306, or MATH 3152.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 306, or MATH 3152.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Real Analysis II
courses.description: Further introduction to concepts and methods basic to real analysis. Concepts may include sequences and series of functions, differentiability of functions of several variables, Implicit and/or Inverse Function theorems, Riemann integration in several variables, and other advanced topics in real analysis. 4 lectures. Formerly offered as part of the MATH 412, 413, 414 series, students may not earn credit for both MATH 414 and MATH 4265.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 413 or MATH 4264.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MATH 413 or MATH 4264.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Real Analysis I Workshop
courses.description: Facilitated study and discussion of the methods and techniques of proof in real analysis. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 laboratory. Formerly MATH 422.
courses.corequisite: Enrollment in the associated section of MATH 4264.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Corequisite: Enrollment in the associated section of MATH 4264.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Nonlinear Dynamical Systems
courses.description: Qualitative theory of ordinary differential equations: Existence and Uniqueness Theorem, phase portraits, limit sets, stability of fixed points and periodic orbits, energy functions, Poincare-Bendixson Theorem, Poincare maps, bifurcations, attractors, chaos. Not open to students with credit in PHYS 428 or PHYS 4428. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 416.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343, and one of the following: MATH 241, DATA/MATH 1265, or MATH 2263; or graduate standing in Mathematics.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343, and one of the following: MATH 241, DATA/MATH 1265, or MATH 2263; or graduate standing in Mathematics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: Introduction to partial differential equations. Transport equations, wave equation, heat equation, and Laplace's equation. The D'Alembert solution to the wave equation, method of characteristics, Green's functions, the maximum principle, separation of variables, Fourier series/transforms, and operator eigenvalue problems. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 418.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics or MATH 3351.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics or MATH 3351.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Problems for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of special problems. Repeatable up to 6 units. Formerly MATH 400.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of department chair.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Teaching Mathematics in Secondary School
courses.description: Research-based methods of teaching and learning mathematics in secondary schools with an emphasis on planning instruction and designing effective assessment and learning experiences for all students. Introduction to current issues in mathematics education. For students who will be teaching in secondary schools. Credit/No Credit grading only. 4 lectures. Formerly MATH 424.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into the Mathematics Single Subject Credential Program or consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: Admission into the Mathematics Single Subject Credential Program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics Teaching Clinical Experience Seminar
courses.description: Principles and practice in effective teaching of mathematics at the secondary level, learning theories, curriculum content and structure, classroom issues, and the teaching profession. Credit/No Credit grading. 2 seminars. Formerly MATH 425.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into the Single Subject Mathematics Credential Program.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Admission into the Single Subject Mathematics Credential Program. Corequisite: EDUC 469 or EDUC 4469.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Senior Project I
courses.description: Selection and development of a capstone mathematics project under direct faculty supervision. Formerly MATH 461.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Senior standing.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Senior Project II
courses.description: Completion of a capstone mathematics project under direct faculty supervision. Project results are presented in a formal report. Formerly MATH 462.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 461 or MATH 4461.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: MATH 461 or MATH 4461.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Senior Project Seminar
courses.description: Written and oral analysis and presentation of topics in advanced mathematics. This capstone course in mathematics involves work in a range of mathematical fields, including linear algebra, number theory, graph theory, abstract algebra, and analysis. Not open to students with credit in MATH 460 or MATH 4464. 3 seminars. Formerly MATH 459.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 412, MATH 481, MATH 4201, or MATH 4264.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 412, MATH 481, MATH 4201, or MATH 4264.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Senior Project Applied Seminar
courses.description: Written and oral analysis and presentation of topics in applied mathematics and mathematical modeling. Construct and analyze mathematical models using a range of mathematical fields, including linear algebra, differential equations, numerical analysis, dynamical systems, and data analytics. Not open to students with credit in MATH 459 or MATH 4463. 3 seminars. Formerly MATH 460.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CSC 101, CSC 1001, MATH 350, or MATH 3681; and MATH 306 or MATH 3152; and MATH 344 or MATH 3351.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: CSC 101, CSC 1001, MATH 350, or MATH 3681; and MATH 306 or MATH 3152; and MATH 344 or MATH 3351.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 470.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Seminar in Mathematics
courses.description: Exploration of advanced topics and problems in mathematics through reading, writing and oral presentations. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Credit/No Credit grading only. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 seminar. Formerly MATH 474.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 306 or MATH 3152; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Prerequisite: MATH 306 or MATH 3152; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Cooperative Education Experience
courses.description: Part-time work experience in business, industry, government, and other areas of student career interest. Positions are paid and usually require relocation. Formal report and evaluation by work supervisor required. Repeatable up to 8 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly MATH 485.
courses.prerequisite: Sophomore standing and consent of department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Prerequisite: Sophomore standing and consent of department chair.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Cooperative Education Experience
courses.description: Full-time work experience in business, industry, government, and other areas of student career interest. Positions are paid and usually require relocation. Formal report and evaluation by work supervisor required. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly MATH 495.
courses.prerequisite: Sophomore standing and consent of department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Prerequisite: Sophomore standing and consent of department chair.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Non-Euclidean Geometry
courses.description: Non-Euclidean geometries, including spherical, hyperbolic, and projective geometry. Properties of geodesics, parallels, biangles, Saccheri and Lambert quadrilaterals, angle-sum, area, Pythagorean Theorem, trigonometry, duality, perspectivity, and fundamental theorems. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 443.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 442, or MATH 3511.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 442, or MATH 3511.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Geometry
courses.description: The theory of curves and surfaces in Euclidean space. May include curvature and torsion of curves, Frenet formulas, covariant derivatives, Cartan structural equations, shape operator, curvature of surfaces, geodesics, Gauss-Bonnet Theorem, and geometric surfaces. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 404.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 241 or MATH 2263, and one of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; or graduate standing in Mathematics.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: MATH 241 or MATH 2263, and one of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; or graduate standing in Mathematics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Topology
courses.description: Introduction to topological spaces. Metric spaces, open and closed sets, continuity, compactness, connectedness. Quotient spaces. Covering spaces and the fundamental group. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 440.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 412, or MATH 4264.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 412, or MATH 4264. Corequisite: MATH 481 or MATH 4201.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Differential Equations
courses.description: Finite-difference methods for boundary-value problems described by ordinary and elliptic partial differential equations. Numerical methods for initial-value problems described by ordinary differential equations and systems thereof. Finite-difference methods for initial-boundary-value problems described by parabolic and hyperbolic partial differential equations. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 452.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 451, or MATH 3651.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 451, or MATH 3651. Recommended: MATH 344 or MATH 3351.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Optimization
courses.description: Algorithms for solving constrained and unconstrained optimization problems. Line searches, gradient methods, Newton's method; conjugate gradient, backpropagation, and global search methods. Linear programming and nonlinear constrained optimization methods including simplex and non-simplex methods. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 453.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 451, or MATH 3651.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 451, or MATH 3651. Recommended: MATH 306 or MATH 3152.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Game Theory
courses.description: Mathematical concepts, techniques, and models used to investigate strategies in competitive situations, matrix games, linear programming, nonzero sum games, evolutionarily stable systems, indices of power, Nash arbitration. May include multiplayer games, fair division, and combinatorial game theory. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 437.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 248 or MATH 2031, and one of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; or graduate standing in Mathematics.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MATH 248 or MATH 2031, and one of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; or graduate standing in Mathematics.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Mathematics for Teaching
courses.description: Advanced exploration of the mathematics taught in California's public high schools and middle schools through problem analysis, concept analysis, and problem connections. Introduction to mathematics education research. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 423.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 442 or MATH 3511; and MATH 481 or MATH 4201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MATH 442 or MATH 3511; and MATH 481 or MATH 4201.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Mathematics
courses.description: Exploration of advanced topics and problems in mathematics. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 475.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 306, or MATH 3152; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 306, or MATH 3152; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Applied Mathematics
courses.description: Exploration of advanced topics and problems in applied mathematics. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 476.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 306, or MATH 3152; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 306, or MATH 3152; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Transition to Graduate Mathematics
courses.description: Interactive construction and analysis of mathematical proof and exposition at the graduate level. Concepts drawn from standard advanced material in real analysis, linear algebra, and modern algebra. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 lecture, 2 seminars. Formerly MATH 548.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Discrete Mathematics
courses.description: Advanced discrete mathematics. Concepts may include the representation theory of the symmetric group, tableaux combinatorics, the RSK algorithm, lattice paths, extremal combinatorics, hypergeometric series algorithms and proof machines, expander families of graphs, Ramsey theory, or finite state machines. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 530.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing, MATH 435, or MATH 4052.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing, MATH 435, or MATH 4052.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra and Module Theory
courses.description: Modules, basic theorems, products and coproducts via universal properties, free modules, and modules over a PID. Applications to linear operators, bilinear forms, corresponding matrix groups; spectral theorems for Hermitian, normal, and unitary operators. Singular values, applications, and introduction to categories. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 560.
courses.prerequisite: Completion of the Graduate Written Examination in Algebra.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Completion of the Graduate Written Examination in Algebra.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebra
courses.description: Action of a group on a set, semi-direct products, solvable groups, p-groups, Sylow theorems, classification of groups of small order, group presentations, finitely generated abelian groups, matrix groups, and advanced concepts. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: Completion of the Graduate Written Exam in Algebra.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Completion of the Graduate Written Exam in Algebra.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Real Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to measure and integration, Lebesgue measure, Lebesgue integration, convergence theorems, Fubini's Theorem and the Radon-Nikodym Theorem. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 550.
courses.prerequisite: Completion of the Graduate Written Examination in Analysis.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Completion of the Graduate Written Examination in Analysis.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Applied Complex Analysis
courses.description: Complex variables and associated topics. Branch cuts, series and product expansions. Asymptotic evaluation of integrals. Conformal mapping; applications and examples. Fourier and Laplace transforms and applications. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 520.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 410, or MATH 3301.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 410, or MATH 3301.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Methods of Applied Mathematics
courses.description: Advanced mathematical methods of analysis in science and engineering, integrated with modeling of physical phenomena. Asymptotics, perturbation methods, and boundary layer analysis. Additional content to be drawn from WKB theory, multi-scale analysis, and the calculus of variations. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 521.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 410, MATH 412, MATH 3301, or MATH 4264.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 410, MATH 412, MATH 3301, or MATH 4264.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Individual Study
courses.description: Individual research or advanced study planned and completed under the direction of a departmental faculty member. Open only to graduate students demonstrating ability to do independent work. Repeatable up to 9 units. Formerly MATH 500.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics and consent of department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics and consent of department chair.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Topology
courses.description: General topological spaces with an emphasis on surfaces and manifolds. Concepts may include fundamental groups and covering spaces, simplicial and singular homology, and differential topology. 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 541.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 440, or MATH 4541.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics, MATH 440, or MATH 4541.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for graduate students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly MATH 570.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: Built around topics in advanced mathematics chosen according to the common interests and needs of the students enrolled. Each seminar will have a subtitle according to the nature of the content. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 9 units. 1 to 3 seminars. Formerly MATH 580.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Comprehensive Examination
courses.description: Culminating oral exam for a non-thesis master's student in mathematics showing integration of knowledge, critical and independent thinking, and mastery of the subject matter. Scheduled with the faculty advisor, typically in the final semester of the graduate program. Credit/No Credit grading only.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics and consent of department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mathematics and consent of department chair.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: Serious research endeavor devoted to the development, pedagogy or learning of mathematics. Repeatable up to 5 units. Formerly MATH 599.
