courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Senior Design Project II
courses.description: Completion of a two-semester team design project. Product realization, including material procurement, prototyping, and testing. Professional skills, including communication, teamwork, project management, and ethics. 2 laboratories. Formerly ME 429.
courses.prerequisite: ME 428 or ME 4460.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: ME 428 or ME 4460.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Experimental Methods in Mechanical Engineering
courses.description: Offered at Solano Campus. Principles and applications of experiments in fluid mechanics, material science, mechanics, and thermodynamics. Technical communication, both oral and written, of the entire experimental process. 2 lectures. Formerly ME 462 at Cal Maritime.
courses.prerequisite: ENG 112 or ENG 1112; ME 332 or ME 3332; ME 340 or ME 3340; and ME 360 or ME 3360.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ENG 112 or ENG 1112; ME 332 or ME 3332; ME 340 or ME 3340; and ME 360 or ME 3360. Concurrent: ME 462L or ME 4462L.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Experimental Methods in Mechanical Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Offered at Solano Campus. Laboratory supporting Experimental Methods in Mechanical Engineering. 1 activity. Formerly ME 462L at Cal Maritime.
courses.prerequisite: ENG 112 or ENG 1112; ME 332 or ME 3332; ME 340 or ME 3340; and ME 360 or ME 3360.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ENG 112 or ENG 1112; ME 332 or ME 3332; ME 340 or ME 3340; and ME 360 or ME 3360. Concurrent: ME 462 or ME 4462.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: HVAC&R Senior Design Project I
courses.description: First semester of a two-semester sequence. Team projects designing sustainable heating, ventilating, air-conditioning, and refrigeration (HVAC&R) systems. New developments, policies, and practices in the HVAC&R industry. Ethics for engineers. 1 lecture, 1 laboratory. Formerly ME 459.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing.
courses.corequisite: ME 343 or ME 3343; and ME 456 or ME 4456.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Senior standing. Corequisite: ME 343 or ME 3343; and ME 456 or ME 4456.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: HVAC&R Senior Design Project II
courses.description: Continuation of senior project. Team project designing sustainable heating, ventilating, air-conditioning and refrigeration (HVAC&R) systems. 2 laboratories. Formerly ME 460.
courses.prerequisite: ME 459 or ME 4465.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ME 459 or ME 4465.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 1 to 4 lectures. Formerly ME 470.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Advanced Laboratory
courses.description: Directed group laboratory study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 to 2 laboratories. Formerly ME 471.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Composite Materials Analysis and Design
courses.description: Behavior of unidirectional fiber composites. Properties of short-fiber composites and orthotropic lamina. Analysis of laminated composites. Strength and hygrothermal behavior of composite materials, sandwich structure, and structural optimization using Finite Element Analysis. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ME 412.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: AERO 331, AERO 3331, ME 328, or ME 3328.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: AERO 331, AERO 3331, ME 328, or ME 3328. Recommended: ME 4380.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Cooperative Education Experience
courses.description: Work experience in business, industry, government, and other areas of student career interest. Positions are paid and usually require relocation and registration in course for one to two consecutive semesters. Formal report and evaluation by work supervisor required. Credit/No Credit grading only. Repeatable up to 12 units. Formerly ME 493.
courses.prerequisite: Sophomore standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Prerequisite: Sophomore standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Wind Power Engineering
courses.description: Engineering aspects of wind power systems including mechanical design, support structure design, aerodynamic analysis, wind field analysis, system concepts and analysis, and economics. Field trip may be required. 3 lectures. Formerly ME 488.
courses.prerequisite: ME 341 or ME 3341.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ME 341 or ME 3341.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Engineering Design Process
courses.description: Offered at Solano Campus. Introduction to the engineering design processes. Identifying objectives and constraints, generating concepts, background research including finding appropriate engineering standards, application of analytical and numerical models for design, evaluating design alternatives, and communication of work to a wide range of audiences. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 1C (GE Area A1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ME 490 at Cal Maritime.
courses.prerequisite: ENG 112 or ENG 1112; ME 332 or ME 3332; ME 340 or ME 3340; and ME 360 or ME 3360.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 1C 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area A1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 1C 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area A1 Prerequisite: ENG 112 or ENG 1112; ME 332 or ME 3332; ME 340 or ME 3340; and ME 360 or ME 3360.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Project Design I
courses.description: Offered at Solano Campus. First of two courses taken sequentially in the application of engineering design principles. Study and application of techniques including problem definition, concept generation, and decision making. Practice of skills including written and oral communication, teamwork, ethics, and demonstrating societal and/or environmental responsibility. 2 lectures. Formerly ME 492 at Cal Maritime.
courses.prerequisite: ME 490 or ME 4490.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ME 490 or ME 4490. Concurrent: ME 492L or ME 4492L.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Project Design I Lab
courses.description: Offered at Solano Campus. group laboratory with technical advisors for projects in Project Design I. 1 laboratory. Formerly ME 492L at Cal Maritime.
courses.prerequisite: ME 490 or ME 4490.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ME 490 or ME 4490. Concurrent: ME 492 or ME 4492.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Project Design II
courses.description: Offered at Solano Campus. Second of two courses taken sequentially in the application of engineering design principles. Study and application of techniques including prototyping and testing. Practice of skills including written and oral communication, teamwork, ethics, and demonstrating societal and/or environmental responsibility. 2 lectures. Formerly ME 494 at Cal Maritime.
courses.prerequisite: ME 492 or ME 4492.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ME 492 or ME 4492. Concurrent: ME 494L or ME 4494L.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Project Design II Lab
courses.description: Offered at Solano Campus. Directed group laboratory with technical advisors for projects in Project Design II. 1 laboratory. Formerly ME 494L at Cal Maritime.
courses.prerequisite: ME 492 or ME 4492.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ME 492 or ME 4492. Concurrent: ME 494 or ME 4494.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Cooperative Education Experience
courses.description: Work experience in business, industry, government, and other areas of student career interest. Positions are paid and usually require relocation and registration in course for one to two consecutive semesters. A more fully developed formal report and evaluation by work supervisor required. Credit/No Credit grading only. Repeatable up to 24 units. Formerly ME 495.
courses.prerequisite: Sophomore standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD CR/NC Prerequisite: Sophomore standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Mechatronics III
courses.description: Application of principles of high-level design to mechanical control system implementation. Design printed circuit boards as system components. Use modified state transition logic in conjunction with object-oriented programming as design methodology. Real-time programming for control of mechanical systems. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ME 507.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Individual Study
courses.description: Advanced study planned and completed under the direction of a member of the department faculty. Enrollment by petition. Repeatable up to 8 units. Formerly ME 500.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of department chair, graduate advisor, and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Consent of department chair, graduate advisor, and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Continuum Mechanics and Elasticity
courses.description: Introduction to continuum mechanics. Kinematics, stress, and balance laws. Constitutive theory for isotropic and anisotropic solids and viscous fluids. Applications including design of beams and pressure vessels, stress concentrations, fiber-reinforced composites, and non-homogeneous biological materials. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as CE 5511/ME 5501. Formerly CE 511/ME 501.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Graduate standing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Inelastic Stress Analysis
courses.description: Perfectly plastic and work hardening materials. Von Mises and Tresca yield, isotropic and kinematic hardening flow rules, and boundary-value problems. Finite elasticity, including kinematics, Cauchy- and Green-elasticity, invariance, constraints, Neo-Hookean and Mooney-Rivlin materials, experimental approaches, anisotropic and fiber reinforced materials, boundary-value problems, stability and strain energy convexity, and viscoelasticity. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as CE 5513/ME 5503. Formerly CE 513/ME 503.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CE 511, CE 5511, ME 501, or ME 5501.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: CE 511, CE 5511, ME 501, or ME 5501.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Finite Element Analysis of Continua
courses.description: Finite element theory and application with a focus on numerical implementation. Strong and weak forms, variational theorems, displacement based methods, mixed methods, viscoelasticity and plasticity type formulations, augmented Lagrangian formulations, transient and modal analysis, and finite deformation. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as AERO/BMED/CE/ME 5504. Formerly CE/ME 504.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BMED/CE/ME 404, BMED/CE/ME 4404, CE 501, CE 5502, AERO 431, or AERO 4431.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: BMED/CE/ME 404, BMED/CE/ME 4404, CE 501, CE 5502, AERO 431, or AERO 4431.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: System Dynamics
courses.description: Unified approach for mathematical modeling and analysis of dynamic physical systems which may store energy in multiple energy domains. Emphasis on developing lumped-parameter linear system models from a set of primitive elements in a systematic manner. 3 lectures. Formerly ME 506.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Vibrations
courses.description: Vibration of complex engineering systems. Inertia and stiffness matrices. Natural frequencies and normal modes. Approximate solutions and computer techniques. Response to transient and periodic inputs. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ME 517.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: ME 318, ME 3317, or ME 3318; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: ME 318, ME 3317, or ME 3318; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Machinery Vibration and Rotor Dynamics
courses.description: Vibrations of rotating machinery. Modeling of structural rotor dynamic phenomena induced by shaft flexibility and bearings. Laboratory measurement of rotor dynamic response and interpretation of machinery diagnostic information. Practical research projects. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ME 518.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Viscous Flow
courses.description: Introduction to tensor calculus, development of Reynolds' Transport Theory, special forms of governing equations of fluid motion, and classical solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations. 3 lectures. Formerly ME 540.
courses.prerequisite: ME 341 or ME 3341; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ME 341 or ME 3341; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Advanced Thermodynamics
courses.description: Selected modern applications of thermodynamics that may include equilibrium and kinetics as applied to combustion and air pollution, analysis and evaluation of techniques used to predict properties of gases and liquids, improvement of modern thermodynamic cycles by second law analysis. 3 lectures. Formerly ME 541.
courses.prerequisite: ME 448 or ME 4440; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ME 448 or ME 4440; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Dynamics and Thermodynamics of Compressible Flow
courses.description: Control volume analysis of fluid-thermo equations for one-dimensional, compressible flow involving area change, normal shocks, friction, and heat transfer. Two-dimensional supersonic flow, including linearization, method of characteristics, and oblique shocks. One-dimensional constant area, unsteady flow. 3 lectures. Formerly ME 542.
courses.prerequisite: ME 303 or ME 3302; and ME 341 or ME 3341; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ME 303 or ME 3302; and ME 341 or ME 3341; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Conduction and Radiation Heat Transfer
courses.description: Advanced principles of conduction and radiation heat transfer. Classical solution techniques to problems in conduction and radiation. 3 lectures. Formerly ME 552.
courses.prerequisite: ME 343 or ME 3343; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: ME 343 or ME 3343; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Convective Heat Transfer
courses.description: Advanced principles of convective heat transfer. Classical solution techniques to problems in convection. 3 lectures. Formerly ME 553.
courses.prerequisite: ME 347 or ME 3342; and ME 343 or ME 3343; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ME 347 or ME 3342; and ME 343 or ME 3343; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Computational Heat Transfer
courses.description: Numerical solutions of classical, industrial, and experimental problems with conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ME 554.
courses.prerequisite: ME 341 or ME 3341; and ME 343 or ME 3343; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: ME 341 or ME 3341; and ME 343 or ME 3343; or graduate standing. Recommended: MATH 418 or MATH 4352.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Graduate Seminar
courses.description: Current developments in mechanical engineering are presented by guest speakers. Participation is by graduate students, faculty, and guests. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 seminar. Formerly ME 563.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mechanical Engineering.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: Graduate standing in Mechanical Engineering.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 1 to 4 lectures. Formerly ME 570.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Special Advanced Laboratory
courses.description: Directed group laboratory study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 to 2 laboratories. Formerly ME 571.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Fluid Power Control
courses.description: Design, analysis, and control of fluid power systems. Analysis of fluid power system components such as pumps, valves, and actuators. Dynamic system modeling, analysis of system response, stability, and controller design. Computer simulation and laboratory experimentation. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly ME 579.
courses.prerequisite: one of the following: ME 418, ME 419, ME 4417, or ME 4419; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: one of the following: ME 418, ME 419, ME 4417, or ME 4419; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Failure Analysis of Advanced Composite Materials
courses.description: Behavior of advanced composite structures, failure analysis, and damage development. Plate and beam, buckling, impact, vibration of laminated plates, and sandwich structures. Fatigue behavior and optimum design of pressure vessels. Hygrothermal fatigue and residual stresses. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: AERO 331, AERO 3331, ME 328, or ME 3328; or graduate standing.
courses.recommended: One of the following: ME 161, ME 412, ME 4380, or ME 4480.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: AERO 331, AERO 3331, ME 328, or ME 3328; or graduate standing. Recommended: One of the following: ME 161, ME 412, ME 4380, or ME 4480.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Comprehensive Examination
courses.description: For the course option for the Master of Science degree in Mechanical Engineering, students must enroll in this course during the semester they take the culminating exam to meet the degree requirements. Credit/No Credit grading only.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: ME
courses.title: Thesis
courses.description: Individual research or activity under faculty supervision as a requirement for the master's degree, culminating in a written report/thesis. Repeatable up to 6 units. Formerly ME 599.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Orientation to Marine Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to Marine Sciences faculty, the Biology Department and campus resources, research opportunities, possible careers, studying science, and current topics in marine sciences. Field trip may be required. Credit/No credit grading only. 1 lecture. Formerly MSCI 100.
courses.prerequisite: Marine Sciences major.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: Marine Sciences major.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: The Oceans
courses.description: Introduction to biological, chemical, geological, and physical features and processes of Earth's oceans. Survey of marine biodiversity, organismal adaptations and ecological significance. Focus on select marine and coastal ecosystems. Interaction between humans and sea (climate change, ocean acidification, pollution, overfishing). Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 5B (GE Area B2 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly MSCI 111.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 5B 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area B2 Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SU 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 5B 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area B2 Sustainability Focused

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: The Oceans Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on exploration of the physical and chemical properties of seawater and how they influence biology within the ocean. Explore oceanographic principles, create and interpret figures and data, and examine the ocean as a part of the Earth's systems and cycles. Field trip required. 1 laboratory.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Corequisite: MSCI 111 or MSCI 1111.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Marine Ecology
courses.description: Introduction to the ecology of marine organisms and the processes that underlie their patterns of distribution and abundance in open oceans, coastal regions, and estuaries. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 2 laboratories. Formerly MSCI 300.
courses.prerequisite: BIO 150 or BIO 1150; BIO 161 or BIO 1151; and one of the following: BIO 263, BIO 2253, MSCI 111, or MSCI 1111.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: BIO 150 or BIO 1150; BIO 161 or BIO 1151; and one of the following: BIO 263, BIO 2253, MSCI 111, or MSCI 1111. Recommended: STAT 218 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Biological Oceanography
courses.description: Interdisciplinary study of marine organisms, how they interact with each other and their physical, chemical, and geological environment. Emphasis on how these interactions impact abundance, diversity, and temporal and spatial distributions. 3 lectures. Formerly MSCI 301.
courses.prerequisite: BIO 150 or BIO 1150; BIO 161 or BIO 1151; CHEM 124, CHEM 127, or CHEM 1120; CHEM 125, CHEM 128, or CHEM 1122; MSCI 300 or MSCI 1111 and MSCI 1112; and PSC 201 or PSC 2201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: BIO 150 or BIO 1150; BIO 161 or BIO 1151; CHEM 124, CHEM 127, or CHEM 1120; CHEM 125, CHEM 128, or CHEM 1122; MSCI 300 or MSCI 1111 and MSCI 1112; and PSC 201 or PSC 2201. Recommended: STAT 218 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Ocean Technologies and Data
courses.description: Overview of ocean data sensors and technologies. Introduction to scientific computing and data analysis techniques in oceanography, ocean observing systems and data portals, data visualization, time series methods, and spatial data analysis. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 activity.
courses.prerequisite: PSC 201 or PSC 2201; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: PSC 201 or PSC 2201; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Marine Mammals, Birds, and Reptiles
courses.description: Introduction to the biology, ecology, and evolution of mammals, birds, and/or reptiles of the marine environment, including diversity patterns, evolutionary relationships, adaptations to the ocean, and conservation issues, with an emphasis on Central California species. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly MSCI 324.
courses.prerequisite: BIO 150 or BIO 1150; and BIO 161 or BIO 1151.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: BIO 150 or BIO 1150; and BIO 161 or BIO 1151. Recommended: STAT 218 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Marine Science Outreach
courses.description: Volunteer or internship experience in a marine science business, industry, government agency or informal science center. Positions require communicating science to the public. Formal report and evaluation by work supervisor required. Field trip required. Repeatable up to 5 units. Credit/No credit grading only. Formerly MSCI 401.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; one of the following: MSCI 300, MSCI 301, MSCI 3300, MSCI 3301, PSC 201, or PSC 2201; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Junior standing; one of the following: MSCI 300, MSCI 301, MSCI 3300, MSCI 3301, PSC 201, or PSC 2201; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Field Oceanography
courses.description: Advanced exploration of coastal ocean ecosystems. Focus on oceanographic field work, including trips to local marine ecosystems and hands-on laboratory investigations. Integration of biological, chemical, physical, and geological observations to gain a holistic understanding of oceanography. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 2 laboratories. Formerly MSCI 403.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: CHEM 302, CHEM 3370, MSCI 301, or MSCI 3301; MSCI 300 or MSCI 1111 and MSCI 1112; and PSC 201 or PSC 2201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: One of the following: CHEM 302, CHEM 3370, MSCI 301, or MSCI 3301; MSCI 300 or MSCI 1111 and MSCI 1112; and PSC 201 or PSC 2201.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Scientific Diving
courses.description: Professional diver training with a focus on scientific methodology and underwater sampling techniques. Satisfies standards of American Academy of Underwater Sciences. Combination of theory, techniques and scuba diving. Experience collecting data and handling scientific equipment underwater. To enroll in the course, student must have an open water diving certificate, first aid and CRP certification, a current diving medical exam, scuba equipment service documentation, medical insurance that covers hyperbaric oxygen treatment for injured divers, and an application for the course. Additional fees required. Field trip required. 1 laboratory, 1 activity. Formerly MSCI 410.
courses.prerequisite: MSCI 111 or MSCI 1111; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SU Prerequisite: MSCI 111 or MSCI 1111; and consent of instructor. Recommended: MSCI 300 or MSCI 3300.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Marine Botany
courses.description: Comprehensive examination of the ecology, life histories, functional morphology, physiology, and taxonomy of marine algae and marine plants. Laboratory emphasizes species endemic to the central coast of California. Field trip required. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly MSCI 437.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BIO 263, BIO 2253, MSCI 300, or MSCI 3300; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: BIO 263, BIO 2253, MSCI 300, or MSCI 3300; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Aquaculture
courses.description: Propagation and rearing of fishes, invertebrates, and algae from marine, freshwater, and estuarine habitats. Global perspectives including aquaculture development and current status in developed and developing countries for food production. Current culture methodologies and examination of system design constraints. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as BRAE/MSCI 4438. Formerly MSCI 438.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BIO 263, BIO 2253, BRAE 220, BRAE 2220, MSCI 300, or MSCI 3300.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: One of the following: BIO 263, BIO 2253, BRAE 220, BRAE 2220, MSCI 300, or MSCI 3300.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Marine Fisheries and Conservation
courses.description: Scientific investigation of the management and conservation of marine fisheries and ecosystems. Integration of ecology, oceanography, socio-economic, and political science disciplines using field, wet-lab, and analytical/computational methods to assess and achieve sustainable fisheries and healthy ecosystems in the ocean. Field trip required. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly MSCI 439.
courses.prerequisite: MSCI 300 or MSCI 3300; or graduate standing.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: MSCI 300 or MSCI 3300; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: MSCI
courses.title: Communicating Ocean Sciences to Informal Audiences
courses.description: Development of knowledge of ocean sciences and advanced educational approaches for communicating that knowledge. Teaching skills developed through coursework, outreach events and collaborative projects. Present ocean-themed inquiry-based science exhibits to improve scientific literacy of audiences of all ages. Field trip required. 1 lecture, 2 activities. Formerly MSCI 440.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 5B (GE Area B2 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: BIO 211, BIO 322, BIO 336, BIO 3210, BIO 3322, BIO 3326, MSCI 300, MSCI 3300, PSC 201, or PSC 2201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 5B (GE Area B2 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: BIO 211, BIO 322, BIO 336, BIO 3210, BIO 3322, BIO 3326, MSCI 300, MSCI 3300, PSC 201, or PSC 2201.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Foundation of Officership I
courses.description: Introduction to issues and competencies of the Army officer profession. Stereotypes about the military, the role of the Army officer, customs and traditions within the military, and personal and physical development. Not open to students with credit in MSL 212 or MSL 2212. 1 lecture. Formerly MSL 101.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Foundation of Officership II
courses.description: The role of leadership within a large organization. Definition of leadership, leadership framework, individual and organizational core values, and the moral responsibility of leadership. Not open to students with credit in MSL 212 or MSL 2212. 1 lecture. Formerly MSL 102.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Basic Exercises in Military Leadership
courses.description: Small-unit military operations. Incorporation of the military decision-making process in the planning, execution and conducting of a wide variety of squad, platoon, and company sized missions. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly MSL 110.
courses.prerequisite: Enrollment in any MSL course or consent of department head.
courses.recommended: Concurrent enrollment in MSL 1101, MSL 1102, MSL 2201, or MSL 2202.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Enrollment in any MSL course or consent of department head. Recommended: Concurrent enrollment in MSL 1101, MSL 1102, MSL 2201, or MSL 2202.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Orienteering
courses.description: Principles of orienteering, basic map reading, and compass skills, including practical land navigation techniques. 2 lectures. Formerly MSL 111.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Basic Army Physical Training Program
courses.description: The Army Physical Fitness Program and its proper execution. Physical training to the Army standards with the goal of successfully passing the Army Combat Fitness Test. 1 laboratory. Formerly MSL 112.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Foundations of Leadership I
courses.description: First of two courses taken sequentially for the development of individual leadership traits and capabilities using the Army officer as a model. The Army's problem solving methods, written and oral communications, tactics, and group leadership. Not open to students with credit in MSL 212 or MSL 2212. 2 lectures. Formerly MSL 201.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Foundations of Leadership II
courses.description: Continuation of the development of individual leadership traits and capabilities using the Army officer as a model. The Army's problem solving methods, tactics, and group leadership. Not open to students with credit in MSL 212 or MSL 2212. 2 lectures. Formerly MSL 202.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Leader's Training Course
courses.description: Completion of Leader's Training Course (LTC). Five weeks of training off campus at a designated military base. Travel pay and salary provided through the Military Science Department. No obligation. LTC graduates eligible to enroll in ROTC Advanced Program. Not open to students with credit in MSL 101, MSL 102, MSL 201, MSL 202, MSL 1101, MSL 1102, MSL 2201, or MSL 2202. 6 lectures. Formerly MSL 212.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: American Military History and the Evolution of Western Warfare
courses.description: Comprehensive analysis of American military history from the early Anglo-French period to the end of the 20th Century. Examination of the strategies, operations and tactics of military warfare, and exploration of how social, economic, and technological factors produced the distinct patterns of war that characterize the struggles of the past two hundred plus years. 4 lectures. Formerly MSL 240.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Facilitation and Teambuilding Experiences
courses.description: Techniques and models used in leadership, facilitation, and team building. Emphasis on leadership and facilitation styles and models, team building and group dynamics, and working with various populations. Field trip required. 3 seminars. Crosslisted as EIM/MSL 2275. Formerly MSL/RPTA 275.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Tactical Leadership I
courses.description: Advanced leadership skills through a focus on the Army's Training Management process, the Warfighting Functions, and foundational command and control doctrine. Analyze and apply mission planning tools (OPORDs, METT-TC), rehearse leadership in field scenarios, and engage in peer evaluation, self-development, and professional reading. 3 lectures., U.S. Army Basic Training, U.S. Army ROTC Basic Camp, etc.). Formerly MSL 3301.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Tactical Leadership II
courses.description: Applied leadership in small unit operations through experiential learning in tactics, ethical decision-making, and communication. Leadership theory and personality assessment tools, offensive and defensive operational plans, and platoon-level operations. 3 lectures. Formerly MSL 302.
courses.prerequisite: MSL 301 or MSL 3301.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MSL 301 or MSL 3301.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Intermediate Exercises in Military Leadership
courses.description: Build upon foundational military leadership in leadership roles during training exercises. Leadership of peer teams through drill, tactical training, and fieldcraft. Initiative, accountability, and instructional ability in dynamic environments. Repeatable up to 3 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly MSL 310.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Recommended: MSL 301 or MSL 3301.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Intermediate Army Physical Training Program
courses.description: The Army's Holistic Health and Fitness (H2F) framework. Student-led physical training (PT) at the junior-cadet level. Cadets will lead group PT sessions, incorporating principles of performance readiness, injury prevention, and fitness planning while developing confidence and command presence in physical training environments. 1 laboratory. Formerly MSL 312.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Recommended: MSL 301, MSL 302, MSL 3301, or MSL 3302.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Leadership Development and Assessment Course
courses.description: Six-week summer training program required to achieve an Army commission. Testing and training as functional Army officers and determination of potential for service. Travel pay, room and board, and salary provided by the United States Army. Held at Fort Knox, Kentucky. Field trip required. Credit/No Credit grading only. 6 lectures. Formerly MSL 314.
courses.prerequisite: MSL 301 or MSL 3301; MSL 302 or MSL 3302; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC Prerequisite: MSL 301 or MSL 3301; MSL 302 or MSL 3302; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Developmental Leadership I
courses.description: Knowledge, skills, and attributes expected of future Army officers operating in complex environments. Mission command, multidomain operations, and unit readiness. Assess threats, plan and evaluate training, and operate as leaders within the Army's organizational and operational structures. 3 lectures. Formerly MSL 401.
courses.prerequisite: MSL 302 or MSL 3302.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: MSL 302 or MSL 3302.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Developmental Leadership II
courses.description: Full spectrum of responsibilities expected of a Company Grade Officer. Multidimensional role of platoon leaders, from fostering ethical climates and mentoring subordinates to ensuring unit readiness, legal compliance, and operational effectiveness. Personal leadership development, military professionalism, and transitioning into officership. 3 lectures. Formerly MSL 402.
courses.prerequisite: MSL 401 or MSL 4401.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MSL 401 or MSL 4401.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Advanced Exercises in Military Leadership
courses.description: The supervision and evaluation of the organization, planning, resourcing, and execution of selected Army tactical missions, and mentoring assigned students. Repeatable up to 3 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 2 activities. Formerly MSL 410.
courses.prerequisite: MSL 302 or MSL 3302 and MSL 310 or MSL 3310.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: MSL 302 or MSL 3302 and MSL 310 or MSL 3310.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Leadership of Army Physical Training Program
courses.description: Senior-level Cadet's ability to lead, mentor, and evaluate junior-level Cadets through the lens of the Army's Holistic Health and Fitness (H2F) system. Supervise physical training sessions, provide developmental feedback, and assess performance in alignment with Army readiness standards. Leadership in health, wellness, resilience, and physical performance. Repeatable up to 3 units. 1 laboratory. Formerly MSL 412.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing and contracted status in Army ROTC.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing and contracted status in Army ROTC. Recommended: MSL 401 or MSL 4401.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Military Leadership at the Platoon Level
courses.description: Individual research and study into the Army Leadership Philosophy and it's practical application to military leadership at the platoon level. Assess and evaluate multiple military leadership techniques and processes to better prepare for future military career. Repeatable up to 2 units. Formerly MSL 400.
courses.prerequisite: MSL 402 or MSL 4402.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: MSL 402 or MSL 4402.

courses.subject: MSL
courses.title: Military Leadership in an Organizational Staff
courses.description: Individual research and study into the Army Leadership Philosophy and it's practical application to military leadership in an organizational staff. Assess and evaluate multiple military leadership techniques and processes to better prepare for future military career. Repeatable up to 2 units. Formerly MSL 470.
courses.prerequisite: MSL 402 or MSL 4402.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: MSL 402 or MSL 4402.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Introduction to Music Studies
courses.description: Introduction to the requirements of the music major, practical methods and cultural objectives of music, available resources, strategies for academic and performance success, and career options in music and related fields with an emphasis on career options and planning. 1 lecture.
courses.prerequisite: Music major or minor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Music major or minor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Music Fundamentals
courses.description: Introduction to materials and structures of music and their use by composers and performers in diverse cultural contexts. Notation of dynamics, pitch, rhythm, scales, key signatures, intervals, and chords. Analysis of musical syntax based on these elements. Concert attendance required. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2022-26 catalog). Formerly MU 101.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Materials and Structures of Music I
courses.description: Introduction to species counterpoint, structure of tonality, figured bass, harmonic progression, composition in four parts, diatonic triads and seventh chords, secondary dominants and leading tone chords, harmonic sequences, melodic organization and phrase structure, harmonization of a melody, nonchord tones, and variation forms. Composition project. 4 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: Placement exam, MU 101, or MU 1101 with a grade of C- or better, or consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Placement exam, MU 101, or MU 1101 with a grade of C- or better, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Musicianship I
courses.description: Sight-singing in major and minor modes; rhythmic performance and dictation in simple and compound meters; identification and performance of melodic and harmonic intervals and triads; dictation of major and minor diatonic melodies and harmonic progressions using diatonic triads; structured melodic and rhythmic improvisation. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 2 activities.
courses.prerequisite: MU 101 or MU 1101; or Music majors and
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: MU 101 or MU 1101; or Music majors and corequisite: MU 1101 or placement exam.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Musicianship II
courses.description: One- and two-part sight singing and melodic dictation; alto and tenor clefs. One- and two-part rhythmic performance and dictation including syncopation and triplets. Harmonic dictation including diatonic triads in all positions and dominant and supertonic seventh chords. Aural identification of cadences and phrase structure. Course may be offered in classroom-based or hybrid format. 2 activities.
courses.prerequisite: MU 1104 with a grade of C- or better, or consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MU 1104 with a grade of C- or better, or consent of instructor. Corequisite: MU 1103.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Introduction to Composition
courses.description: Fundamental concepts in music composition. Creative projects. Compositional techniques, development, and structure. Analysis of examples from the literature. 3 lectures. Formerly MU 114.
courses.prerequisite: MU 101 or MU 1101.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MU 101 or MU 1101.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Music Appreciation
courses.description: Explores the elements of music with emphasis on orchestral, operatic, liturgical, and chamber music traditions. Language of music, the role of music in society. Historical context and major composers from the Middle Ages to the present. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as HNRS/MU 1120. Fulfills GE Area 3A (GE Area C1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly HNRS/MU 120.
courses.geArea: 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP 2026-28 or later catalog: GE Area 3A 2020-26 catalogs: GE Area C1

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Ethnomusicology and World Music I
courses.description: Introduction to ethnomusicology and survey of world music cultures. History, aims, and methods of ethnomusicology as well as cultural context, aesthetics, and practices of selected music traditions. Open to all qualified students who perform on string, woodwind, brass, and percussion instruments. Audition required. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 laboratory. Formerly MU 374.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: New / Electronic Music Ensemble
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of music with electronic instruments, extended techniques, multimedia, improvisation, and other forms of contemporary music composition for upper-division credit. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Mustang Band
courses.description: Public performance of music and specially-designed shows written for marching band for upper-division credit: woodwinds, brass, percussion, and flag team auxiliary. Audition required. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 laboratory. Formerly MU 376.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Methods Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of music written for woodwinds, brass, percussion, or strings, for upper-division credit and for students interested in teaching music. Content emphasis for students performing on secondary instruments to further their proficiency on another instrument. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 activity. Formerly MU 377.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor. Recommended: MU 361 or MU 3361.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Mustang Band Field Show
courses.description: Study and application of advanced field show marching techniques for upper-division credit used in performance by the Cal Poly Mustang Band. Audition required. Field trip required. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 activity. Formerly MU 378.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Vocal Ensemble
courses.description: Open to qualified singers for upper-division credit. Rehearsal and performance of specialized vocal music. Audition required. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 activity. Formerly MU 383.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: PolyPhonics
courses.description: Advanced study and public performance of music for mixed chorus for upper-division credit. Audition required. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 laboratory. Formerly MU 381.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Cantabile
courses.description: Advanced study and public performance of music for soprano and alto chorus for upper-division credit. A variety of styles of choral literature specifically intended for treble voices from various time periods is explored. Audition required. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 laboratory. Formerly MU 382.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: University Singers
courses.description: Study and public performance of music for large mixed chorus for upper-division credit. Audition required. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 activity. Formerly MU 385.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Chamber Choir
courses.description: Advanced study and public performance of music for small ensemble for upper-division credit. Focus on music of the Renaissance, Baroque and Modern Eras. Exploration of a variety of styles of choral literature, specifically intended for a small performing ensemble. Audition required. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 laboratory. Formerly MU 386.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Vocal Jazz Ensemble
courses.description: Rehearsal and public performance of small or large vocal jazz ensemble repertory for upper-division credit. Open to qualified students who sing or play piano, guitar, bass, or drums. Audition required. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Arab Music Ensemble
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of vocal and instrumental music of Arabic-speaking societies and historically related cultures for upper-division credit. Study of associated music theory, performance practice, and improvisation, with presentation of seminal works in public concerts. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 laboratory. Formerly MU 388.
courses.prerequisite: Junior Standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior Standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Vocal Practicum
courses.description: Study and implementation of performing techniques used by vocalists in a recital or concert setting for upper-division credit. Repeatable up to 4 units. 1 activity. Formerly MU 389.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.corequisite: Vocal topic in one of the following: MU 1150, MU 2250, MU 3350, or MU 4450.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing. Corequisite: Vocal topic in one of the following: MU 1150, MU 2250, MU 3350, or MU 4450.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Special Problems for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly MU 400.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and consent of department chair.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Music Technology and Multimedia Performance
courses.description: Performative and compositional applications of synthesis and recording techniques in making a live multimedia production. Creative projects. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly MU 411.
courses.prerequisite: MU 312 or MU 3312.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MU 312 or MU 3312.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Composing and Producing a Multimedia Performance
courses.description: Production of electroacoustic music and multimedia. Program analysis, technical planning, composition, and product development. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly MU 412.
courses.prerequisite: MU 312 or MU 3312.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MU 312 or MU 3312.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Historical Musicology II
courses.description: Musical literature, styles, composers, theory, and genres of the Classic through Modern eras. 4 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: MU 3331 with a grade of C- or better, or consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: MU 3331 with a grade of C- or better, or consent of instructor. Recommended: MU 120 or MU 3303.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Applied Music IV
courses.description: Individual instruction in performance and composition. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly MU 450.
courses.prerequisite: MU 350 or MU 3350 and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: MU 350 or MU 3350 and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Selection and completion of a project under faculty supervision. Results presented in a recital, creative work, formal report, or a combination of all three. Formerly MU 461.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing and consent of department chair.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing and consent of department chair.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Choral Literature and Rehearsal Techniques
courses.description: Survey of choral literature especially suited for secondary schools. Philosophy and strategy for developing a school program. Musical as well as non-musical techniques for effective rehearsal. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly MU 465.
courses.prerequisite: MU 341 or MU 3341.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MU 341 or MU 3341.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Instrumental Literature and Rehearsal Techniques
courses.description: Survey of instrumental literature written for orchestras, bands, solo instrument, and chamber ensembles. Philosophy and strategy necessary for developing a professional, semi-professional, or school instrumental music program. Musical as well as non-musical techniques for effective rehearsal. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly MU 466.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: MU 101, MU 1101, MU 103, or MU 1103; and one of the following: MU 172, MU 1172, MU 173, MU 1173, MU 174, or MU 1174.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: MU 101, MU 1101, MU 103, or MU 1103; and one of the following: MU 172, MU 1172, MU 173, MU 1173, MU 174, or MU 1174.

courses.subject: MU
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Intensive study of special topics. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. 1 to 4 lectures. Formerly MU 470.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Careers in Natural Resources Management and Environmental Sciences
courses.description: Analysis and development of career goals in natural resources and environmental sciences. Acquainting students with potential career options and preparation of academic plans for the majors in the Natural Resources Management and Environmental Sciences Department. 1 seminar. Formerly NR 140.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Related
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Sustainability Related

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Introduction to Forest Ecosystem Management
courses.description: Fundamentals of forestry including basic silviculture, forest protection, measurement and policy. Integrated resource management of forest lands for multiple uses. Introduction to land and resource measurements, including field instruments, property description, map and photograph reconciliation, and data accuracy and precision. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 141.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Environmental Management
courses.description: An introduction to environmental management as a field and orientation for ENVM majors. Explores the effects of human activities on the natural environment as well as past and current efforts to balance human resource demands with ecosystem integrity. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly NR 142.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Special Problems for Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Credit/No Credit grading only. Repeatable up to 12 units. Formerly NR 200.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Resource Law Enforcement
courses.description: Law enforcement applied to natural resource conservation on public and private lands. Examination of state and federal laws related to fish and wildlife management. Problems associated with implementation of resource laws examined. 3 lectures. Formerly NR 203.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Wildland Fire Control
courses.description: Fire control techniques for various wildland fuels. Elementary fire physics, fuels, weather, fire behavior, fire suppression techniques, line construction, "mop-up", fire line safety, air operations, and fire organization. Meets wildland fire fighter certification for United States Forest Service (USFS). Partially meets California Department of Forestry (CDF) Firefighter I. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 204.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Dendrology
courses.description: Identification, classification, silvical characteristics, distribution, environmental requirements, and economic importance of woody plants in shrub, woodland, and forest ecosystems of the United States. Emphasis on species located in the Pacific Coastal, Sierran, and Cascade ecosystems. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 208.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Recommended: BOT 121 or BOT 1121.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
courses.description: Fundamental concepts and functions of Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Create, manage, analyze, and display geographically referenced data. Explore how GIS is applied to analyze environmental, social, and natural resource issues. 2 lecture, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as LA/NR 2218. Formerly LA/NR 218.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 8 units. 1 to 4 lectures. Formerly NR 270.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Intercollegiate Forestry Activities
courses.description: Beginning through advanced skills in the event areas of college forestry activities. Instruction in use of specialized equipment and safety. Field trip required. Repeatable up to 8 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 290.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Urban Forestry
courses.description: Establishment and management of municipal forests, wildland-urban interface, wildlife habitat, and pollution abatement. Management of forest areas with a focus on addressing challenges related to heavy recreational use, fire hazard, watershed, and societal values. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Replaces NR 350.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Recommended: NR 208 or NR 2208.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Agroecology
courses.description: Ecological concepts and principles applied to the design and management of agricultural systems. Discussion of research in agroecology and assessment of cropping system sustainability. Laboratory section emphasizes field assessment of ecological structures and functions, experimental design, and data interpretation. 3 lectures. 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly NR 304.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: STAT 218, STAT 252, STAT 301, STAT 312, STAT 1110, STAT 1220, STAT 1510, or STAT 3210.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Forest and Fire Ecology
courses.description: Examination of major forest types and processes that determine their development and productivity across the earth (silvics). Overview of the biophysical dynamics of fire and its interactions with vegetation structure and fuels management. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 305.
courses.prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 5B (GE Area B2 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5C (GE Area B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 5B (GE Area B2 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5C (GE Area B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Natural Resource Ecology and Habitat Management
courses.description: Ecology and management implications in North American ecosystems. Importance of maintaining natural dynamics of energy flow and nutrient cycles at the community and ecosystem levels for sustainability. Humanity's role as principal factor of change of the resources in natural systems. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 306.
courses.prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 5B (GE Area B2 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5C (GE Area B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 5B (GE Area B2 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5C (GE Area B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Fire and Society
courses.description: Prehistorical and historical record of human use of and attitude toward fire. Mythology and religion of fire. Traditional, cultural, and ethnic variations and their influence on modern United States institutions involved in managing fire. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly ES/NR 308.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of one lower-division course in GE Area 4 (GE Areas D1 or D2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Global Climate Change
courses.description: Global climate change ranks among the most impactful environmental challenges humans have faced. Exploration of biophysical mechanisms governing the climate system, the drivers of climate change, and the implications of these unprecedented changes for Earth's coupled human-environmental systems. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly NR 310.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5 (GE Areas B1 to B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Technology of Wildland Fire Management
courses.description: Historic, current and future perspectives of wildland fire in California. Sustainability and ecosystem health. The use of models and technology to solve complex land management problems. Assumptions and limitations of fire behavior and suppression models. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly NR 312.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5 (GE Areas B1 to B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Forest Mensuration
courses.description: Principles and methods of sampling and measurement for forest and natural resource quantities, determination of density measures, and site index. Modeling and estimation for tree volumes, stand structure, and composition. Applications in sampling, statistical, and inventory techniques. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 315.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BRAE 237, BRAE 239, BRAE 1239, or BRAE 2237; NR 141 or NR 1141; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: BRAE 237, BRAE 239, BRAE 1239, or BRAE 2237; NR 141 or NR 1141; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Environmental Literacy: An Integrative STEM Approach
courses.description: Examination of local environmental challenges with systems thinking strategies and tools. Explore natural and human factors shaping coastal watersheds. Design for environmental education, analyze science data and practices, develop critical environmental literacy, and practice culturally inclusive communication strategies. Field trip required. 2 seminars, 1 activity. Crosslisted as NR/SCM 3316. Formerly NR/SCM 316.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5 (GE Areas B1 to B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5 (GE Areas B1 to B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs). Recommended: Introductory statistics course.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: The World of Spatial Data and Geographic Information Technology
courses.description: Foundation for understanding the world through geographic information as well as the tools available to utilize spatial data. Experience with Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and related technology. Not open to students with credit in GEOG 218, GEOG 2218, LA/NR 218, or LA/NR 2218. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Crosslisted as LA/NR 3317. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly LA/NR 317.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5 (GE Areas B1 to B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Data Science
courses.description: Introduction to methods and applications in environmental data science. Computer programming to manipulate and analyze environmental data. Techniques to import, clean, analyze, model, and visualize environmental data. Introduction to data sources in forestry, fire science, natural resources, and environmental science. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: LA/NR 218 or LA/NR 2218; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: LA/NR 218 or LA/NR 2218; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Watershed Processes and Management
courses.description: Introduction, analysis, and measurement of watershed processes of precipitation, evapotranspiration, streamflow, stream channels, erosion, and riparian functions. Watershed management toward aquatic habitat and water quality goals. Field trip required. 2 lectures. Formerly NR 320.
courses.prerequisite: LA/NR 218 or LA/NR 2218; and SS 120 or SS 1120.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: LA/NR 218 or LA/NR 2218; and SS 120 or SS 1120.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Watershed Processes and Management Laboratory
courses.description: Evaluation, analysis, or measurement of watershed processes of precipitation, evapotranspiration, streamflow, stream channels, erosion, assessment of riparian functions, stream ecology, and water quality. Field trip required. 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: LA/NR 218 or LA/NR 2218; and SS 120 or SS 1120.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: LA/NR 218 or LA/NR 2218; and SS 120 or SS 1120. Corequisite: NR 3319.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Water Resources Technology and Society
courses.description: Study of technologies for sustainable management of water resources. Focus on monitoring of drinking water supply and quality, groundwater wells, surface water storage and conveyance systems, industrial, and oil and gas water use and management and stresses due to climate change. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly NR 321.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5 (GE Areas B1 to B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Human Dimensions in Natural Resources Management
courses.description: Social, economic, political, and ecological conditions and institutions that influence decisions affecting the environment. Examination of human-caused environmental impacts and how they in turn influence social institutions. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly NR 323.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); Completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 4A (GE Area D1 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Social Dimensions of Sustainable Food Systems
courses.description: Historical, political, socio-economic, and cultural dimensions of sustainable food and fiber systems. Overview of frameworks used for understanding agro-ecological sustainability with an emphasis on human elements. Exploration of core sustainability concepts, practices, and goals through case studies. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly NR 324.

courses.title: Natural Resources Economics and Valuation
courses.description: Theory of efficient use of renewable and nonrenewable natural resources, including methods for non-market valuation. Economic perspectives of sustainability and climate change. Environmental and ecological economic theories and techniques to address allocation of water, timber, wildlife/fisheries, open space, and recreation. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as AGB/NR 3326. Formerly NR 326.

courses.title: Environmental Leadership and Community Engagement
courses.description: Theories and practices of leadership and community engagement for a wide range of environmental issues. Development of personal leadership skills and methods for effectively working with non-profit organizations, governmental agencies, community groups, and the private sector to advance sustainability principles. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as EIM/NR 3328. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly NR/RPTA 328.

courses.title: Conflict Management in Natural Resources
courses.description: Application of behavioral science principles and techniques in the management of natural resource systems. Management of internal and external human resource issues and concerns in natural resources organizations is emphasized. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Internship in Natural Resources and Environmental Sciences
courses.description: Work with an approved firm or agency engaged in natural resources or environmental management, education, research, policy, or monitoring. Apply and develop professional skills and competencies. Repeatable up to 8 units. Credit/No Credit grading. Formerly NR 339.
courses.prerequisite: NR 140 or NR 1140; or one of the following: ERSC 144, ERSC 1144, NR 141, NR 142, NR 1141, or NR 1142; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Wildland Fire Management
courses.description: Wildland fuels, fire weather, and fire danger ratings in chaparral, grassland, and forested areas. Advanced modeling of surface and crown fire behavior. Fire management strategies and implications, policies and objectives of fire management organizations. Field trip required. 2 lectures. Formerly NR 340.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Junior standing. Recommended: NR 204 or NR 2204.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Wildland Fire Behavior
courses.description: Assessment of factors influencing wildland fire behavior in grassland, shrubland, and forested ecosystems. Impacts of fuels, weather, and/or topography on wildland fire behavior. Examination of extreme fire behavior. Fire behavior prediction systems employed at stand-level and landscape-level. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 341.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Junior standing. Recommended: NR 204 or NR 2204.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Water for a Sustainable Society
courses.description: Historical, political, economic, socio-technical, and cultural dimensions of water sustainability. Overview of complex systems with an emphasis on individual choices and their impact on water sustainability. Exploration of core sustainability concepts, practices, barriers, and goals related to water resources. Course offered online only. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as BRAE/NR 3349. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 4 (GE Area Upper-Division D for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly BRAE/NR 349.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Ethnicity, Culture, and the Environment in the United States
courses.description: Exploration of how ethnicity and culture shape landscapes and how social hierarchies structure access to and impacts from natural resource use in the United States. Examination of how social values, land ethics, and environmental contexts influence human-environment relationships, with emphasis on systemic inequities affecting marginalized communities. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing or one of the following: Environmental Earth and Soil Sciences major, Environmental Management and Protection major, or Forest and Fire Sciences major; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
