courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Career Preparation and Practices in Natural Resources Fields
courses.description: Introduction to professional practices, including preparation of professional materials and interview skills. Review and presentation of current published research and library researching techniques in environmental science/management and forestry and fire sciences. Development of presentation skills. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 2 seminars. Formerly NR 363.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Silviculture and Fuels Management
courses.description: Forest ecology focusing on the development of sustainable forest management practices for achieving diverse forest ecosystem management objectives in US forests. Natural forest ecology, silvicultural systems and forest regeneration, and forest ecosystem services. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 365.
courses.prerequisite: NR 208 or NR 2208; and NR 315 or NR 3315.
courses.recommended: One of the following: NR 304, NR 305, NR 306, NR 3304, NR 3305, or NR 3306.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: NR 208 or NR 2208; and NR 315 or NR 3315. Recommended: One of the following: NR 304, NR 305, NR 306, NR 3304, NR 3305, or NR 3306.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Special Problems for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies or surveys of selected problems. Repeatable up to 12 units. Formerly NR 400.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Forest Health and Disturbance Ecology
courses.description: Impact and losses to forested areas caused by physical and biotic agents with a special focus on insects, diseases, drought, and wildfire. Relation of direct and indirect control practices to forest management. 3 lectures. Formerly NR 402.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; one of the following: BIO 162, BIO 222, BIO 227, BIO 2215, BIO 2217, NR 208, or NR 2208; and one of the following: NR 304, NR 305, NR 306, NR 3304, NR 3305, or NR 3306.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Forest Health and Disturbance Ecology Laboratory
courses.description: Overview of disturbance ecology agents and abiotic events. Laboratory analysis of common forest microbes, development of techniques for isolating microbes, field identification of signs of insect damage, examination of interactions between biotic agents and abiotic events focusing on wildfire. Field trip required. 1 laboratory.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Concurrent: NR 4402.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Environmental Law
courses.description: Investigation of law as a tool for furthering environmental planning, management and protection with focus on federal environmental laws including the Clean Water Act, Clean Air Act, and Endangered Species Act. Legal research skills and legal analysis. 4 lectures. Crosslisted as CRP/NR 4404. Formerly CRP/NR 404.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Water Resource Law and Policy
courses.description: Examination of water quality and quantity regulation and management in California, the United States, and globally. Coverage of freshwater and marine water issues. Research case study on water law and policy development. 4 lectures. Crosslisted as CRP/NR 4408. Formerly CRP/NR 408.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 1 (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); or graduate standing.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 1 (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); or graduate standing.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Agricultural Law
courses.description: Analysis of agricultural law and policy including the business of agriculture, agricultural legislation, and coverage of contemporary agricultural issues such as water, food safety, and labor. Examination of statutory, judicial, policy and administrative areas in agriculture. 4 lectures. Formerly NR 413.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and completion of GE Area 1 (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Sustainable Forest Management and Forest Operations
courses.description: Biophysical, economic, social and political influences on optimal forest. Relationships between sustainable forests, ecosystem services, operational practices, forest road design, safety in forest operations, and environmental protection. Forest investment analysis and sustainable forest production. Field trip required. 1 lecture, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 414.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Environmental Impact Analysis and Management
courses.description: National Environmental Policy and California Environmental Quality Acts applied to private and public planning, development, and restoration projects. Intent, purpose, and application of the laws. Differences and similarities between laws and relationship with other environmental regulations. Review of real-world case studies. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 416.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.title: Natural Resource Protection and Policy
courses.description: Overview of regulations pertaining to natural resource protection and management of public and private lands. Current environmental and natural resource law issues and disputes, focusing on evaluation of environmental impacts of public and private projects, programs, and activities. Course may be offered in classroom-base or online format. 3 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused

courses.title: Applied Geographic Information System
courses.description: Acquisition, organization, and analysis of spatial data from diverse sources using Geographic Information System (GIS) software. GIS modeling applications, validation techniques, and quantitative reasoning are applied to develop and accomplish spatial analysis projects. 1 lecture, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 418.

courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: GEOG 218, GEOG 2218, LA/NR 218, or LA/NR 2218.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Wetlands
courses.description: Formation, characteristics, and functions of wetlands. Genesis of hydric soils. Plant adaptations to saturated soils. Wetlands as wildlife habitat. Policies and social issues associated with wetlands. Procedures of wetland delineations. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as NR/SS 4421. Formerly NR 421.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Stream Measurements and Water Quality Monitoring
courses.description: Field measurement of streamflow, water quality, and water resources to support environmental evaluations of local water resources. Application of quality assurance procedures for monitoring water resources. Field trip required. Repeatable up to 2 units. 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 422.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Junior standing.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Spatial Data Analysis and Environmental Mapping
courses.description: Introduction to methods and applications in spatial data science. Use of computer programming and geographic information systems (GIS) to manipulate and analyze spatial data. Applied mapping of environmental, agricultural and natural resource data using modeling techniques. 2 lectures, 2 laboratories. Crosslisted as NR/SS 4431. Formerly SS 431.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Environmental Life-Cycle Analysis
courses.description: Assess and quantify environmental impacts of human activities, industrial production processes, and organizational sustainability performance using life-cycle analysis. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly NR 314.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Systems Thinking in Environmental Management
courses.description: Analysis of environmental challenges by incorporating systems thinking and system dynamics simulations with quantitative models. Interpretation of modeling results and their social and political implications. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Formerly NR 445.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Senior Project - Watershed Assessment and Protection
courses.description: Assessment of streamflow, peak flows, and land management effects using established techniques and hydrologic models. Fluvial processes, sediment transport, and stream restoration techniques. Assessment and restoration plan of a watershed toward protection of aquatic and public resources. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 420.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing, and NR 320 or NR 3320; or graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Senior standing, and NR 320 or NR 3320; or graduate standing.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Senior Project - Applied Resource Analysis and Assessment
courses.description: Evaluation of environmental impacts of public and private projects, programs, and activities. Preparation, implementation, and coordination of environmental plans. Criteria for measurement, interpretation, and evaluation. Resource inventories, permitting and environmental constraints analysis, evaluation, synthesis, environmental assessment writing, and preparation. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing and NR 416 or NR 4416.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing and NR 416 or NR 4416.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Senior Project - Ecological Restoration
courses.description: Targeted study and application of ecological restoration concepts, theories, and practices. Evaluate benefits and limitations of restoration strategies. Develop and execute an applied restoration project in San Luis Obispo County. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 464.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; and one of the following: NR 304, NR 306, NR 402, NR 3304, NR 3306, NR 4402, SS 321, SS 422, SS 3321, or SS 4422.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Senior standing; and one of the following: NR 304, NR 306, NR 402, NR 3304, NR 3306, NR 4402, SS 321, SS 422, SS 3321, or SS 4422.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Senior Project - Environmental Policy Analysis
courses.description: Survey of policy tools and approaches to manage environmental challenges. Analyze environmental challenges, evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of existing policy tools, and propose new policies to address policy gaps. 4 lectures. Formerly NR 435.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; and one of the following: NR 404, NR 408, NR 4404, or NR 4408.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing; and one of the following: NR 404, NR 408, NR 4404, or NR 4408.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Senior Project - Ecosystem Management
courses.description: Capstone course integrating biophysical and social sciences. Principles, concepts, and techniques designed to utilize resources while sustaining ecosystem health within acceptable limits of change. Ecosystem assessment, planning, and/or management project. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 465.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; and one of the following: Environmental Earth and Soil Sciences major, Environmental Management and Protection major, or Forest and Fire Sciences major.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Senior standing; and one of the following: Environmental Earth and Soil Sciences major, Environmental Management and Protection major, or Forest and Fire Sciences major.

courses.subject: NR
courses.title: Senior Project - Wildland-Urban Interface Fire Protection
courses.description: Biophysical and socioeconomic issues affecting wildland fire management in urbanized landscapes. Fire risk assessment. Pre-fire prevention, mitigation, and preparedness during-fire response and post-fire recovery actions by public- and private-sector agencies and residents. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 455.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing.

courses.title: Senior Project - Forest Stewardship Practices
courses.description: Sustainable forest management, ecosystem sampling and inventory methods, hydrologic resources, road condition, forest project impact analysis, and best management practices related to forest stewardship. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly NR 474.

courses.title: Senior Project - Advanced Internship Experience in Environmental Science/Management
courses.description: Independent internship experience conducted under faculty supervision focusing on a discipline area of environmental science/management. Completion of a project as a component of the internship. Crosslisted as ERSC/NR 4476. Formerly ERSC/NR 476.

courses.title: Senior Project - Research Experience in Environmental Science
courses.description: Guided research experience in a specific area of environmental science. Implementation of materials and methods. Collection, analysis and interpretation of data. Completion of formal written report. 1 lecture, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as ERSC/NR 4477. Formerly ERSC/NR 477.

courses.title: Senior Project - Current Topics in Environmental Science
courses.description: Critical evaluation and formal presentation of current issues in environmental science/management. Satisfies the senior project requirement. 2 lectures. Crosslisted as ERSC/NR 4478. Formerly ERSC/NR 478.

courses.title: Senior Project - Independent Study
courses.description: Selection and completion of a project under faculty supervision. Projects typical of problems that graduates must solve in their fields of employment. Project results are presented in a formal report. Crosslisted as ERSC/NR 4479. Formerly ERSC/NR 479.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Orientation to the Nutrition Major
courses.description: Understanding the depth and breadth of the Nutrition program and academic and career planning. Students are required to complete this course within their first year in the major. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 lecture. Formerly FSN 101.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Maternal and Child Nutrition
courses.description: Nutritional needs and related nutritional challenges of women and children, including fertility, pregnancy and lactation; physical, nutritional, social growth and development from infancy through adolescence. Current nutrition issues in maternal and child nutrition. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly FSN 310.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; and FSN 202 or FSN 2202.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing; and FSN 202 or FSN 2202.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrition in Aging
courses.description: Nutrition issues in the middle and later years. Changes in organ systems, nutrient needs, functional status, and food preferences as adults age. Nutrition and chronic disease. Nutritional assessment and screening. Nutrition-related healthcare and preventative interventions for longevity and healthspan. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 2 lectures. Crosslisted as HNRS/NUTR 3315. Formerly FSN 315.
courses.prerequisite: Sophomore standing; and FSN 202 or FSN 2202.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Sophomore standing; and FSN 202 or FSN 2202.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Experimental Foods
courses.description: Overview of the science and processes used to produce foods consumed daily. An experimental approach to solve challenges in choosing, purchasing, and preparing foods for diverse populations emphasizing food's nutritional, aesthetic, economic and cultural aspects. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly FSN 321.
courses.prerequisite: Sophomore standing; and FSN 202 or FSN 2202.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Sophomore standing; and FSN 202 or FSN 2202. Corequisite: FSN 121 or FSN 1121.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Macronutrient Metabolism
courses.description: Metabolism of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins as it applies to human nutrition. Integration and regulation of metabolic pathways. 3 lectures. Formerly FSN 331.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; BIO 161 or BIO 1151; FSN 202 or FSN 2202; and one of the following: CHEM 314, CHEM 369, CHEM 3350, or CHEM 3352.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing; BIO 161 or BIO 1151; FSN 202 or FSN 2202; and one of the following: CHEM 314, CHEM 369, CHEM 3350, or CHEM 3352.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Micronutrient Metabolism
courses.description: Biochemical, molecular, and physiological functions of vitamins and minerals and their interaction with other nutrients. 3 lectures. Formerly FSN 332.
courses.prerequisite: FSN 331 or NUTR 3331.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: FSN 331 or NUTR 3331.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrient Metabolism Lab
courses.description: Application of biochemical, absorptiometry, calorimetry, and other methods to assess health indicators and nutritional status. 1 laboratory. Formerly FSN 333.
courses.prerequisite: FSN 331 or NUTR 3331.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: FSN 331 or NUTR 3331. Corequisite: FSN 332 or NUTR 3332.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Advanced Sport Nutrition & Exercise Metabolism
courses.description: Advanced concepts in sports nutrition and interaction of exercise and nutrition, including classic and recent findings related to mechanisms of nutrient effects on exercise performance, metabolism, muscle physiology, body composition, and health. 3 lectures. Formerly FSN 405.
courses.prerequisite: FSN 331 or NUTR 3331.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: FSN 331 or NUTR 3331.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrition Counseling & Education
courses.description: Appropriate behavior and learning theories in nutrition education and counseling in communications across diverse individuals. Counseling techniques, materials, and theories to educate individuals. Includes community-based learning projects. 3 lectures. Formerly FSN 415.
courses.prerequisite: FSN 331 or NUTR 3331.
courses.corequisite: FSN 332 or NUTR 3332; and FSN 333 or NUTR 3333.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: FSN 331 or NUTR 3331. Corequisite: FSN 332 or NUTR 3332; and FSN 333 or NUTR 3333.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Community Nutrition
courses.description: Federal, state, and local nutrition assessment activities, group education and communication, and program services. Public health, health promotion, and disease prevention. Development of skills in group education, assessing community nutrition problems, and planning community interventions. 3 lectures. Formerly FSN 416.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; FSN 310 or NUTR 3310; FSN 315 or NUTR 3315; and FSN 331 or NUTR 3331.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing; FSN 310 or NUTR 3310; FSN 315 or NUTR 3315; and FSN 331 or NUTR 3331. Recommended: FSN 415 or NUTR 4415.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Professional Practice in Nutrition and Dietetics
courses.description: Exploration of students' transition to professional practice, graduate schools, career opportunities, and factors to be considered in career decisions. Strategic planning, critical thinking, and written and oral communication skills in preparation for nutrition and dietetics professions. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 lecture. Formerly FSN 463.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Junior standing. Recommended: FSN 332 or NUTR 3332.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrition and Foodservice Systems Management
courses.description: Principles of successful organization and management for clinical, community, and foodservice systems. Administrative responsibilities of nutrition and foodservice directors. Management theories and practice. Labor relations. Discipline and performance appraisal. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly FSN 426.
courses.prerequisite: FSN 344 or FSN 3346.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: FSN 344 or FSN 3346.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy I
courses.description: Nutrition care processes for physiological disorders that may alter nutritional requirements and require dietary modifications for Diabetes Mellitus, enteral and parenteral nutrition, anemias, acid-base conditions, cardiovascular disease, and obesity. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly FSN 431.
courses.prerequisite: BIO 231 or BIO 2231; FSN 310 or NUTR 3310; and FSN 315 or NUTR 3315.
courses.corequisite: BIO 232 or BIO 2232; FSN 332 or NUTR 3332; and FSN 333 or NUTR 3333.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: BIO 231 or BIO 2231; FSN 310 or NUTR 3310; and FSN 315 or NUTR 3315. Corequisite: BIO 232 or BIO 2232; FSN 332 or NUTR 3332; and FSN 333 or NUTR 3333.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy II
courses.description: Application of the nutrition care process to physiological disorders which may alter nutritional requirements for: Upper and lower GI diseases, liver, gallbladder, and exocrine pancreas diseases, renal diseases, respiratory diseases, metabolic stress disorders, cancer, and metabolic disorders. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly FSN 432.
courses.prerequisite: FSN 431 or NUTR 4431.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: FSN 431 or NUTR 4431.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Senior Project - Scientific and Technical Writing
courses.description: Directed culminating experience for Nutrition students choosing the Senior Project Scientific & Technical Writing option. Development of literature review. 2 lectures.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; FSN 310 or NUTR 3310; FSN 315 or NUTR 3315; FSN 333 or NUTR 3333; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing; FSN 310 or NUTR 3310; FSN 315 or NUTR 3315; FSN 333 or NUTR 3333; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Senior Project - Research
courses.description: Directed culminating experience for Nutrition students choosing the senior project research option. Selection of scientific research topic in major area. Development of literature review, research questions, research design, data collection, and analysis. Required for Blended MS in Nutrition. Formerly FSN 461.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; FSN 310 or NUTR 3310; FSN 315 or NUTR 3315; FSN 333 or NUTR 3333; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Senior standing; FSN 310 or NUTR 3310; FSN 315 or NUTR 3315; FSN 333 or NUTR 3333; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Senior Project - Internship
courses.description: Directed culminating experience for Nutrition majors choosing the senior project internship option. Students must complete a project as a component of their internship in an approved organization in California.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing; two of the following: FSN 310, NUTR 3310, FSN 315, NUTR 3315, FSN 333, or NUTR 3333; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Senior standing; two of the following: FSN 310, NUTR 3310, FSN 315, NUTR 3315, FSN 333, or NUTR 3333; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrition Epidemiology
courses.description: Concepts and issues in nutrition epidemiology. Epidemiologic methods, study design, and population health from nutrition perspective. Analytical considerations related to nutrition and population health. Nutrition-related issues at national and global levels. 2 lectures. Formerly FSN 516.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing, FSN 416, or NUTR 4416.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing, FSN 416, or NUTR 4416.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Biochemical and Molecular Aspects of Human Macronutrient Metabolism
courses.description: Advanced aspects of the human metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids and proteins. Classic and recent findings related to mechanisms of nutrient-regulated gene expression. Metabolism related to specific diseases. 3 lectures. Formerly FSN 528.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing, FSN 331, or NUTR 3331.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing, FSN 331, or NUTR 3331.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Metabolic and Molecular Aspects of Vitamins and Minerals
courses.description: Advanced aspects of vitamins and minerals. Metabolic details and functional roles. Mechanisms of vitamin- and mineral-regulated gene expression. Aspects of vitamin and mineral status. 3 lectures. Formerly FSN 529.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing, FSN 332, or NUTR 3332.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing, FSN 332, or NUTR 3332.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Lipid Metabolism and Nutrition
courses.description: Digestion, absorption and metabolism of lipids with emphasis on lipoprotein metabolism, regulation of lipid metabolism, effects of gene expression, essential fatty acid requirements and functions. 3 lectures. Formerly FSN 531.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Graduate standing. Recommended: FSN 331 or NUTR 3331.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrition & Dietetics Leadership & Professionalism Seminar
courses.description: Seminar focused on professionalism and leadership in dietetics and current issues in medical nutrition therapy, food service management, and management and community nutrition. Field trip may be required. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 seminars. Formerly FSN 550.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy Practicum I
courses.description: Supervised practice providing medical nutrition therapy for patients with lower-acuity care needs/low-moderate nutrition risk in outpatient and inpatient medical facilities. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly FSN 551.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy Practicum II
courses.description: Supervised practice providing medical nutrition therapy for patients with mid-level acute care needs/moderate nutrition risk. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly FSN 552.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy Practicum III
courses.description: Supervised practice providing medical nutrition therapy for patients with high-level acute care needs/high nutrition risk. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly FSN 553.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Community Nutrition Practicum
courses.description: Supervised practice in community nutrition settings. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly FSN 554.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Food & Nutrition Service Management Practicum
courses.description: Supervised practice in food and nutrition service and management facilities, such as hospitals and school districts. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly FSN 556.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Current Nutrition Research
courses.description: Directed group study and presentation of selected nutrition research topics for graduate and advanced undergraduate students. Students will select, read, critically analyze and present nutrition research within designated themes. Repeatable up to 3 units. 1 seminar. Formerly FSN 582.
courses.prerequisite: Graduate standing.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Graduate standing.

courses.subject: NUTR
courses.title: Nutrition & Dietetics Capstone Project
courses.description: Capstone project for students to apply and synthesize their knowledge and experiences to address current issues in nutrition and dietetics practice. Repeatable up to 6 units. Formerly FSN 598.
courses.prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs; and STAT 511 or STAT 5110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Admission into Cal Poly's dietetic internship programs; and STAT 511 or STAT 5110.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.description: Foundational methods and central issues in contemporary philosophy including logic, epistemology, metaphysics and ethics. Advising and orientation to the Philosophy major for first-year students in their first quarter at Cal Poly. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly PHIL 101.
courses.prerequisite: Philosophy major.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Philosophy major.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Logic and Argumentative Writing
courses.description: Principles of argument analysis, evaluation and construction. Deductive and inductive reasoning, including analogical arguments, universal and statistical generalizations, and causal inferences. Principles of organizing and writing argumentative essays. Moral dimensions of rational discourse. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 1B with a grade of C- or better (GE Area A3 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly PHIL 126.
courses.prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 1A with a grade of C- or better (GE Area A2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophical Classics: Knowledge and Reality
courses.description: Critical examination of primary philosophical works with focus on the nature of reality and the sources and limits of human knowledge. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as HNRS/PHIL 2230. Fulfills GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly HNRS/PHIL 230.
courses.prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 1A with a grade of C- or better (GE Area A2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.title: Philosophical Classics: Ethics and Political Philosophy
courses.description: Critical examination of primary philosophical works, with focus on the identification and evaluation of the central ethical, social and political themes and arguments presented in them. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as HNRS/PHIL 2231. Fulfills GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly HNRS/PHIL 231.

courses.title: Symbolic Logic
courses.description: The nature of deductive logical systems. Methods of notation, translation and proof in sentential and predicate calculi including truth-trees and natural deduction systems. courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Completion of GE Area 1B with a grade of C- or better (GE Area A3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly PHIL 270.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophical Writing and Research
courses.description: Develop writing and research skills by composing a substantial research paper on a specific topic. Revisions based on instructor and peer feedback. Oral presentation of research project. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly PHIL 300.

courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: PHIL 230, PHIL 2230, PHIL 231, or PHIL 2231; and Philosophy major.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophical Topics
courses.description: Examination and analysis of philosophical areas, movements, texts, or figures. Topics may be of historical or contemporary importance. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 12 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. courses.description: Philosophies developed in China, Japan and East Asia, including Buddhism, Confucian moral philosophy, Daoist metaphysics and social ecology. courses.title: Postmodernism
courses.description: Primary issues and developments in recent and contemporary European philosophy. Examination of the influence of postmodern philosophy in areas such as art, literature, architecture, culture studies, philosophy of language, and philosophy of religion. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Upper-Division 3 (GE Area Upper-Division C for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly PHIL 369.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Metaphysics
courses.description: Traditional and current ideas and arguments about substance, the relation of universals to particulars, space and time, events, causation and necessity, the self and free will. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly PHIL 411.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Epistemology
courses.description: Analysis of the concept of knowledge. Study of competing theories of epistemic justification. Inquiry into relationship between knowledge, belief, justification, and truth. Examination of skepticism. Study of expanded epistemology. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly PHIL 412.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Space, Time, and Matter
courses.description: Investigation of the philosophical foundations and interpretation of relativity theory and elementary quantum mechanics. Emphasis on philosophical issues relevant to contemporary philosophy of science such as scientific realism. Some discussion of very recent theories of space, time, and matter. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly PHIL 421.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Mind
courses.description: Classic and current work in the problems and issues of the nature and unity of the self, consciousness, mental representations, and action, and of the relation of philosophy of mind to psychology, linguistics and computer science. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly PHIL 422.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Language
courses.description: Traditional and contemporary philosophical issues that arise from the structure of language. Relevant concepts include: syntax, semantics, pragmatics, meaning, reference, truth, identity, thought, reality. Important distinctions: use/mention, relations/properties of relations, sentences/statements/propositions. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly PHIL 423.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics in the History of Philosophy
courses.description: Advanced discussion of topics in the history of philosophy. Examination and analysis of philosophical movements (e.g., Stoicism, critical theory), particular philosophers (e.g., William James, W.E.B. Du Bois), or philosophical works (e.g., Kant's Critique of Pure Reason, Hannah Arendt's The Life of the Mind). The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 12 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly PHIL 429.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics in Ethics and Political Philosophy
courses.description: Advanced discussion of topics in ethics and political philosophy. Examination and analysis of ethical or political theories (e.g., utilitarianism, contractarianism) or alternatively, of particular philosophers or philosophical works (e.g., John Stuart Mill; John Rawls' A Theory of Justice). The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 12 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly PHIL 439.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics in Recent Philosophy
courses.description: Advanced discussion of topics in recent philosophy or of recent philosophers or recent philosophical works. The Class Schedule will list subtitle selected. Repeatable up to 12 units. Course may be offered in classroom-based, online, or hybrid format. 3 lectures. Formerly PHIL 449.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 3B (GE Area C2 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Senior Project Preparation
courses.description: Group and individual discussion of senior project advisor selection and initial research for senior project. Library research training, completion of exit interview, and career advising for Philosophy majors nearing graduation. Credit/No Credit grading only. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 1 laboratory. Formerly PHIL 459.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing, Philosophy major, and consent of instructor.

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Development and completion of a research project under faculty supervision. Results presented in a formal thesis. Formerly PHIL 460.

courses.title: Special Advanced Topics

courses.title: Introduction to the Physics Major
courses.description: Introduction to the skills, tools, and habits-of-mind physicists use to investigate physical phenomena. Exploration of possible careers and issues of diversity and representation in physics. Introduction to the research programs and opportunities in the department. Credit/No credit grading only. 1 activity. Formerly PHYS 100.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introductory Physics
courses.description: Elementary introduction to mechanics, gases, liquids and solids, heat, vibrations and waves, light, electricity and magnetism. Intended to provide non-science students with an understanding of basic physical concepts. Not open to students who have credit in a college physics course. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 5A (GE Area B1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly PHYS 104.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Contemporary Physics for Nonscientists
courses.description: Qualitative exploration of the key concepts of quantum mechanics and Einstein's special and general theories of relativity. Particle-wave duality, Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, Schrodinger's cat, warped spacetime, black holes. Not open to students with credit in PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Area 5A (GE Area B1 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly PHYS 111.

courses.title: College Physics I
courses.description: Introduction to mechanics emphasizing motion, force, energy, and fluids. Waves and vibrations, sound, thermodynamics, and heat. Not open to students with a grade of C- or better in PHYS 141 or PHYS 1141. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Fulfills GE Area 5A and 5C (GE Areas B1 and B3 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: College Physics II
courses.description: Continuation of two course college physics series. Electrostatics, electric current, magnetic fields and induction. Light and optics. Elements of modern physics. Not open to students with a grade of C- or better in PHYS 143 or PHYS 1143. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly offered as part of the PHYS 121, 122, 123 series, students may not earn credit for both PHYS 123 and PHYS 1123.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Physics I
courses.description: Fundamental principles of mechanics. 1D and 2D particle kinematics and vectors. Newton's laws. Work and energy, and momentum. Equilibrium of a rigid body, rotational kinematics and dynamics. Simple harmonic motion. Gravitation. Kinetic theory and laws of thermodynamics. Primarily for engineering and science students. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as HNRS/PHYS 1141. Fulfills GE Areas 5A and 5C (GE Areas B1 and B3 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly offered as part of the PHYS 141, 142, 143 series, students may not earn credit for both PHYS 141 and PHYS 1141.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Physics II
courses.description: Wave optics, geometrical optics, lenses, mirrors, and optical instruments. Charge and matter, electric force, field and potential, capacitance. Current and resistance, circuits, magnetic field and force, induced emf, Maxwell's equations, and AC circuits. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Crosslisted as HNRS/PHYS 1143. Fulfills GE Areas 5A and 5C (GE Areas B1 and B3 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly offered as part of the PHYS 141, 142, 143 series, students may not earn credit for both PHYS 143 and PHYS 1143.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Physics III: Modern Physics
courses.description: Introduction to modern physics. Special relativity, quantum mechanics, and statistical mechanics. Application to atoms, molecules, crystalline solids, nuclei, and elementary particles. 4 lectures. Formerly PHYS 211.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, or PHYS 1143; and MATH 241 or MATH 2263.

courses.title: Special Topics

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Introduction to statistical mechanics and thermodynamics. Entropy, temperature, ensembles, partition functions, chemical potential, free energy. Applications include paramagnetism, ideal gas, Fermi-Dirac and Bose-Einstein distributions. 3 lectures. Formerly PHYS 301.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211; and MATH 143 or MATH 1262.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Classical Mechanics I
courses.description: Laws of motion, kinematics and dynamics of a particle. Oscillations. Work and energy. Linear and angular momentum. Lagrange's and Hamilton's equations. Kepler's laws of orbital motion and central force problems. Use of numerical methods for solving problems. 3 lectures. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly PHYS 305.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Classical Mechanics II
courses.description: Mechanics in non-inertial reference frames. Dynamics of rigid bodies. Coupled oscillators and normal modes. Nonlinear Mechanics and Chaos. Collision Theory and Continuum Mechanics. Use of numerical methods for solving problems. 3 lectures. Formerly PHYS 306.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 305 or PHYS 3305.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: PHYS 305 or PHYS 3305.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics of Energy
courses.description: Physics and mathematics applied to broad energy concepts and interplay of these technologies with society and government policy. Efficient usage, transportation, transmission, storage, planning and public policy. Concepts may include fossil fuels, solar, nuclear fission and fusion, fuel cells, wind, wave, tidal, and geothermal energy. 2 lectures. Formerly PHYS 310.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, or PHYS 1143.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Related
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Sustainability Related Prerequisite: PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, or PHYS 1143.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Ocean Dynamics
courses.description: Physics governing ocean circulation and transport processes. Physical environment, dynamics of fluid motion in the presence of rotation and stratification, balanced flows, heat budgets, ocean waves, mixing and turbulence, and applications to climate processes and the biological environment. 3 lectures. Formerly PHYS 314.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: PHYS 123, PHYS 123C, PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, PHYS 1123, or PHYS 1143; and MATH 241 or MATH 2263.
courses.recommended: One of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Lasers
courses.description: Interaction of light with matter, theory of laser action, laser beam characteristics, continuous and pulsed output, types of lasers. Laser applications that may include interferometry, fiber optics, pulsed laser applications, atom trapping, nonlinear optics. 2 lectures. Formerly PHYS 315.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Instrumentation and Techniques of Experimental Physics
courses.description: Statistical data analysis. Introduction to laboratory test and measurement equipment. Basic analog and digital electronic circuits emphasizing applications in experimental physics. Computer based data acquisition, data analysis and control. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Replaced PHYS 206.
courses.prerequisite: CSC 101 or CSC 1001; and PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, or PHYS 1143.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CSC 101 or CSC 1001; and PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, or PHYS 1143.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
courses.description: Mathematical techniques of theoretical physics with applications from classical mechanics, optics, electromagnetism, and quantum mechanics. Maxwell's equations and vector calculus. Fourier analysis. Series solutions. Partial differential equations with problems involving the heat equation, the wave equation, and the Schroedinger equation. 4 lectures. Formerly PHYS 320.
courses.prerequisite: Physics majors; PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211; and one of the following: MATH 244, MATH 2341, MATH 242, or MATH 2343.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Physics majors; PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211; and one of the following: MATH 244, MATH 2341, MATH 242, or MATH 2343.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Optics
courses.description: Ray optics, lens systems, optical instruments, wave optics, interference, diffraction, polarization of light, wave propagation in media and at interfaces, waveguides, optical fiber. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly PHYS 323.
courses.prerequisite: MATH 241 or MATH 2263; PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, or PHYS 1143; and one of the following: PHYS 320, PHYS 3320, EE 2328, EE 201, EE 2201, ME 318, or ME 3318.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: MATH 241 or MATH 2263; PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, or PHYS 1143; and one of the following: PHYS 320, PHYS 3320, EE 2328, EE 201, EE 2201, ME 318, or ME 3318.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Teaching Physics
courses.description: Inquiry approaches to teaching physics incorporating insights from physics education research and computer technology. Pedagogical approaches and assessment that engages learners in scientific discourse and development of basic models of physics phenomena such as motion, forces, energy, and momentum through experimentation. 1 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly PHYS 330.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: PHYS 123, PHYS 123C, PHYS 1123, PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, PHYS 1143, PSC 103, or PSC 1102.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: PHYS 123, PHYS 123C, PHYS 1123, PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, PHYS 1143, PSC 103, or PSC 1102.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Communicating Physics
courses.description: Communication techniques for physics. Critical study of scientific literature, creation of lab reports, oral presentations, posters, outreach, with peer-review. 1 activity. Fulfills GWR.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs).
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP GWR Prerequisite: Junior standing and completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs). Concurrent: PHYS 3340.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Physics Laboratory I
courses.description: Experimental studies of quantum properties of atoms and nuclei. Measurements of fundamental constants. Use of modern laboratory instruments in physical measurements. Overview of skills needed in a working physics laboratory. Rigorous computer-based statistical and error analysis of data. 1 laboratory. Formerly PHYS 340.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 206 or PHYS 3316; and PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: PHYS 206 or PHYS 3316; and PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211. Concurrent: PHYS 3339.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Physics Laboratory II
courses.description: Second semester of the advanced lab experience. Advanced experimental physics techniques, instrumentation, data acquisition and analysis. Quantum experimental studies of atoms, molecules and nuclei, and their interactions with light, other forms of radiation, and static electric and magnetic fields. 1 laboratory. Formerly PHYS 341.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 340; or PHYS 3339 and PHYS 3340.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: PHYS 340; or PHYS 3339 and PHYS 3340.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Computing
courses.description: Quantum mechanical wave functions. Principle of superposition and entanglement. States of one or more quantum bits. Quantum gates and circuits. Application of quantum gates on simulators and quantum computers. Quantum computer architectures. Quantum algorithms. Ethics of quantum computing. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Crosslisted as CPE/PHYS 3345. Formerly CPE/PHYS 345.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; and one of the following: CHEM 353, CHEM 3392, PHYS 211, or PHYS 2211.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: MATH 206, MATH 244, MATH 1151, or MATH 2341; and one of the following: CHEM 353, CHEM 3392, PHYS 211, or PHYS 2211.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Computational Physics
courses.description: Applications of computational methods in physics. Concepts may include data selection and feature extraction with machine learning, finite difference methods in calculus, Monte-Carlo simulations, and spectral methods. 2 lectures, 2 activities.
courses.prerequisite: CSC 101 or CSC 1001; and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: CSC 101 or CSC 1001; and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Special Problems for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigations, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Repeatable up to 4 units. Formerly PHYS 400.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Particle and Nuclear Physics
courses.description: Comprehensive exploration of particle and nuclear physics, including the Standard Model, neutrinos, heavy ion collisions, and nuclear structure and reactions. Instructors may choose to emphasize theoretical and/or experimental treatments of contemporary research concepts. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly PHYS 403.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211; and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343.
courses.recommended: CSC 101, CSC 1001, or other programming experience.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211; and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343. Recommended: CSC 101, CSC 1001, or other programming experience.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Research Experience for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigations, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Repeatable up to 4 units. Credit/No Credit grading only. Formerly PHYS 404.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics I
courses.description: The postulates and interpretation of quantum mechanics. Wave functions. The Schroedinger equation and its solutions in one and more dimensions. The hydrogen atom. Discrete problems, including spin. 3 lectures. Formerly PHYS 405.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 305 or PHYS 3305; and PHYS 320 or PHYS 3320.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: PHYS 305 or PHYS 3305; and PHYS 320 or PHYS 3320.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics II
courses.description: Symmetries and conservation laws. Time-independent and time-dependent perturbation theory. Variational principle and WKB approximation. Scattering and the Born approximation. Quantum dynamics. 3 lectures. Formerly PHYS 406.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 405 or PHYS 4405.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: PHYS 405 or PHYS 4405.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electromagnetic Fields and Waves I
courses.description: Electric and magnetic field theory using vector analysis. Electric fields, dielectric materials, magnetic fields, magnetic materials. Induced emf, Maxwell's equations, wave equation, plane electromagnetic waves. 3 lectures. Formerly PHYS 408.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 320 or PHYS 3320.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: PHYS 320 or PHYS 3320.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electromagnetic Fields and Waves II
courses.description: Wave equation, plane electromagnetic waves, guided waves. Dipole radiation, radiation from an accelerated charge. Special relativity. 3 lectures. Formerly PHYS 409.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 408 or PHYS 4408.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: PHYS 408 or PHYS 4408.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics of Solid Earth
courses.description: Methods of body wave seismology applied to determination of interior structure and composition of the Earth. Planetary seismology. The geomagnetic field and its source. Application of earthquake seismology, paleomagnetism, heat flow, and gravity to plate tectonics and geodynamics. 3 lectures. Formerly PHYS 410.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, or PHYS 1143; MATH 241 or MATH 2263; and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, or PHYS 1143; MATH 241 or MATH 2263; and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introduction to Special and General Relativity
courses.description: Introduction to the theory of special and general relativity. Simultaneity, length and time measurements. Space-time diagrams. Lorentz transformations. Four-Vectors and Relativistic mechanics. Gravity as curved spacetime. Solar system tests of relativity. Black holes, gravitational waves, and cosmology. 3 lectures. Formerly PHYS 418.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211; and PHYS 305 or PHYS 3305.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: PHYS 211 or PHYS 2211; and PHYS 305 or PHYS 3305.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Solid State Physics
courses.description: Physics of solids including structural, mechanical, thermal, electronic, and magnetic properties, and additional selected concepts. Introduction to the description of electrons and phonons in crystalline solids, including the properties of metals, semiconductors, and superconductors. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly PHYS 425.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: PHYS 211, PHYS 2211, CHEM 353, or CHEM 3392; and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2343, or MATH 2341.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: One of the following: PHYS 211, PHYS 2211, CHEM 353, or CHEM 3392; and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2343, or MATH 2341.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos
courses.description: Analysis of linear and nonlinear dynamical systems with emphasis on geometrical methods and visualization techniques. Fixed points, phase plane analysis, bifurcations, limit cycles, chaos, and fractals. Laboratory component includes data acquisition and analysis, numerical simulations of dynamical systems, and analysis of discrete systems. Not open to students with credit in MATH 416 or MATH 4342. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly PHYS 428.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, or PHYS 1143; MATH 241 or MATH 2263; and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Prerequisite: PHYS 143, PHYS 143C, or PHYS 1143; MATH 241 or MATH 2263; and one of the following: MATH 242, MATH 244, MATH 2341, or MATH 2343. Recommended: Junior standing.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Senior Project I
courses.description: Selection and completion of a project under faculty supervision. Projects typical of the type of topics graduates may encounter in graduate study or field of employment. Project results culminate in appropriate deliverable. Formerly PHYS 461.
courses.prerequisite: Senior standing and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Senior standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Senior Project II
courses.description: Continuation of project under faculty supervision. Projects typical of the type of topics graduates may encounter in graduate study or field of employment. Project results culminate in appropriate deliverable. Formerly PHYS 462.
courses.prerequisite: PHYS 461 or PHYS 4461; and consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: PHYS 461 or PHYS 4461; and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly PHYS 470.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Special Advanced Laboratory
courses.description: Directed group laboratory study of special topics for advanced students. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 laboratories. Formerly PHYS 471.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Orientation to Plant Sciences
courses.description: Discussion of careers in Plant Sciences, department curriculum, and field, orchard, and greenhouse operations. Introduction to student and professional organizations. Discussion of advising and academic resources. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 lecture. Formerly PLSC 101.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F CR/NC

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: People, Pests, and Plagues
courses.description: Introduction to the science of entomology, including insect identification, biology, ecology, and evolution. Insects as beneficials, disease vectors, and crop pests and their interactions with humans, including roles in human culture and history. Not open for major credit in Plant Sciences or Wine and Viticulture, Viticulture concentration. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Fulfills GE Areas 5B and 5C (GE Areas B2 and B3 for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly PLSC 110.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Principles of Plant Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to applied plant sciences. Basic plant classification, anatomy, growth, and physiology, including effects of environmental conditions, soil and media properties, and biotic and abiotic factors affecting commercial plant production. 2 lectures. Formerly PLSC 120.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Concurrent: PLSC 1120L.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Principles of Plant Sciences Lab
courses.description: Introductory laboratory in applied plant sciences. Basic plant classification, anatomy, growth, and physiology, including effects of environmental conditions, soil and media properties, and biotic and abiotic factors affecting commercial plant production. 1 laboratory.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Concurrent: PLSC 120 or PLSC 1120.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Introduction to Sustainable Site Horticulture
courses.description: Scientific and hands-on introduction to planting, caring for, and managing sustainable horticultural spaces. Plant health care, pruning, soils, irrigation, and stormwater management in the landscape. Equipment operation, safety, and materials. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly PLSC 123.
courses.recommended: BOT 121 and PLSC 120 or BOT 1121 and PLSC 1120.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Sustainability Focused Recommended: BOT 121 and PLSC 120 or BOT 1121 and PLSC 1120.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Plant Propagation
courses.description: Plant propagation principles and practices, including analysis of why and how techniques work. Discussion of current commercial horticulture propagation trends. Hands-on propagation experience. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly PLSC 124.
courses.prerequisite: BOT 121 and PLSC 120 or BOT 1121 and PLSC 1120.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: BOT 121 and PLSC 120 or BOT 1121 and PLSC 1120.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Introduction to Fruit Crop Production
courses.description: Orchard design and development, cultural practices and physiological responses of perennial fruit crops. Practices, propagation, harvest and postharvest practices and strategies to maximize sustainability of California fruit crops. 3 lectures, 1 activity. Formerly PLSC 132.
courses.prerequisite: PLSC 1120L.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Prerequisite: PLSC 1120L.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: California Row Crop Production
courses.description: Botany, growth characteristics, pests, and harvesting methods for the most important row crops grown in California. Production practices from tillage to harvest for important forages, grains, and vegetable crops. Current issues in agriculture important to the row crop industry. Field trip required. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly PLSC 190.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Corequisite: PLSC 120 or PLSC 1120.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Beekeeping
courses.description: Introduction to honeybee biology and apiculture. Exploration of the life cycle of honeybees, biogeography, and evolution of beekeeping. Equipment, techniques, management practices, pollination ecology, economic practices, and current issues within beekeeping. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly PLSC 175.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Special Problems for Undergraduates
courses.description: Individual investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Report required. Repeatable up to 3 units. Formerly PLSC 200.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP, SU Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Orchard and Vegetable Enterprise Project
courses.description: Hands-on experience in the production, management, marketing, and sales of fruit and vegetable crops. Activities required to successfully grow, harvest, and market orchard and vegetable crops. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 lecture, 1 activity. Formerly PLSC 205.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Environmental Horticulture Enterprise Project
courses.description: Hands-on experience in all aspects of ornamental horticulture production. Planning, controlled environment growing and selling. Field trip required. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 lecture, 1 activity. Formerly PLSC 212.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP CR/NC Recommended: PLSC 120 or PLSC 1120.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Floral Design
courses.description: Fundamentals of theory, techniques, and skills currently practiced in the floral industry. Appropriate utilization of current sales and business practices in a florist setting. Beginning and advanced techniques and skills for construction of floral designs. 1 lecture, 2 laboratories. Formerly PLSC 225.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Basic Viticulture
courses.description: Fundamentals of grape growing, with emphasis on wine grapes. Fundamentals of vine anatomy and physiology, development and phenology, trellising systems, soils, climatic factors, vineyard establishment, grafting, irrigation, fertility, harvest practices, pruning, major pests, and major varieties and rootstocks. Course may be offered in classroom-based or online format. 3 lectures. Crosslisted as PLSC 2232/WVIT 2233. Formerly PLSC 232/WVIT 232.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: PLSC 120, PLSC 1120, BOT 121 or BOT 1121; one of the following: CHEM 124, CHEM 1120, CHEM 127, or CHEM 1122; and SS 120 or SS 1120.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: PLSC 120, PLSC 1120, BOT 121 or BOT 1121; one of the following: CHEM 124, CHEM 1120, CHEM 127, or CHEM 1122; and SS 120 or SS 1120.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Introduction to Plant Materials
courses.description: Systematic introduction to herbaceous and woody landscape plants. Responsible plant selection and management, including plant identification, cultural requirements, and landscape uses. Featuring common California native and non-native plants. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly PLSC 233.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F Recommended: BOT 121 or BOT 1121.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Precision Farming
courses.description: Introduction to precision agriculture technologies. Review of the development and utilization of GIS, GPS, remote sensing, and variable rate technology for site-specific management. Economic and environmental benefits of site-specific versus whole field management. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly BRAE/PLSC 244.
courses.corequisite: PLSC 132 or PLSC 1132; and PLSC 190 or PLSC 1150.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Corequisite: PLSC 132 or PLSC 1132; and PLSC 190 or PLSC 1150.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Directed group study of special topics. The Class Schedule will list topic selected. Repeatable up to 6 units. 1 to 3 lectures. Formerly PLSC 270.
courses.prerequisite: Consent of instructor.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: TBD Prerequisite: Consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Greenhouse Vegetable Enterprise Project
courses.description: Production, management, and sales of a variety of hydroponically-grown greenhouse vegetables. Credit/No Credit grading only. 1 lecture, 1 activity. Replaced PLSC 334.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP CR/NC Recommended: PLSC 333 or PLSC 3333.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Horticultural Production Techniques
courses.description: Principles of plant growth in the production horticulture industry, with an emphasis on sustainability. Substrates, nutrient management, irrigation, plant growth regulators, containers, and cultural techniques. Current technology and innovations. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Replaced PLSC 245.
courses.prerequisite: PLSC 120 or PLSC 1120.
courses.geArea: Sustainability Focused
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: SP Sustainability Focused Prerequisite: PLSC 120 or PLSC 1120.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Introduction to Plant Breeding
courses.description: Principles of qualitative and quantitative genetics useful in the development of new plant varieties. Procedures for the creation of genetic variability, testing procedures, and selection schemes for development of improved plant types. 3 lectures. Formerly PLSC 304.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BOT 121, BOT 1121, PLSC 120, or PLSC 1120; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: BOT 121, BOT 1121, PLSC 120, or PLSC 1120; and STAT 218 or STAT 1110.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Agricultural Entomology
courses.description: Science of entomology relating to agriculturally important insects. Biology, ecology, and identification of insects and mites and their management in horticulture, field crops, and landscapes. Integration of sustainable pest control practices. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly PLSC 313.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BOT 121, BOT 1121, PLSC 120, or PLSC 1120.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: BOT 121, BOT 1121, PLSC 120, or PLSC 1120.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Principles of Organic Crop Production
courses.description: Origins, application, regulation, and technology of organic crop production. Theoretical and practical issues surrounding organic crop production from a cross-disciplinary perspective. History of the organic movement, current regulation and certification, and field management practices and technologies. Features industry guest lecturers. Field trip required. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Crosslisted as AG/PLSC 3315. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly AG/PLSC 315.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and completion of GE Area 5 (GE Areas B1 to B3 for the 2020-26 catalogs).

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Weed Biology and Management
courses.description: Weed ecology, biology, physiology, and implications for management. Identification of weeds and invasive plant species in agricultural and managed ecosystems. Organic, cultural, biological, physical/mechanical, and chemical methods and their integrated pest management (IPM) uses. 3 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly AEPS 321.
courses.prerequisite: One of the following: BOT 121, BOT 1121, PLSC 120, or PLSC 1120.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: One of the following: BOT 121, BOT 1121, PLSC 120, or PLSC 1120.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Plant Pathology
courses.description: Comprehensive study of plant pathology. Plant disease impact on California's agriculturally important crops. Plant disease diagnosis, integrated and sustainable practices for disease management. 2 lectures, 1 laboratory. Formerly BOT/PLSC 323.
courses.prerequisite: BOT 121 or BOT 1121.
courses.catalogDetails: Term Typically Offered: F, SP Prerequisite: BOT 121 or BOT 1121.

courses.subject: PLSC
courses.title: Plants, Biotechnology, and the Media
courses.description: Agriculture as applied biology and its impact on civilization. Application of technology to increase the efficiency of food production. Genetics and biotechnology; culminating in an assessment of genetically engineered foods, the myths, the controversy, and the science. 2 lectures, 1 activity. Fulfills GE Areas Upper-Division 2 or Upper-Division 5 (GE Area Upper-Division B for students on the 2020-26 catalogs). Formerly PLSC 329.
courses.prerequisite: Junior standing; completion of GE Area 1 with grades of C- or better (GE Area A for the 2020-26 catalogs); completion of GE Area 2 with a grade of C- or better (GE Area B4 for the 2020-26 catalogs); and one of the following: BIO 111, BIO 114, BIO 161, BIO 1111, BIO 1114, BIO 1151, BOT 121, BOT 1121, PLSC 120, or PLSC 1120.
